hook.en: Hong Kong, 1963. After a long drought the government rationed tap water. From 1 June, homes had water for only 4 hours every four days, and people queued at street standpipes to collect water.
hook.zh: 1963 年香港大旱，政府制水。由 6 月 1 日起，住戶每四日先有 4 個鐘水，市民要喺街喉排隊輪水。

stops.src: Industrial History of Hong Kong, “The 1963 Water Drought”

q.en: Hong Kong still had some water in 1963. So was water scarce?
q.zh: 1963 年香港仲有啲水。咁水算唔算 scarce？

o.en: Yes. The water was not enough to satisfy everyone’s wants.
o.zh: 算，啲水唔夠滿足所有人嘅 wants。

o.en: No. There was still some water.

w.en: Scarcity does not mean “none left”. It compares resources with wants.
w.zh: Scarcity 唔係「冇晒」，係將資源同 wants 比較。

d.en: Scarcity: the resources available are not enough to satisfy all human wants.
d.zh: Scarcity：可用嘅資源唔夠滿足人類所有 wants。

p.en: Wants are unlimited: when one want is satisfied, new ones appear.
p.zh: Wants 係無限嘅：滿足咗一個，又會有新嘅。

p.en: Resources (land, labour, capital, time) are limited.
p.zh: 資源（土地、勞力、資本、時間）係有限嘅。

p.en: Scarcity is relative. “Limited” alone is not scarcity: always compare with wants.
p.zh: Scarcity 係相對嘅。淨係「有限」唔等於 scarcity，一定要同 wants 比較。

s.en: Resources: the water left in Hong Kong’s reservoirs.
s.zh: 資源：水塘剩低嘅水。

s.en: Wants: drinking, cooking, washing, factories.
s.zh: Wants：飲、煮飯、洗衫沖涼、工廠用水。

s.en: Compare: the water could not satisfy all these wants, so water was scarce.
s.zh: 比較：啲水滿足唔到晒呢啲 wants，所以水係 scarce。

s.en: Result: people had to choose how to use the water, and compete for it at the standpipes.
s.zh: 結果：大家要揀點用水，仲要喺街喉爭水。

q.en: Which statement is correct?
q.zh: 以下邊句啱？

o.en: Scarcity exists when resources are not enough to satisfy all wants.
o.zh: 資源唔夠滿足所有 wants，就有 scarcity。

o.en: Wants are limited but resources are unlimited.
A resource is scarce whenever its quantity is limited.
o.zh: 資源只要數量有限，就一定 scarce。

w.en: Scarcity compares resources with wants. Even a rich person’s time is limited.
w.zh: Scarcity 係資源同 wants 嘅比較。有錢人嘅時間都係有限。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why was water scarce in Hong Kong in 1963?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解 1963 年香港嘅水係 scarce？

o.en: Because people had to queue for water.
Queuing is a result of scarcity (competition), not the reason.
o.zh: 排隊係 scarcity 嘅結果（競爭），唔係原因。

o.en: Because the water available was not enough to satisfy all people’s wants for water.
o.zh: 因為可用嘅水唔夠滿足所有人對水嘅 wants。

o.en: Resources compared with wants: that is the definition.
o.zh: 資源同 wants 比較，正正係定義。

o.en: Because the amount of water was small.
“Small” alone is not enough. Compare with wants.
o.zh: 淨係「少」唔夠，要同 wants 比較。

hook.en: Tai O, 1955 to the mid-1960s. Competition from imported salt grew, and salt-pan owners one by one stopped making salt. Each owner had to ask: what is the best use of my land and my time?
hook.zh: 1955 年至 1960 年代中，大澳鹽田面對進口鹽嘅競爭，鹽田主陸續停止曬鹽。每個鹽田主都要諗：我塊地、我啲時間，最好用嚟做咩？

stops.src: Industrial History of Hong Kong, Tai O salt production

q.en: (Fictional figures) Ah Ying, a Tai O S4 student in 2026, has one Sunday afternoon. Her ranking: ① revise for Monday’s test ② help at her family’s shrimp-paste stall (paid $200) ③ play football. She revises. What is her opportunity cost?
q.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年，大澳中四學生阿瑩有一個星期日下晝。佢嘅排序：① 溫書準備星期一測驗 ② 喺屋企嘅蝦醬檔幫手（有 $200）③ 踢波。佢揀咗溫書。佢嘅 opportunity cost 係乜？

o.en: Helping at the stall and playing football

w.en: Only the highest-valued option she gives up counts: the stall. Not everything added up, and not zero just because she pays no money.
w.zh: 只計佢放棄嘅最高價值選項：蝦醬檔。唔係全部加埋，亦唔會因為唔使俾錢就係零。

d.en: Opportunity cost: the value of the highest-valued option forgone when a choice is made.
d.zh: Opportunity cost：作出選擇時，被放棄嘅最高價值選項嘅價值。

p.en: Scarcity means we must choose, and every choice gives something up.
p.zh: 有 scarcity 就要揀，每個選擇都要放棄啲嘢。

p.en: Count one option only: the best one given up. Never add the options together.
p.zh: 只計一個選項：被放棄嘅最好嗰個。唔好將選項加埋。

p.en: It need not be money. Money is only a unit for measuring it.
p.zh: 唔一定係錢。錢只係計算嘅單位。

p.en: No alternative means no choice, and no choice means no cost.
p.zh: 冇其他選項就冇選擇，冇選擇就冇成本。

s.en: Write the ranking: ① revise ② stall ③ football.
s.zh: 寫低排序：① 溫書 ② 蝦醬檔 ③ 踢波。

s.en: Circle the choice: ① revise.
s.zh: 圈出揀咗嘅：① 溫書。

s.en: The highest-valued option forgone (HVOF) is the next one down: ② the stall.
s.zh: 被放棄嘅最高價值選項（HVOF）就係下一個：② 蝦醬檔。

s.en: Opportunity cost of revising = helping at the stall, worth $200 to her.
s.zh: 溫書嘅 opportunity cost = 喺蝦醬檔幫手，對佢值 $200。

q.en: A Tai O fisherman in the 1960s can spend Sunday on only one of: ① fishing ② mending his nets ③ resting. He goes fishing. What is his opportunity cost?
q.zh: 1960 年代，一個大澳漁民星期日只可以做一樣：① 出海捕魚 ② 補網 ③ 休息。佢出海捕魚。佢嘅 opportunity cost 係乜？

w.en: Only the next-best option, ②. The fish is the benefit of his choice, not its cost.
w.zh: 只計次佳選項 ②。魚係佢選擇嘅得益，唔係成本。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of opportunity cost.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 opportunity cost 解釋。

o.en: Everything you give up when you choose.
o.zh: 你作出選擇時放棄嘅所有嘢。

o.en: Only the highest-valued option counts, not the sum.
o.zh: 只計最高價值嗰個，唔係總和。

o.en: The money you pay for your choice.
Money is a unit. The cost is the option forgone.
o.zh: 錢只係單位，成本係被放棄嘅選項。

o.en: The best option you give up when you choose.
o.zh: 你作出選擇時放棄嘅最好選項。
一個選項，最高價值嗰個。

t.en: Will the cost change? EE + HVOF

hook.en: Same Sunday, same ranking, but things around Ah Ying keep changing. DSE often asks: will her opportunity cost change?
hook.zh: 同一個星期日、同一個排序，但阿瑩身邊啲嘢不斷變。DSE 成日問：佢嘅 opportunity cost 會唔會變？

q.en: (Fictional figures) Tourists crowd into Tai O on a public holiday, so the stall now pays her $300 instead of $200. Does her opportunity cost of revising change?
q.zh: （虛構數字）公眾假期大澳好多遊客，蝦醬檔幫手由 $200 加到 $300。佢溫書嘅 opportunity cost 會唔會變？

w.en: The option she gives up (the HVOF) became more valuable, so the cost rose.
w.zh: 佢放棄嘅選項（HVOF）價值上升，所以成本上升。

d.en: Opportunity cost changes only if (1) the highest-valued option forgone (HVOF) changes, or (2) the value of the HVOF changes.
d.zh: Opportunity cost 只會喺兩種情況下改變：(1) HVOF 換咗；或者 (2) HVOF 嘅價值變咗。

p.en: EE = Effect of the Event: which option’s value moved?
p.zh: EE（Effect of the Event）：件事令邊個選項嘅價值變？

p.en: The chosen option’s value changes → the cost is unchanged.
p.zh: 被揀選項嘅價值變 → 成本唔變。

p.en: A lower option rises → it may overtake the HVOF → the cost will “not necessarily” stay unchanged.
p.zh: 排低啲嘅選項升值 → 可能爬頭變 HVOF → 成本「唔一定」唔變。

t.en: Four events, one ranking: ① revise ② stall ③ football
t.zh: 四件事，同一個排序：① 溫書 ② 蝦醬檔 ③ 踢波

s.en: Stall pays $300 (② the HVOF ↑) → cost rises.
s.zh: 蝦醬檔加到 $300（② HVOF ↑）→ 成本上升。

s.en: Monday’s test now counts more (① the chosen option ↑) → cost unchanged.
s.zh: 星期一測驗佔分多咗（① 被揀選項 ↑）→ 成本唔變。

s.en: Rain makes football less fun (③ ↓, not the HVOF) → cost unchanged.
s.zh: 落雨，踢波冇咁好玩（③ ↓，唔係 HVOF）→ 成本唔變。

s.en: Friends organise a final match (③ ↑) → ③ may overtake ② → cost may change.
s.zh: 朋友搞決賽（③ ↑）→ ③ 可能超越 ② → 成本可能變。

q.en: Her friends organise a final match, so football (③) becomes more valuable to her. Will her opportunity cost of revising necessarily remain unchanged?
q.zh: 朋友搞決賽，踢波（③）對佢嚟講價值上升。佢溫書嘅 opportunity cost 係咪一定唔變？

o.en: Yes, because ③ is not the HVOF.
o.zh: 係，因為 ③ 唔係 HVOF。

o.en: No, because any change always changes the cost.
o.zh: 唔係，因為任何改變都一定令成本變。

o.en: No. ③ may overtake ② and become the HVOF.
o.zh: 唔一定。③ 可能超越 ②，變成 HVOF。

o.en: Yes, because her chosen option did not change.

w.en: “Necessarily” is the trap. The order may rearrange, so the cost may change. “Any change always changes it” goes too far.
w.zh: 「一定」係陷阱。排序可能重排，所以成本可能變。「任何改變都一定令成本變」就講過龍。

q.en: Pick the best way to answer “Will the opportunity cost change?”
q.zh: 揀最好嘅方法答「Opportunity cost 會唔會變？」

o.en: Any change in the story changes the cost.
o.zh: 故事有任何改變，成本都會變。

o.en: Only changes to the HVOF matter.
o.zh: 只有 HVOF 嘅改變先有影響。

o.en: Find which option the event affects, then check whether the HVOF or its value changes.
o.zh: 搵出件事影響邊個選項，再睇 HVOF 或者佢嘅價值有冇變。

o.en: Check whether the chosen option became better.
Changes in the chosen option never change the cost.
o.zh: 被揀選項變，成本唔會變。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Ah Ying’s Saturday tutorial class in Tung Chung costs $300 and takes 3 hours including the bus ride from Tai O. Is the cost just $300?
hook.zh: （虛構數字）阿瑩星期六去東涌上補習班，學費 $300，連由大澳坐巴士來回共 3 個鐘。成本係咪淨係 $300？

q.en: If the class were free, would going to it cost her nothing?
q.zh: 如果補習班免費，去上堂係咪就冇成本？

o.en: No. She still gives up the best use of her 3 hours.
o.zh: 唔係。佢仍然放棄咗嗰 3 個鐘嘅最佳用途。

w.en: Time has other uses, so time is a cost too.
w.zh: 時間有其他用途，所以時間都係成本。

d.en: Full cost = money cost + time cost (a non-money cost).
d.zh: Full cost = money cost（金錢成本）+ time cost（時間成本，非金錢成本）。

p.en: Money cost: the money spent on the choice.
p.zh: Money cost：為呢個選擇使嘅錢。

p.en: Time cost: the value of the best alternative use of the time. One option only, never the sum.
p.zh: Time cost：嗰段時間最佳其他用途嘅價值。只計一個，唔好加埋。

p.en: Time cost differs between people: the same hour costs more for someone with a better alternative.
p.zh: Time cost 因人而異：同一個鐘，有更好選擇嘅人成本更高。

t.zh: 阿瑩嘅補習班（虛構數字）

s.en: Money cost: the $300 fee.
s.zh: Money cost：$300 學費。

s.en: Other uses of the 3 hours: the stall at $60 an hour, or tutoring her cousin at $50 an hour.
s.zh: 嗰 3 個鐘嘅其他用途：蝦醬檔每個鐘 $60，或者幫表妹補習每個鐘 $50。

s.en: Time cost = the best one only = 3 × $60 = $180.
s.zh: Time cost = 只計最好嗰個 = 3 × $60 = $180。

q.en: (Fictional figures) Two Tai O residents queue 1 hour for the same free event. One could earn $80 in that hour, the other $40. Which is correct?
q.zh: （虛構數字）兩個大澳居民為同一個免費活動排隊 1 個鐘。一個嗰個鐘可以賺 $80，另一個可以賺 $40。以下邊句啱？

o.en: The first person’s full cost is higher, because their time cost is higher.
o.zh: 第一個人嘅 full cost 較高，因為佢嘅 time cost 較高。
兩人嘅 full cost 都係零。

o.en: Their full costs are the same, because the event is free.
o.zh: 兩人嘅 full cost 一樣，因為活動免費。
每人嘅 full cost 都係 $120。

w.en: Same queue, different best use of time, so different time costs. $120 wrongly adds two people’s figures.
w.zh: 同一條隊，時間嘅最佳用途唔同，所以 time cost 唔同。$120 係錯將兩個人嘅數加埋。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why can the same queue cost two people differently?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解同一條隊，兩個人嘅成本可以唔同？

o.en: Because each person’s best alternative use of the time is different.
o.zh: 因為每個人嗰段時間嘅最佳其他用途唔同。

o.en: Time cost depends on the best alternative.
o.zh: Time cost 取決於最佳其他選擇。

o.en: Because some people dislike queuing more.
o.zh: 因為有啲人更加憎排隊。

o.en: Time cost is about the best alternative use of the time.
o.zh: Time cost 講嘅係時間嘅最佳其他用途。

o.en: Because one of them pays more money.
o.zh: 因為其中一個俾多啲錢。

o.en: The event is free: nobody pays money here.

t.zh: 沉沒成本：已經使咗嘅錢

hook.en: By the late 1950s, as competition from imported salt grew, the money once spent building Tai O’s salt pans could not be recovered, whatever the owners decided next.
hook.zh: 到 1950 年代後期，進口鹽競爭越嚟越大。當年起鹽田使咗嘅錢，無論鹽田主之後點揀，都拎唔返。

stops.src: Industrial History of Hong Kong, Tai O salt production

q.en: When deciding whether to keep making salt, should an owner count the money spent building the pans years ago?
q.zh: 決定繼唔繼續曬鹽嗰陣，鹽田主應唔應該計埋好多年前起鹽田使咗嘅錢？

o.en: Yes, because it was a big cost.
No, because it cannot be recovered whatever he chooses.
o.zh: 唔應該，因為無論點揀都拎唔返。

w.en: Money already gone is the same under every choice, so it is not given up by any choice now.
w.zh: 已經使咗嘅錢，揀邊樣都一樣，所以而家冇任何選擇放棄咗佢。

d.en: Historical cost is not a cost: money already spent that cannot be recovered does not affect the cost of any choice now.
d.zh: Historical cost is not a cost：已經使咗又拎唔返嘅錢，唔影響而家任何選擇嘅成本。

p.en: Only count options still available at the moment of choice.
p.zh: 只計作決定嗰一刻仲有嘅選項。

p.en: If part can be recovered (for example a resale value), that part is still a cost of keeping the thing.
p.zh: 如果有部分拎得返（例如轉售價值），嗰部分仍然係保留佢嘅成本。

p.en: No choice, no cost.
p.zh: 冇選擇就冇成本。

t.en: A salt-pan owner in the late 1950s

s.en: Past: building the pans. Spent and cannot be recovered, so ignore it.
s.zh: 過去：起鹽田。已經使咗、拎唔返，唔計。

s.en: Now: keep making salt, or use the land and his time another way.
s.zh: 而家：繼續曬鹽，定係將塊地同時間用喺其他地方。

s.en: Cost of continuing = the best of those other uses now.
s.zh: 繼續曬鹽嘅成本 = 而家其他用途之中最好嗰個。

q.en: (Fictional figures) Ah Ying paid a non-refundable $100 deposit for a kayak trip at Tai O. On the day it rains and she would rather study. Which should NOT affect her decision?
q.zh: （虛構數字）阿瑩俾咗 $100 唔退嘅訂金參加大澳獨木舟活動。當日落雨，佢寧願溫書。以下邊樣唔應該影響佢嘅決定？

o.en: Whether the trip is still safe
How much she wants to study

w.en: The deposit is gone whether she goes or not. The others are about the options still open.
w.zh: 無論去唔去，訂金都拎唔返。其他幾樣都關乎仲有嘅選項。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does the $100 deposit not matter?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解 $100 訂金唔重要？

o.en: It is gone whether she goes or not, so neither choice gives it up.
o.zh: 去唔去都冇咗，所以兩個選擇都冇放棄佢。

o.en: That is why sunk cost is ignored.
o.zh: 所以 sunk cost 唔計。

o.en: Size does not matter: even a huge sunk cost is ignored.
o.zh: 金額大細冇關係，幾大嘅 sunk cost 都唔計。

hook.en: At Tai O’s salt pans, sea water was let in through sluices and dried in the sun. Sea water at the shore was plentiful; making salt took land, labour and time.
hook.zh: 大澳鹽田用水閘引海水入田，再靠太陽曬乾。岸邊嘅海水好多；但係曬鹽要用土地、人手同時間。

stops.src: Industrial History of Hong Kong, Tai O salt production

q.en: The free newspapers handed out at MTR exits in the 2010s were free goods. True or false?
q.zh: 2010 年代港鐵站出口派嘅免費報紙係 free good。啱定錯？

o.en: False. Free of charge is not the same as a free good.
o.zh: 錯。免費派唔等於 free good。

w.en: Paper, ink and labour had other uses, so the newspaper had an opportunity cost. It was an economic good given out free of charge.
w.zh: 紙、墨同人手都有其他用途，所以報紙有 opportunity cost。佢係免費派嘅 economic good。

d.en: Free good: enough to satisfy all wants, so no opportunity cost. Economic good: not enough to satisfy all wants, so it has an opportunity cost and people compete for it.
d.zh: Free good（免費物品）：數量夠滿足所有 wants，冇 opportunity cost。Economic good（經濟物品）：數量唔夠滿足所有 wants，有 opportunity cost，大家會爭。

p.en: Ask one question: is the quantity enough for everyone’s wants?
p.zh: 只問一條問題：數量夠唔夠滿足所有人嘅 wants？

p.en: Free of charge ≠ free good.
p.zh: 免費派 ≠ free good。

p.en: It depends on the situation: air on land is a free good; air in a diver’s tank is not.
p.zh: 視乎情況：陸地上嘅空氣係 free good；潛水員氧氣樽入面嘅空氣就唔係。

t.en: Two goods at the same salt pan

s.en: Sea water at the shore: enough for everyone who wanted it, so a free good.
s.zh: 岸邊嘅海水：夠晒所有想要嘅人用，所以係 free good。

s.en: Salt: needed land, labour and time that had other uses, so an economic good.
s.zh: 鹽：要用有其他用途嘅土地、人手同時間，所以係 economic good。

s.en: That is why Saltling lives on the salt pan: one place, both kinds of goods.
s.zh: 所以鹽精住喺鹽田：同一個地方，兩種物品都有。

q.en: Which statement is correct?
q.zh: 以下邊句啱？

o.en: People prefer economic goods to free goods.
o.zh: 大家鍾意 economic good 多過 free good。

o.en: Economic goods may not be scarce.
People compete for both free and economic goods.
o.zh: Free good 同 economic good 大家都會爭。

w.en: Not enough for everyone, so people compete. Nobody competes for something that is enough for all.
w.zh: 唔夠所有人用，所以要爭。夠晒人用嘅嘢就冇人會爭。

q.en: Pick the best test for an economic good.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 economic good 判斷方法。

o.en: You have to pay for it.
Price is not the test. A free newspaper has no price but is an economic good.
o.zh: 價錢唔係判斷方法。免費報紙冇價錢，但係 economic good。

o.en: The quantity is not enough to satisfy all wants.
o.zh: 數量唔夠滿足所有 wants。

hook.en: Hong Kong today: a bank pays you interest if you keep money in a time deposit, and charges you interest if you borrow.
hook.zh: 今日香港：你將錢放喺銀行定期存款，銀行會俾利息你；你借錢，就要俾利息銀行。

q.en: If there were no money at all, would interest still exist?
q.zh: 如果世界冇錢，利息仲會唔會存在？

o.en: No, because interest is about money.
Yes, because people would still pay extra to get goods earlier.
o.zh: 會，因為大家仍然願意俾多啲去早啲得到物品。

w.en: Interest is the price of getting resources earlier. It can be paid in goods.
w.zh: 利息係提早得到資源嘅價錢，可以用物品支付。

d.en: Interest is the cost of earlier availability of resources.
d.zh: Interest 係提早得到資源嘅成本。

p.en: Borrower: interest is the cost of getting resources earlier.
p.zh: 借方：利息係提早得到資源嘅成本。

p.en: Lender: interest is the reward for waiting (deferring consumption).
p.zh: 貸方：利息係延遲消費嘅補償。

p.en: It can be paid in goods, not only money: lend rice, get more rice back.
p.zh: 可以用物品支付，唔一定用錢：借米出去，收返多啲米。

p.en: Interest rate ↑ → consuming now costs more → present consumption ↓, saving ↑.
p.zh: 利率 ↑ → 而家消費嘅成本 ↑ → 現時消費 ↓，儲蓄 ↑。

s.en: Borrower: uses the resources now, pays back more later. The extra pays for earlier availability.
s.zh: 借方：而家用資源，之後還多啲。多出嚟嗰部分就係提早得到資源嘅代價。

s.en: Lender: gives up using the resources now, and is paid for waiting.
s.zh: 貸方：放棄而家用資源，等嘅代價由利息補償。

s.en: Interest rate rises: spending now costs more, so people save more and consume less now.
s.zh: 利率上升：而家使錢嘅成本高咗，所以多啲儲蓄、少啲現時消費。

q.en: When the interest rate rises, which is most likely?
q.zh: 利率上升，最可能出現以下邊個情況？

o.en: People consume less now and save more.
o.zh: 大家而家少咗消費，多咗儲蓄。

w.en: A higher rate raises the cost of consuming now and the reward for waiting.
w.zh: 利率高咗，而家消費嘅成本同等待嘅回報都上升。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of interest.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅利息解釋。

o.en: It exists even without money or banks.
It is the price of getting resources earlier.
o.zh: 佢係提早得到資源嘅價錢。

o.en: Interest exists even with no inflation.

chain.zh: 無限 wants + 有限資源

chain.en: Full cost = money + time; sunk cost not counted
chain.zh: Full cost = 錢 + 時間；sunk cost 唔計

q.en: (Fictional figures) The stall now pays only $50, and football is now worth more to Ah Ying than the stall. Her opportunity cost of revising is now…
q.zh: （虛構數字）蝦醬檔而家只俾 $50，踢波對阿瑩嚟講價值高過蝦醬檔。佢溫書嘅 opportunity cost 而家係…

w.en: The order rearranged, so football is the new HVOF.
w.zh: 排序重排咗，踢波變成新嘅 HVOF。

q.en: Which is a free good?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係 free good？

o.en: Salt from the Tai O salt pans
Sea water at the Tai O shore
A free newspaper at an MTR exit
o.zh: 港鐵站出口嘅免費報紙

w.en: Only the sea water was enough for all wants.
w.zh: 只有海水夠滿足所有 wants。

q.en: When making a decision now, which is NOT a cost?
q.zh: 而家作決定，以下邊樣唔係成本？

o.en: A resale value you give up by keeping something
o.zh: 保留一樣嘢而放棄嘅轉售價值

o.en: Money already spent that cannot be recovered
o.zh: 已經使咗又拎唔返嘅錢

o.en: The best alternative use of your time
o.zh: 你時間嘅最佳其他用途

w.en: Sunk cost is not a cost.
w.zh: Sunk cost 唔係成本。

q.en: In your own words: why does every choice have a cost? (1–2 sentences)
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解每個選擇都有成本？（1–2 句）

ck.en: I said resources are not enough for all wants (scarcity).
ck.zh: 我有講資源唔夠滿足所有 wants（scarcity）。

ck.en: I said we must choose.
ck.zh: 我有講要作出選擇。

ck.en: I said the cost is the highest-valued option given up.
ck.zh: 我有講成本係被放棄嘅最高價值選項。

hook.en: (Fictional family) In 2026 Ah Ying’s family runs a shrimp-paste stall in Tai O. Every month they decide how much paste to make, whether to sun-dry it by hand or buy a drying machine, and who gets the jars.
hook.zh: （虛構家庭）2026 年，阿瑩屋企喺大澳開蝦醬檔。每個月都要決定：整幾多蝦醬、用人手曬定買部烘乾機，同埋啲蝦醬俾邊個。

q.en: The family sells each jar to whoever pays the stall price. Which basic economic problem does this answer?
q.zh: 佢哋將每樽蝦醬賣俾肯俾檔口價錢嘅人。呢個答緊邊個基本經濟問題？

o.zh: How to produce 點樣生產
For whom to produce 為誰生產

w.en: “For whom” asks which rule decides who gets the output. Here the rule is price.
w.zh: 「為誰生產」問嘅係用咩準則決定邊個得到產品。呢度嘅準則係價格。

d.en: Every society must decide what to produce (which goods, how much), how to produce (which method) and for whom to produce (by what rule the output is shared).
d.zh: 每個社會都要決定：what to produce（生產咩、幾多）、how to produce（用咩方法）、for whom to produce（用咩準則分配產品）。

p.en: The problems exist because of scarcity: resources cannot produce everything for everyone.
p.zh: 呢三個問題源於 scarcity：資源唔可以為所有人生產所有嘢。

p.en: Rich or poor, every society faces all three.
p.zh: 無論貧富，每個社會都要面對呢三個問題。

t.zh: 阿瑩屋企嘅蝦醬檔（虛構數字）

s.en: What: shrimp paste, 200 jars this month.
s.zh: What：蝦醬，今個月 200 樽。

s.en: How: sun-dry on the yard by hand instead of using a machine.
s.zh: How：喺曬場用人手曬，唔用機器。

s.en: For whom: whoever pays $50 a jar.
s.zh: For whom：肯俾 $50 一樽嘅人。

q.en: Ah Ying’s uncle replaces hand-stirring with an electric mixer at the shrimp-paste yard. Which problem is he answering?
q.zh: 阿瑩舅父喺蝦醬曬場用電動攪拌機代替人手攪。佢答緊邊個問題？

w.en: Choosing between hand labour and machines is a choice of production method.
w.zh: 揀人手定機器，係揀生產方法。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why must every society answer the three basic economic problems?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解每個社會都要答三個基本經濟問題？

o.en: Because resources are scarce, so it must choose what, how and for whom.
o.zh: 因為資源 scarce，所以要揀生產咩、點生產、為誰生產。
Scarcity 迫使社會作出選擇。

o.en: Because only poor societies lack resources.
o.zh: 因為只有窮嘅社會先缺乏資源。

o.en: Because every society has a government that likes planning.
o.zh: 因為每個社會都有鍾意計劃嘅政府。

o.en: A market economy faces the same problems without central planning.
o.zh: 市場經濟冇中央計劃都一樣要面對。

hook.en: In the 1960s, Hong Kong mostly let markets and prices answer the three questions, while mainland China used a planned economy run by government commands.
hook.zh: 1960 年代，香港主要靠市場同價格解答三個基本問題；中國內地就實行計劃經濟，靠政府指令。

q.en: In a market economy, what mainly decides what gets produced?
q.zh: 市場經濟入面，主要靠乜決定生產咩？

w.en: Prices signal what buyers want and guide private owners’ decisions.
w.zh: 價格反映買家想要乜，引導私人業主作決定。

d.en: Traditional economy: mainly customs and traditions. Planned (command) economy: mainly government commands; resources mainly owned by the state. Market economy: mainly the market mechanism (price system); resources mainly privately owned.
d.zh: Traditional economy：主要靠習俗同傳統。Planned（command）economy：主要靠政府指令，資源主要由 the state 擁有。Market economy：主要靠 market mechanism（price system），資源主要由私人擁有。

p.en: Real economies mix the methods. We classify by the main method used.
p.zh: 現實經濟體系都係混合，按「主要」用咩方法分類。

p.en: In a market economy the market price is the signal for allocating resources.
p.zh: 市場經濟入面，market price 係分配資源嘅訊號。

t.en: One question, three answers: who decides what to produce?
t.zh: 同一條問題，三個答案：邊個決定生產咩？

s.en: Do what your parents did → traditional economy.
s.zh: 跟上一代做法 → traditional economy。

s.en: The state owns most resources and orders the output → planned economy.
s.zh: 政府擁有大部分資源，下令生產 → planned economy。

s.en: Private owners produce what buyers will pay for → market economy.
s.zh: 私人業主生產買家肯俾錢嘅嘢 → market economy。

q.en: Which statement about a planned economy is correct?
q.zh: 以下關於 planned economy 嘅描述，邊句啱？

o.en: There is no scarcity in a planned economy.
Resources are mainly owned by the state and decisions are mainly made by the government.
o.zh: 資源主要由政府擁有，決策主要由政府做。

o.en: Market prices are the main signal for allocating resources.
o.zh: Market price 係分配資源嘅主要訊號。

o.en: Customs mainly decide what to produce.
o.zh: 主要由習俗決定生產咩。

w.en: Command and state ownership define a planned economy. Scarcity exists in every system.
w.zh: 政府指令同國家擁有資源係計劃經濟嘅特徵。每個體系都有 scarcity。

q.en: Pick the best way to classify an economic system.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅經濟體系分類方法。

o.en: Money is not the test; planned economies use money too.
o.zh: 用唔用錢唔係準則，計劃經濟都用錢。

o.en: By the main method it uses to solve the three basic economic problems.
o.zh: 睇佢主要用咩方法解決三個基本經濟問題。

o.en: By whether it has a government.

o.zh: 每個經濟體系都有政府。

hook.en: (Fictional family) Ah Ying’s family owns their shrimp-paste stall in Tai O. They decide how to use it, they keep what it earns, and they could sell it.
hook.zh: （虛構家庭）阿瑩屋企擁有大澳嗰個蝦醬檔。佢哋決定點用、賺到嘅錢歸佢哋，亦可以將檔口賣出。

q.en: The family rents the stall to a souvenir seller for a month and keeps the rent. Which right are they using?
q.zh: 佢哋將檔口租俾紀念品商販一個月，收租歸自己。佢哋用緊邊種權利？

o.en: The exclusive right to receive income
o.zh: Exclusive right to receive income 收益權
Exclusive right to use 專用權

w.en: Keeping the rent is receiving income from the property.
w.zh: 收租就係由財產得到收入。

d.en: Private property rights are the exclusive right to use, the exclusive right to receive income from, and the right to transfer a private property.
d.zh: Private property rights 係對私有財產嘅 exclusive right to use（專用權）、exclusive right to receive income（收益權）同 right to transfer（轉讓權）。

p.en: “Exclusive” means the owner can stop others from using it or taking its income.
p.zh: 「Exclusive」即係業主可以排除其他人使用或拎收益。

p.en: Transfer means selling, giving or leasing it to someone else.
p.zh: 轉讓即係賣、送或者租俾其他人。

s.en: Use: the family opens the stall on Sundays.
s.zh: 使用：屋企人星期日開檔。

s.en: Income: they keep the rent when they lease it out.
s.zh: 收益：租出去嘅租金歸佢哋。

s.en: Transfer: they could sell it or give it to a cousin.
s.zh: 轉讓：可以賣出或者送俾表哥。

q.en: The family sells the stall to a neighbour. Which right are they using?
q.zh: 佢哋將檔口賣俾鄰居。佢哋用緊邊種權利？

o.en: The exclusive right to receive income

w.en: Selling passes the property to another owner: that is transfer.
w.zh: 賣出將財產交俾另一個業主，即係轉讓。

q.en: Pick the best description of the right to transfer.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 right to transfer 描述。

o.en: The owner can keep the rent.
That is the exclusive right to receive income.
The owner can use the property alone.
o.zh: 業主可以自己獨用財產。

o.en: That is the exclusive right to use.
The owner can sell, give or lease the property to others.
o.zh: 業主可以將財產賣、送或者租俾其他人。

t.zh: 交換、專門化同經濟活動

hook.en: (Fictional family) Ah Ying’s family makes shrimp paste and sells it. With the money they buy rice, clothes and phones that other people made.
hook.zh: （虛構家庭）阿瑩屋企整蝦醬嚟賣，再用賺到嘅錢買其他人生產嘅米、衫同手機。

q.en: Why doesn’t the family make its own rice, clothes and phones?
q.zh: 點解佢哋唔自己種米、整衫同手機？

o.en: Focusing on shrimp paste and exchanging gets them more.
o.zh: 專心整蝦醬再交換，可以得到更多。

o.en: They do not want those goods.
o.zh: 因為佢哋唔想要嗰啲嘢。

w.en: Specialising and then exchanging lets everyone get more than producing everything alone.
w.zh: 專門化再交換，大家都可以得到多過自己樣樣嘢都做。

d.en: Specialisation: different people or economies concentrate on producing different goods, or different stages of the same good. Exchange can take place with money or without it (barter).
d.zh: Specialisation：唔同人或經濟體系專注生產唔同物品，或者同一物品嘅唔同生產階段。Exchange 可以用錢，亦可以唔用錢（barter 以物易物）。

p.en: Private property rights enable exchange; exchange enables specialisation.
p.zh: Private property rights 令交換成為可能；交換令專門化成為可能。

p.en: Economic activities: production (turning inputs into output), exchange (buying, selling or barter), consumption (directly satisfying wants).
p.zh: 經濟活動：production（將投入變成產出）、exchange（買賣或以物易物）、consumption（直接滿足 wants）。

p.en: Firms are production units; households are consumption units.
p.zh: Firms 係生產單位；households 係消費單位。

s.en: Production: the family turns shrimp and salt into paste.
s.zh: Production：屋企人將蝦同鹽變成蝦醬。

s.en: Exchange: a tourist buys a jar at the stall.
s.zh: Exchange：遊客喺檔口買一樽。

s.en: Consumption: the tourist eats it with rice at home.
s.zh: Consumption：遊客返屋企送飯食。

q.en: A tourist eats Tai O shrimp paste with fried rice at home. Which activity is this?
q.zh: 遊客喺屋企用大澳蝦醬炒飯食。呢個係邊種活動？

w.en: Eating it satisfies a want directly.
w.zh: 食落肚係直接滿足 wants。

q.en: Pick the correct chain.
q.zh: 揀正確嘅關係鏈。

o.zh: 以物易物就係唔用錢嘅交換。

o.en: You can only trade what is yours, and you only specialise if you can trade.
o.zh: 有產權先可以交換，可以交換先會專門化。

o.en: Specialisation depends on exchange, not the other way round.
o.zh: 專門化靠交換，唔係倒轉。

hook.en: Hong Kong today: public rental flats are allocated by eligibility rules and a waiting list, not by price.
hook.zh: 今日香港：公屋係按資格同輪候冊分配，唔係價高者得。

q.en: Is anyone discriminated against when public flats are allocated by waiting list?
q.zh: 用輪候冊分配公屋，有冇人被 discriminated against？

o.en: No, because no price is charged.
Yes. People who do not meet the rules, or cannot wait, lose out under the rules.
o.zh: 有。唔符合資格或者等唔到嘅人，喺規則下輸咗。

w.en: Every competition rule favours some people and leaves others out.
w.zh: 每種競爭準則都會令一啲人得益、一啲人輸。

d.en: Scarcity → competition → discrimination. Competition decides who gets the good and how much; those who lose are discriminated against by the rule.
d.zh: Scarcity → competition → discrimination。Competition 決定邊個得到物品同得到幾多；輸咗嘅人被規則 discriminated against。

p.en: Price competition uses price as the rule; non-price competition uses other rules (queuing, lottery, exam results).
p.zh: Price competition 以價格做準則；non-price competition 用其他準則（排隊、抽籤、考試成績）。

p.en: Here “discrimination” describes any allocation rule. It is not a moral or legal accusation.
p.zh: 呢度嘅「歧視」只係描述分配規則，唔係道德或法律指控。

s.en: Scarcity: there are not enough flats for everyone who wants one.
s.zh: Scarcity：公屋唔夠所有想要嘅人。

s.en: Competition: eligibility rules and waiting time decide who gets a flat (non-price).
s.zh: Competition：資格同輪候時間決定邊個上樓（non-price competition）。

s.en: Discrimination: people who cannot meet the rules lose out.
s.zh: Discrimination：達唔到準則嘅人就得唔到。

q.en: Which is an example of price competition?
q.zh: 以下邊個係 price competition？

o.en: The Transport Department auctions special car registration marks to the highest bidder.
o.zh: 運輸署將特別車牌拍賣俾出價最高嘅人。

o.en: University places are given by DSE results.
o.zh: 大學學額按 DSE 成績分配。

o.en: Free newspapers go to whoever comes first.
Home Ownership Scheme flats are sold by ballot.

w.en: Only the auction uses willingness and ability to pay as the rule.
w.zh: 只有拍賣用「願意並有能力付款」做準則。

q.en: Pick the correct statement.
q.zh: 揀正確嘅說法。

o.en: Discrimination means the allocation is illegal.
It is a technical term, not a legal one.
o.zh: 佢係經濟學術語，唔係法律用語。

o.en: There is no competition when the good is given out free.
Free goods given out by queue still involve non-price competition.
o.zh: 免費但要排隊，一樣有 non-price competition。

o.en: Scarcity leads to competition, and competition always implies discrimination.
o.zh: Scarcity 引致 competition，competition 一定隱含 discrimination。

hook.en: (Fictional family) Ah Ying’s mum works as a waitress at a Tai O seafood restaurant and spends her wages on rice and shrimp paste.
hook.zh: （虛構家庭）阿瑩媽媽喺大澳一間海鮮酒家做侍應，用人工買米同蝦醬。

q.en: When Ah Ying’s mum works at the restaurant, what does she supply to the firm?
q.zh: 阿瑩媽媽喺酒家返工，佢向廠商提供咗乜？

o.zh: Goods and services 物品同服務

w.en: A household supplies labour, a factor service, to the firm.
w.zh: 住戶向廠商提供勞動，即係 factor service。

d.en: Households supply factor services in the factor market and receive factor income. Firms supply goods and services in the product market and receive households’ expenditure.
d.zh: Households 喺 factor market 提供 factor services，收取 factor income；firms 喺 product market 提供 goods and services，收取 households 嘅開支。

p.en: Real flows: factor services and goods and services.
p.zh: Real flow：factor services、goods and services。

p.en: Money flows: factor income and consumption expenditure. They run opposite to the real flows.
p.zh: Money flow：factor income、consumption expenditure，同 real flow 方向相反。

s.en: Real flow: mum’s labour goes to the restaurant.
s.zh: Real flow：媽媽嘅勞動流向酒家。

s.en: Money flow: wages go from the restaurant to mum.
s.zh: Money flow：人工由酒家流向媽媽。

s.en: Real flow: rice and shrimp paste go to the household; money flow: her spending goes back to firms.
s.zh: Real flow：米同蝦醬流向住戶；money flow：佢嘅開支流返去廠商。

q.en: Which is a money flow in the circular flow?
q.zh: 以下邊個係循環流程入面嘅 money flow？

w.en: Wages are factor income, a money flow. The others are real flows.
w.zh: 工資係 factor income，屬 money flow。其他都係 real flow。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why do real flows and money flows go in opposite directions?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解 real flow 同 money flow 方向相反？

o.zh: 因為廠商從來唔俾錢住戶。

o.en: Firms pay factor income to households.
o.zh: 廠商會付 factor income 俾住戶。

o.en: Because money is a real flow.
Every payment is made in return for something supplied the other way.
o.zh: 每筆付款都係為咗換取由對方提供嘅嘢。

o.en: Money goes one way, the thing paid for goes the other.
o.zh: 錢去一邊，買到嘅嘢去另一邊。

hook.en: (Fictional people) Two Tai O residents talk on a Sunday in 2026. One says, “More tourists came today than last Sunday.” The other says, “There are too many tourists.”
hook.zh: （虛構人物）2026 年一個星期日，兩個大澳街坊傾偈。一個話：「今日遊客多過上個星期日。」另一個話：「遊客太多喇。」

q.en: Which statement can be checked against facts?
q.zh: 邊句可以用事實驗證？

o.en: “More tourists came today than last Sunday.”

w.en: You can count tourists. “Too many” depends on a value judgement.
w.zh: 遊客數目可以點算；「太多」視乎價值判斷。

d.en: Positive statements are about facts and can be refuted by facts. Normative statements involve value judgements and cannot be refuted by facts.
d.zh: Positive statement 關於事實，可以被事實推翻。Normative statement 涉及 value judgement，唔可以被事實推翻。

p.en: Test: can facts reject it? Yes → positive.
p.zh: 測試：事實可唔可以推翻佢？可以 → positive。

p.en: Words like should, ought, too high, better usually signal normative.
p.zh: 有 should、ought、太高、較好等字眼，通常係 normative。

p.en: A false statement can still be positive, because it can be tested.
p.zh: 錯嘅陳述都可以係 positive，因為佢可以被驗證。

s.en: “More tourists came today” → count them → positive.
s.zh: 「今日遊客多咗」→ 可以點算 → positive。

s.en: “There are too many tourists” → a value judgement → normative.
s.zh: 「遊客太多」→ 價值判斷 → normative。

s.en: “Tai O has one million residents” → false, but testable → positive.
s.zh: 「大澳有一百萬居民」→ 錯，但可以驗證 → positive。

q.en: Which is a normative statement?
q.zh: 以下邊句係 normative statement？

o.en: Higher fares will reduce the number of passengers.
Tai O is on Lantau Island.
The government should cut ferry fares to Tai O.
Ferry fares to Tai O rose last year.

w.en: “Should” is a value judgement. A prediction like the last option can be tested, so it is positive.
w.zh: 「應該」係價值判斷。最後一項係預測，可以驗證，所以係 positive。

q.en: Pick the best definition of a positive statement.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 positive statement 定義。

o.en: False statements can be positive too.
o.zh: 錯嘅陳述都可以係 positive。

o.en: It can be tested and refuted by facts, even if it turns out to be wrong.
o.zh: 可以用事實驗證同推翻，就算佢最後係錯。

q.en: Hong Kong mainly uses prices to decide what is produced. Its economy is mainly a…
q.zh: 香港主要靠價格決定生產咩，佢主要係…

w.en: Prices are the main method, so it is mainly a market economy.
w.zh: 主要靠價格，所以主要係市場經濟。

q.en: Which is normative?
q.zh: 以下邊句係 normative？

o.en: Rents of public flats are below market rents.
o.zh: 公屋租金低過市場租金。

o.en: Hong Kong should build more public flats.
Public flats are allocated by waiting list.
Hong Kong built public flats last year.

w.en: “Should” signals a value judgement.
w.zh: 「應該」代表價值判斷。

q.en: A worker’s wages in the circular flow are…
q.zh: 循環流程入面，工人嘅工資係…

o.en: a real flow from households to firms
o.zh: 由住戶流向廠商嘅 real flow

o.en: not part of the circular flow
o.zh: 唔係循環流程嘅一部分

o.en: a money flow from households to firms
o.zh: 由住戶流向廠商嘅 money flow

o.en: a money flow from firms to households
o.zh: 由廠商流向住戶嘅 money flow

w.en: Wages are factor income paid by firms.
w.zh: 工資係廠商付出嘅 factor income。

q.en: In your own words: why does a market economy need private property rights?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解市場經濟需要私有產權？

ck.en: I named the rights: use, income, transfer.
ck.zh: 我有講出三種權利：使用、收益、轉讓。

ck.en: I said the right to transfer makes exchange possible.
ck.zh: 我有講轉讓權令交換成為可能。

ck.en: I said exchange allows specialisation.
ck.zh: 我有講交換令專門化成為可能。

t.en: Goods, services, consumer and producer goods
t.zh: 物品、服務、消費品同生產品

hook.en: Sham Shui Po, 1970s. Garment factories gathered in Sham Shui Po and Cheung Sha Wan, and garment making was Hong Kong’s leading industry by number of factories, workers and export value.
hook.zh: 1970 年代，製衣廠集中喺深水埗同長沙灣。按工廠數目、工人數目同出口值計，製衣業係香港最主要嘅工業。

q.en: A sewing machine in a Cheung Sha Wan factory is used to make shirts. What kind of good is it?
q.zh: 長沙灣工廠嘅衣車用嚟車恤衫。佢係咩物品？

w.en: It is used to produce other goods, so here it is a producer good.
w.zh: 佢用嚟生產其他物品，所以喺呢度係生產品。

idea.term: goods vs services; consumer vs producer goods

d.en: Goods are tangible; services are intangible. By use: consumer goods satisfy wants directly; producer (capital) goods are used to produce other goods. The same good can be either.
d.zh: Goods 係有形（tangible），services 係無形（intangible）。按用途分：直接滿足 wants 嘅係 consumer goods；用嚟生產其他物品嘅係 producer（capital）goods。同一件物品可以兩樣都係。

p.en: Classify by how the good is used, not by what it is.
p.zh: 按用途分類，唔係按物品本身。

p.en: A tailor’s fitting is a service: you cannot hold it.
p.zh: 裁縫度身係服務：摸唔到。

t.zh: 一部衣車，兩種用途（2026 年）

s.en: In a factory it makes shirts for sale → producer good.
s.zh: 喺工廠車衫出售 → 生產品。

s.en: At home Ah Ying’s grandma uses it to mend her own clothes → consumer good.
s.zh: 阿瑩嫲嫲喺屋企用嚟補自己件衫 → 消費品。

s.en: The alteration shop on Ki Lung Street sells a service: changing your trousers.
s.zh: 基隆街（布行街）改衫舖賣嘅係服務：幫你改褲。

q.en: Which is a service?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係服務？

o.en: A haircut in Sham Shui Po

w.en: A haircut is intangible: you buy the act, not an object.
w.zh: 剪頭髮係無形嘅：你買嘅係過程，唔係一件物件。

q.en: Pick the best rule for consumer vs producer goods.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅消費品／生產品分類規則。

o.en: A sewing machine at home can be a consumer good.
o.zh: 屋企用嘅衣車可以係消費品。

o.en: Look at how the good is used: to satisfy wants directly, or to produce other goods.
o.zh: 睇物品點用：直接滿足 wants，定係用嚟生產其他物品。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) In 2026 Ah Ying walks from a Sham Shui Po street stall, where she buys a $10 egg waffle, to the street lights along Apliu Street.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年，阿瑩喺深水埗街邊檔買咗一份 $10 雞蛋仔，再行去鴨寮街，街燈照住佢。

q.en: If Ah Ying eats the egg waffle, can someone else eat the same one?
q.zh: 阿瑩食咗份雞蛋仔，其他人仲可唔可以食同一份？

w.en: Her eating it reduces what is left for others: it is rival.
w.zh: 佢食咗就冇得俾其他人食：即係 rival。

d.en: Private goods are rival (one person’s use reduces what is left for others) and excludable (non-payers can be kept out at low cost). Public goods are non-rival and non-excludable.
d.zh: Private goods：rival（一個人用咗會減少其他人可用嘅數量）同 excludable（排除唔俾錢嘅人成本唔高）。Public goods：non-rival 同 non-excludable。

p.en: Classify by the nature of the good, not by who provides it or whether it is free.
p.zh: 按物品性質分類，唔係睇邊個提供、收唔收錢。

p.en: A street light is non-rival and non-excludable: a public good.
p.zh: 街燈 non-rival 又 non-excludable，係公共物品。

s.en: Egg waffle: rival (eaten once) and excludable (pay first) → private good.
s.zh: 雞蛋仔：rival（食咗就冇）同 excludable（要俾錢先有）→ 私人物品。

s.en: Street light: one more walker does not dim it (non-rival), and you cannot stop passers-by enjoying it (non-excludable) → public good.
s.zh: 街燈：多一個人行過唔會暗啲（non-rival），亦攔唔到路人受惠（non-excludable）→ 公共物品。

s.en: A free egg waffle handed out by the government is still a private good.
s.zh: 就算政府免費派雞蛋仔，佢都仍然係私人物品。

q.en: Which statement is correct?
q.zh: 以下邊句啱？

o.en: A good is public if it is non-rival and non-excludable.
o.zh: Non-rival 同 non-excludable 嘅物品係公共物品。

o.en: A free good is the same as a public good.
o.zh: Free good 同公共物品一樣。

o.en: A good provided by the government must be a public good.
o.zh: 政府提供嘅物品一定係公共物品。

o.en: Private goods are always sold by private firms.
o.zh: 私人物品一定由私人公司出售。

w.en: Nature decides, not the provider or the price.
w.zh: 睇物品性質，唔睇提供者或價錢。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is a street light a public good?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解街燈係公共物品？

o.en: One more user does not reduce the light for others, and non-payers cannot be kept out.
o.zh: 多一個人用都唔會減少其他人用到嘅光，亦排除唔到唔俾錢嘅人。

o.en: Free of charge does not make a good public.
o.zh: 免費唔會令物品變成公共物品。

hook.en: Sham Shui Po, 1970s: cotton was spun and woven into cloth, sewn into jeans in Cheung Sha Wan, then shipped and sold.
hook.zh: 1970 年代深水埗：棉花紡成紗、織成布，喺長沙灣車成牛仔褲，再付運同出售。

q.en: A Cheung Sha Wan factory sews cloth into jeans. Which type of production is this?
q.zh: 長沙灣工廠將布車成牛仔褲。呢個係邊類生產？

w.en: Turning materials into finished goods is secondary production.
w.zh: 將原料變成製成品係第二產業。

d.en: Primary production takes resources directly from nature. Secondary production turns raw materials into semi-finished or finished goods, including construction. Tertiary production provides services.
d.zh: Primary production 直接由大自然攞資源；secondary production 將原料變成半製成品或製成品（包括建造）；tertiary production 提供服務。

p.en: Construction counts as secondary production.
p.zh: 建造業屬第二產業。

p.en: Transport, retail and banking are tertiary.
p.zh: 運輸、零售同銀行屬第三產業。

s.en: Growing cotton → primary.
s.zh: 種棉花 → 第一產業。

s.en: Weaving cloth and sewing jeans → secondary.
s.zh: 織布、車牛仔褲 → 第二產業。

s.en: Shipping the jeans and selling them in a shop → tertiary.
s.zh: 運送同喺舖頭出售 → 第三產業。

q.en: Which is tertiary production?
q.zh: 以下邊個屬第三產業？

o.en: A truck delivering cloth to a factory

w.en: Delivery is a service. Building is secondary, fishing is primary.
w.zh: 運送係服務。起樓屬第二產業，捕魚屬第一產業。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of secondary production.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅第二產業解釋。

o.en: Any production that comes second in time.
It is about the type of work, not timing.
o.zh: 講嘅係工作性質，唔係時間先後。

o.en: Turning raw materials into semi-finished or finished goods, including construction.
o.zh: 將原料變成半製成品或製成品，包括建造。

hook.en: Sham Shui Po, 1970s: inside a garment factory, one worker cut cloth, another sewed sleeves, another attached buttons.
hook.zh: 1970 年代深水埗：製衣廠入面，有人裁布、有人車衫袖、有人釘鈕。

q.en: Different workers do different steps of the same shirt. Which type of division of labour is this?
q.zh: 唔同工人做同一件恤衫嘅唔同工序。呢個係邊種分工？

w.en: Splitting one product into steps is complex division of labour.
w.zh: 將一件產品拆成工序，係複雜分工。

d.en: Simple: different workers specialise in producing different goods. Complex: different workers specialise in different steps of the same good. Regional: different regions specialise in different goods or steps.
d.zh: Simple：唔同工人專門生產唔同物品。Complex：唔同工人專門做同一物品嘅唔同工序。Regional：唔同地區專門生產唔同物品或工序。

p.en: Look at what is split: whole goods, steps, or places.
p.zh: 睇拆開嘅係咩：整件物品、工序，定係地方。

s.en: A tailor makes whole suits, a cobbler makes whole shoes → simple.
s.zh: 裁縫整成套西裝、鞋匠整成對鞋 → 簡單分工。

s.en: In a factory, cutting, sewing and buttoning are done by different workers → complex.
s.zh: 工廠入面，裁、車、釘鈕由唔同工人做 → 複雜分工。

s.en: Sham Shui Po focuses on garments while another district focuses on electronics → regional.
s.zh: 深水埗集中做製衣，另一區集中做電子 → 地域分工。

q.en: A Sham Shui Po baker makes bread while her neighbour makes noodles. Which type of division of labour is this?
q.zh: 深水埗一個師傅專做麵包，隔籬專做麵。呢個係邊種分工？

w.en: Different people make different whole goods.
w.zh: 唔同人生產唔同嘅完整物品。

q.en: Pick the best description of complex division of labour.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅複雜分工描述。

o.en: Workers each make a different whole good.
o.zh: 每個工人整一件唔同嘅完整物品。

o.en: That is simple division of labour.
Workers each do one step of making the same good.
o.zh: 每個工人做同一物品嘅其中一個工序。

o.en: That is regional division of labour.

t.en: Pros, cons and limits of division of labour
t.zh: 分工嘅好處、壞處同限制

hook.en: Sham Shui Po, 1970s: garment output was so high that manufacturers could not keep up with orders in peak seasons. Many workers did the same step all day.
hook.zh: 1970 年代深水埗：製衣業產量高到旺季都趕唔切訂單。好多工人成日都做同一個工序。

q.en: Why can a worker who sews only sleeves all day produce faster?
q.zh: 點解成日淨係車衫袖嘅工人做得快啲？

o.en: Practice makes perfect, and no time is lost switching tasks.
o.zh: 熟能生巧，又慳咗轉工序嘅時間。

w.en: Repetition builds skill and saves switching time, so labour productivity rises.
w.zh: 重複令技術熟練，又慳轉工序時間，labour productivity 上升。

idea.term: division of labour: pros, cons, limits

d.en: Pros: higher labour productivity (better use of capital, choose the most suitable person, practice makes perfect, saves switching and training time, encourages mechanisation) and higher living standards. Cons: boredom, less job satisfaction, risk of unemployment, interdependence, over-standardised products. Limits: the nature of the product (creative work) and a small market.
d.zh: 好處：提高 labour productivity（善用 capital、揀最合適嘅人、熟能生巧、慳轉工序時間、慳訓練時間、促進機械化），改善生活水平。壞處：沉悶、失去工作滿足感、失業風險、互相依賴、產品過度標準化。限制：產品性質（要創意）、市場太細。

p.en: A small market limits division of labour: no point splitting steps for ten shirts a month.
p.zh: 市場細會限制分工：一個月只賣十件衫，冇必要拆細工序。

t.en: A sleeve sewer in a 1970s factory

s.en: Good: she becomes very fast at sleeves → productivity ↑.
s.zh: 好處：車衫袖越嚟越快 → productivity ↑。

s.en: Bad: the work is boring, and if sleeves are later sewn by machine she may lose her job.
s.zh: 壞處：工作沉悶；如果之後改用機器車袖，佢可能失業。

s.en: Limit: a custom wedding dress needs one skilled tailor, not a production line.
s.zh: 限制：度身訂造嘅婚紗要一個熟手裁縫，唔適合生產線。

q.en: Which is a LIMIT of division of labour?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係分工嘅「限制」？

o.en: The market for the product is too small.

w.en: A small market limits how far work can be split. Boredom and interdependence are disadvantages, not limits.
w.zh: 市場細限制分工嘅程度。沉悶同互相依賴係壞處，唔係限制。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does division of labour raise labour productivity?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解分工會提高 labour productivity？

o.en: Longer hours raise output, not output per hour.
o.zh: 工時長會增加產量，但唔係每小時產量。

o.en: Workers become skilled at one task and save time switching between tasks.
o.zh: 工人專做一樣變得熟練，又慳轉工序時間。

o.en: Two key reasons in one line.
o.zh: 一句講到兩個主要原因。

o.en: Division of labour tends to standardise products.
o.zh: 分工反而令產品更標準化。

chain.en: Limited by market size and product nature
chain.zh: 受市場大小同產品性質限制

q.en: Which is a public good?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係公共物品？

w.en: Non-rival and non-excludable.
w.zh: Non-rival 同 non-excludable。

q.en: Building a factory belongs to…
q.zh: 起工廠屬於…

w.en: Construction is secondary.
w.zh: 建造業屬第二產業。

q.en: Workers in different steps of making the same shirt shows…
q.zh: 唔同工人做同一件恤衫嘅唔同工序，係…

w.en: Steps of one good.
w.zh: 同一物品嘅工序。

q.en: In your own words: why did 1970s garment factories split work into steps, and what was the cost to workers?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解 1970 年代製衣廠將工作拆成工序？對工人有咩代價？

ck.en: I said splitting steps raises labour productivity.
ck.zh: 我有講拆工序會提高 labour productivity。

ck.en: I gave a reason: practice, saving switching time, or mechanisation.
ck.zh: 我有講原因：熟能生巧、慳轉工序時間或機械化。

ck.en: I named a cost: boredom, less satisfaction, or unemployment risk.
ck.zh: 我有講代價：沉悶、少咗滿足感或者失業風險。

hook.en: (Fictional business) In 2026 a small garment workshop in Cheung Sha Wan rents its unit, borrows money for sewing machines, hires workers, and its owner takes the risk.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）2026 年，長沙灣一間細製衣工場租舖位、借錢買衣車、請工人，由老闆承擔風險。

q.en: What is the return to the owner who organises the workshop and bears the risk?
q.zh: 組織工場、承擔風險嘅老闆，佢嘅回報係乜？

w.en: Entrepreneurship earns profits.
w.zh: Entrepreneurship 嘅回報係 profits。

d.en: Labour earns wages, capital earns interest, land earns rent, entrepreneurship earns profits.
d.zh: Labour（wages）、capital（interest）、land（rent）、entrepreneurship（profits）。

p.en: Land is created at no cost, but using it has a cost. Its supply cannot be increased by human effort, but it is not fixed.
p.zh: Land 創造冇成本，但使用有成本；供應唔可以靠人力增加，但唔係固定。

p.en: Capital accumulation happens when capital formation is greater than capital depreciation.
p.zh: Capital formation > capital depreciation → capital accumulation。

s.en: Land: the space the unit stands on → rent.
s.zh: Land：舖位所在嘅土地 → rent。

s.en: Capital: the sewing machines → interest.
s.zh: Capital：衣車 → interest。

s.en: Labour: the sewers → wages. Entrepreneurship: the owner → profits.
s.zh: Labour：車衣工人 → wages。Entrepreneurship：老闆 → profits。

q.en: A sewing machine in the workshop is an example of…
q.zh: 工場嘅衣車屬於…

w.en: A man-made good used in production is capital.
w.zh: 用嚟生產嘅人造物品係 capital。

q.en: Pick the correct statement about land.
q.zh: 揀關於 land 嘅正確說法。

o.en: Land costs nothing to create, but using it has an opportunity cost.
o.zh: Land 創造冇成本，但使用佢有 opportunity cost。

o.en: Its other uses are given up.
o.zh: 用咗就放棄咗其他用途。

o.en: The supply of land is completely fixed.

o.zh: 填海可以增加可用土地。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) The Cheung Sha Wan workshop has 10 workers, each working 8 hours a day.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）長沙灣工場有 10 個工人，每人每日做 8 個鐘。

q.en: What is the workshop’s daily labour supply?
q.zh: 工場每日嘅 labour supply 係幾多？

w.en: Labour supply is counted in hours: 10 × 8 = 80 man-hours.
w.zh: Labour supply 用工時計：10 × 8 = 80 工時。

d.en: Labour supply = total working hours (man-hours) = number of workers × average working hours per worker. It is not a head count.
d.zh: Labour supply = 總工作時數（man-hours）= 工人數目 × 每人平均工作時數，唔係以人頭計。

p.en: More workers working fewer hours each can mean less labour supply.
p.zh: 人多但每人做少啲，labour supply 可以減少。

s.en: Start: 10 workers × 8 hours = 80 man-hours.
s.zh: 開始：10 人 × 8 個鐘 = 80 工時。

s.en: Hire 2 more but cut hours to 6: 12 × 6 = 72 man-hours.
s.zh: 多請 2 人但減到每人 6 個鐘：12 × 6 = 72 工時。

s.en: More workers, yet labour supply fell from 80 to 72.
s.zh: 工人多咗，但 labour supply 由 80 跌到 72。

q.en: (Fictional figures) A shop has 5 workers working 9 hours a day. One leaves and the rest work 10 hours. Labour supply…
q.zh: （虛構數字）一間舖有 5 個工人，每日做 9 個鐘。走咗一個，其餘每人做 10 個鐘。Labour supply…

q.en: Pick the best explanation of labour supply.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 labour supply 解釋。

o.en: The total number of working hours: workers × hours each.
o.zh: 總工作時數：工人數目 × 每人工時。

o.en: The number of hours one worker works.
That ignores the number of workers.

hook.en: (Fictional figures) In 2026 the Cheung Sha Wan workshop sews 400 shirts in a day using 80 man-hours.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年，長沙灣工場一日用 80 工時車咗 400 件恤衫。

q.en: What is its labour productivity?
q.zh: 佢嘅 labour productivity 係幾多？

w.en: Output ÷ working hours = 400 ÷ 80 = 5.

d.en: Labour productivity = total output ÷ total number of working hours (output per working hour). It is not output per worker.
d.zh: Labour productivity = total output ÷ total number of working hours（每工時產量），唔係每個工人嘅產量。

p.en: Output can rise while productivity falls, if hours rise even faster.
p.zh: 產量上升，但如果工時升得更快，productivity 可以下跌。

t.zh: 同樣產量，唔同工時（虛構數字）

s.en: Day 1: 400 shirts ÷ 80 hours = 5 per hour.
s.zh: 第一日：400 件 ÷ 80 工時 = 每工時 5 件。

s.en: Day 2: 400 shirts ÷ 100 hours = 4 per hour.
s.zh: 第二日：400 件 ÷ 100 工時 = 每工時 4 件。

s.en: Same output, more hours → productivity fell.
s.zh: 產量一樣，工時多咗 → productivity 下跌。

q.en: (Fictional figures) Output rises from 400 to 450 shirts, and working hours rise from 80 to 100. Labour productivity…
q.zh: （虛構數字）產量由 400 件升到 450 件，工時由 80 升到 100。Labour productivity…

o.zh: 由每工時 5 件跌到 4.5 件
因為產量升咗所以上升
由每工時 5 件升到 5.6 件

q.en: Pick the best explanation of labour productivity.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 labour productivity 解釋。

o.zh: 淨係睇產量冇計用咗幾多工時。
佢係量度出嚟，唔係感覺。

hook.en: Late 1980s to early 1990s: many Hong Kong garment factories moved production to the Pearl River Delta, and many low-skilled workers here were laid off.
hook.zh: 1980 年代末至 1990 年代初，好多香港製衣廠將生產線北移到珠江三角洲，大批低技術工人被裁。

q.en: A sewing worker retrains as a care worker. Which mobility is this?
q.zh: 車衣工人再培訓做護理員。呢個係邊種流動性？

w.en: Changing occupation is occupational mobility.
w.zh: 轉職業係職業流動性。

d.en: Occupational mobility: the willingness and ease of changing occupations. Geographical mobility: the willingness and ease of changing work location.
d.zh: Occupational mobility：轉職業嘅意願同容易程度。Geographical mobility：轉工作地點嘅意願同容易程度。

p.en: Retraining raises occupational mobility.
p.zh: 再培訓提高職業流動性。

p.en: Cheaper, faster transport raises geographical mobility.
p.zh: 交通平啲、快啲，會提高地域流動性。

s.en: A Sham Shui Po seamstress becomes a care worker → occupational.
s.zh: 深水埗車衣女工轉做護理員 → 職業流動。

s.en: A sales clerk moves from a Sham Shui Po shop to a Central shop, same job → geographical.
s.zh: 售貨員由深水埗嘅舖轉去中環嘅舖，做同一份工 → 地域流動。

s.en: Both kinds can rise or fall with training, transport, housing and family ties.
s.zh: 兩種流動性都受培訓、交通、住屋同家庭因素影響。

q.en: Which raises geographical mobility of labour?
q.zh: 以下邊樣會提高地域流動性？

o.en: A new railway line cuts travel time between districts.
o.zh: 新鐵路縮短區與區之間嘅交通時間。

w.en: Easier travel makes changing work location easier.
w.zh: 交通方便令轉工作地點更容易。

q.en: Pick the best description of occupational mobility.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅職業流動性描述。

o.en: How willing and able workers are to change occupations.
o.zh: 工人有幾願意、幾容易轉職業。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) In 2026, at Ah Ying’s aunt’s Sham Shui Po phone shop, sales staff get a basic wage plus 2% of their sales.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年，阿瑩姨媽喺深水埗嘅手機舖，售貨員有底薪加 2% 營業額。

q.en: The 2% of sales is which payment method?
q.zh: 2% 營業額係邊種計薪方法？

w.en: A share of sales revenue is commission.
w.zh: 按銷售收入抽成係佣金。

d.en: Piece rate (per unit produced), time rate (per period of time), commission (a share of sales revenue), profit-sharing (a share of profits), tips (paid by customers).
d.zh: Piece rate（按件）、time rate（按時間）、commission（銷售收入嘅一部分）、profit-sharing（利潤嘅一部分）、tips（客人俾嘅打賞）。

p.en: Piece rate rewards speed but may lower quality.
p.zh: 按件計鼓勵快，但質素可能下降。

p.en: Time rate suits work whose output is hard to count.
p.zh: 按時間計適合產量難以點算嘅工作。

s.en: A seamstress earns $3 per shirt sewn → piece rate.
s.zh: 車衣女工每車一件衫 $3 → piece rate。

s.en: A cleaner earns $60 an hour → time rate.
s.zh: 清潔工每個鐘 $60 → time rate。

s.en: A waiter keeps diners’ tips; a manager gets 5% of profits → tips, profit-sharing.
s.zh: 侍應收客人貼士；經理分 5% 利潤 → tips、profit-sharing。

q.en: Which job is best paid by time rate rather than piece rate?
q.zh: 以下邊份工最適合按時間計而唔係按件計？

o.en: A leaflet distributor paid per leaflet
A worker packing boxes of masks

w.en: A guard’s output cannot be counted in units.
w.zh: 保安嘅產出唔可以按件點算。

q.en: Pick the best description of commission.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅佣金描述。

o.en: A share of the firm’s profits.
Pay that is a share of the sales revenue the worker brings in.
o.zh: 按員工帶嚟嘅銷售收入抽成。

chain.zh: Labour supply = 人數 × 工時
Labour productivity = 產量 ÷ 工時

chain.en: Mobility lets labour move to better uses
chain.zh: 流動性令勞動轉去更好用途

chain.en: Wage methods reward work in different ways
chain.zh: 計薪方法用唔同方式回報工作

q.en: Which factor earns rent?
q.zh: 邊種生產要素嘅回報係 rent？

w.en: Land earns rent.
w.zh: Land 嘅回報係 rent。

q.en: (Fictional figures) 6 workers each work 7 hours. Labour supply is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）6 個工人每人做 7 個鐘，labour supply 係…

q.en: A Sham Shui Po clerk moves to the same job in Kwun Tong. This shows…
q.zh: 深水埗文員轉去觀塘做同一份工，呢個係…

w.en: Same job, new place.
w.zh: 同一份工，新地點。

q.en: In your own words: why is labour productivity measured per working hour, not per worker?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解 labour productivity 用每工時計，而唔係每個工人計？

ck.en: I said workers can work different numbers of hours.
ck.zh: 我有講工人嘅工時可以唔同。

ck.en: I said output per hour compares like with like.
ck.zh: 我有講每工時產量先可以公平比較。

ck.en: I gave the formula: output ÷ total working hours.
ck.zh: 我有寫公式：產量 ÷ 總工時。

hook.en: (Fictional business) In 2026 a Sham Shui Po bakery has one oven and a two-year lease. This month it can hire more bakers, but it cannot add a second oven room.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）2026 年，深水埗一間餅店得一個焗爐，租約兩年。今個月可以多請師傅，但唔可以加多一間焗爐房。

q.en: Is the bakery in the short run or the long run?
q.zh: 呢間餅店處於短期定長期？

w.en: At least one factor (the oven room) is fixed.
w.zh: 最少有一種要素（焗爐房）係固定。

d.en: Short run: at least one factor of production is fixed. Long run: all factors are variable. It is not about calendar time.
d.zh: Short run：最少有一種 fixed factor。Long run：所有生產要素都係 variable。唔係按日曆長短分。

p.en: Fixed factor: its quantity cannot be changed in the period (e.g. the shop space).
p.zh: Fixed factor：喺嗰段時間數量改變唔到（例如舖位）。

p.en: Variable factor: its quantity can be changed (e.g. bakers, flour).
p.zh: Variable factor：數量可以改變（例如師傅、麵粉）。

s.en: Bakers and flour can change this month → variable factors.
s.zh: 師傅同麵粉今個月可以變 → variable factors。

s.en: The shop space is fixed until the lease ends → fixed factor → short run.
s.zh: 舖位要等租約完先可以變 → fixed factor → short run。

s.en: When the lease ends and everything can change → long run.
s.zh: 租約完咗，所有嘢都可以變 → long run。

q.en: Which statement is correct?
q.zh: 以下邊句啱？

o.en: The long run is any period longer than one year.
In the long run all factors are variable.
o.zh: 長期入面所有生產要素都係 variable。

o.en: In the short run all factors are fixed.
o.zh: 短期入面所有生產要素都係固定。

o.en: The short run is always less than a month.

w.en: Defined by fixed vs variable factors, not by the calendar.
w.zh: 用固定同可變要素界定，唔係日曆。

q.en: Pick the best test for the short run.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅短期判斷方法。

o.en: At least one factor cannot be changed.
o.zh: 最少有一種要素改變唔到。
有一種固定要素就係短期。

o.en: The period is shorter than a year.
Calendar length is not the test.

t.en: TFC, TVC, TC, AC and MC

hook.en: (Fictional figures) The Sham Shui Po bakery pays $1,000 a day in rent. Making 100 buns costs $300 in flour and wages; making 101 buns costs $303.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）深水埗餅店每日租金 $1,000。整 100 個包，麵粉同人工 $300；整 101 個包要 $303。

q.en: What is the marginal cost of the 101st bun?
q.zh: 第 101 個包嘅 marginal cost 係幾多？

d.en: TC = TFC + TVC. AC = TC ÷ Q. MC = TC(x) − TC(x−1) = TVC(x) − TVC(x−1).
d.zh: TC = TFC + TVC；AC = TC ÷ Q；MC = TC(x) − TC(x−1) = TVC(x) − TVC(x−1)。

p.en: A change in fixed cost does not change MC.
p.zh: Fixed cost 改變唔影響 MC。

p.en: TFC stays the same at every output, even zero.
p.zh: TFC 喺任何產量（包括零）都一樣。

s.en: TFC = $1,000 rent; TVC = $300.
Rent rises to $1,200: TC and AC rise, but MC of the 101st bun is still $3.
s.zh: 租金加到 $1,200：TC 同 AC 上升，但第 101 個包嘅 MC 仍然係 $3。

q.en: (Fictional figures) Rent rises. Which cost is NOT affected?
q.zh: （虛構數字）租金上升。以下邊種成本唔受影響？

w.en: Rent is fixed cost; MC depends only on variable cost.
w.zh: 租金係固定成本；MC 只受可變成本影響。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does a rise in rent not change MC?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解加租唔影響 MC？

o.en: Payment timing is not the reason.
Rent is the same whatever the output, so it adds nothing to the cost of one more unit.
o.zh: 無論產量幾多租金都一樣，所以唔會令多生產一單位嘅成本增加。
因為 MC 包括 TFC。

t.en: TP, AP, MP and diminishing marginal returns

hook.en: (Fictional figures) The Sham Shui Po bakery keeps one oven and adds bakers one by one: 1 baker makes 60 buns an hour, 2 make 140, 3 make 190, 4 make 220.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）深水埗餅店維持一個焗爐，逐個加師傅：1 個師傅每小時整 60 個包，2 個整 140 個，3 個整 190 個，4 個整 220 個。

q.en: What is the marginal product (MP) of the 3rd baker?
q.zh: 第 3 個師傅嘅 marginal product（MP）係幾多？

idea.term: TP, AP, MP and the law of diminishing marginal returns

d.en: AP = TP ÷ units of the variable factor. MP(n) = TP(n) − TP(n−1). In the short run, as more units of a variable factor are added to a fixed amount of fixed factors, the MP of the variable factor will eventually fall (technology unchanged).
d.zh: AP = TP ÷ variable factor 單位；MP(n) = TP(n) − TP(n−1)。Short run 入面，不斷將 variable factor 加落固定數量嘅 fixed factors，variable factor 嘅 MP 最終會下降（technology 不變）。

p.en: MP > AP → AP rises; MP < AP → AP falls.
p.zh: MP > AP 時 AP 上升；MP < AP 時 AP 下降。

p.en: The law applies only in the short run, with at least one fixed factor.
p.zh: 呢條定律只適用於 short run，要有 fixed factor。

t.zh: 每個師傅嘅 MP（虛構數字）

s.en: MP rises at first (bakers share tasks), then falls after the 2nd baker: diminishing marginal returns.
s.zh: MP 初時上升（師傅分工），過咗第 2 個之後下降：邊際回報遞減。

s.en: Why: all bakers share one oven, the fixed factor.
s.zh: 原因：所有師傅共用一個焗爐，即係 fixed factor。

q.en: Which condition is needed for the law of diminishing marginal returns?
q.zh: 邊個係邊際回報遞減定律嘅必要條件？

o.en: At least one factor is fixed.

w.en: It is a short-run law about adding a variable factor to fixed factors.
w.zh: 佢係短期定律：將可變要素加落固定要素。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of diminishing marginal returns.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅邊際回報遞減解釋。

o.en: With a fixed factor, each extra unit of the variable factor eventually adds less output.
o.zh: 有固定要素時，每多一單位可變要素最終會增加越嚟越少嘅產量。
固定要素 + 越嚟越多可變要素。

o.en: Total output falls when more workers are hired.
TP can still rise while MP falls.
o.zh: MP 下跌時 TP 仍然可以上升。

o.en: The law assumes identical units of the variable factor.
o.zh: 定律假設每單位可變要素一樣。

hook.en: (Fictional business) In 2026 the Sham Shui Po bakery opens a bigger central kitchen and buys flour in bulk at a lower price per bag.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）2026 年，深水埗餅店開咗一個更大嘅中央廚房，大量入貨，每包麵粉平咗。

q.en: The bakery expands its own scale and its long-run average cost (LRAC) falls. This is…
q.zh: 餅店擴大自己嘅生產規模，LRAC 下降。呢個係…

w.en: The firm’s own expansion lowers its LRAC.
w.zh: 廠商自己擴張令 LRAC 下降。

d.en: When a firm expands its own scale of production and its LRAC falls, it enjoys internal economies of scale. Beyond the optimal scale, LRAC rises: internal diseconomies of scale.
d.zh: 廠商擴大自己嘅生產規模，LRAC 下降 = internal economies of scale；超過 optimal scale 後 LRAC 上升 = internal diseconomies of scale。

p.en: Sources include bulk buying, specialised machines and staff, and cheaper borrowing.
p.zh: 來源包括大量採購、專門化機器同人手、借錢較易較平。

p.en: Diseconomies: management becomes harder and communication slower.
p.zh: 規模不經濟：管理變難、溝通變慢。

s.en: Bulk flour at a lower price per bag → LRAC ↓.
s.zh: 大量買麵粉，每包平咗 → LRAC ↓。

s.en: A big dough machine replaces hand kneading → LRAC ↓.
s.zh: 用大型搓粉機代替人手搓 → LRAC ↓。

s.en: Twenty shops later, orders get mixed up between branches → LRAC ↑ (diseconomies).
s.zh: 開到二十間分店，分店之間訂單亂晒 → LRAC ↑（diseconomies）。

q.en: Which is an internal DISeconomy of scale?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係 internal diseconomy of scale？

o.en: Rents rise in the whole district.
A very large firm finds it hard to coordinate its managers.
o.zh: 大公司好難協調各層管理人員。

o.en: A large firm gets bank loans at lower interest.
A large firm buys raw materials in bulk.

w.en: Coordination problems inside the firm raise LRAC. District-wide rent is external.
w.zh: 公司內部協調困難令 LRAC 上升。成區加租屬外部因素。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of internal economies of scale.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 internal economies of scale 解釋。

o.en: A firm’s LRAC falls because the firm itself expands.
o.zh: 廠商因為自己擴張而令 LRAC 下降。

o.en: Output rises when more workers are hired.
That is about MP, not scale.
A firm’s LRAC falls because the whole industry grows.
o.zh: 因為成個行業擴張，廠商 LRAC 下降。

hook.en: Sham Shui Po, after the war: garment factories clustered in Sham Shui Po and Cheung Sha Wan, where nearby textile and clothing makers kept raw materials readily available.
hook.zh: 戰後，製衣廠集中喺深水埗同長沙灣；附近嘅紡織同成衣廠令原料好容易買到。

q.en: A factory’s costs fall because many related firms are nearby. This is…
q.zh: 因為附近有好多相關廠商，工廠成本下降。呢個係…

w.en: The whole industry’s growth, not the firm’s own, lowers its LRAC.
w.zh: 係成個行業擴張，唔係廠商自己，令 LRAC 下降。

d.en: When the whole industry expands and an individual firm’s LRAC falls, that is external economies of scale. If the industry over-expands and LRAC rises, that is external diseconomies of scale.
d.zh: 整個行業擴張，個別廠商嘅 LRAC 下降 = external economies of scale；行業過度擴張令 LRAC 上升 = external diseconomies of scale。

p.en: Sources: nearby suppliers, a pool of skilled workers, shared information and services.
p.zh: 來源：附近有供應商、有熟練工人、資訊同服務共享。

p.en: Diseconomies: rents and wages bid up, congestion.
p.zh: 不經濟：租金同工資被推高、交通擠塞。

s.en: More garment firms nearby → cloth and buttons on Ki Lung Street close at hand → LRAC ↓.
s.zh: 附近多咗製衣廠 → 基隆街嘅布同鈕近在咫尺 → LRAC ↓。

s.en: A big pool of trained sewers → less training cost → LRAC ↓.
s.zh: 大量熟練車衣工人 → 培訓成本低 → LRAC ↓。

s.en: Too many firms → rents and wages bid up → LRAC ↑ (external diseconomies).
s.zh: 廠商太多 → 租金同工資被推高 → LRAC ↑（external diseconomies）。

q.en: Which is an external DISeconomy of scale?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係 external diseconomy of scale？

o.en: A firm hires one more worker.
A firm buys materials in bulk.
Industrial rents rise as the industry crowds into one district.
o.zh: 行業擠喺同一區，工廈租金上升。

w.en: The rise comes from the industry’s expansion, outside the firm.
w.zh: 成本上升嚟自行業擴張，喺廠商之外。

q.en: Pick the best way to tell internal from external economies of scale.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅方法分辨 internal 同 external economies of scale。

o.en: Ask whose expansion lowers the cost: the firm’s own, or the whole industry’s.
o.zh: 問：係廠商自己擴張，定係成個行業擴張令成本下降。

o.en: External means the firm sells abroad.
Internal means the cost falls inside the factory building.
o.zh: Internal 即係成本喺工廠入面下降。

o.en: It is about whose growth causes it.

q.en: (Fictional figures) TC is $500 at 10 units and $530 at 11 units. MC of the 11th unit is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）產量 10 時 TC $500，產量 11 時 TC $530。第 11 單位嘅 MC 係…

q.en: The law of diminishing marginal returns applies…
q.zh: 邊際回報遞減定律適用於…

w.en: It needs a fixed factor.
w.zh: 要有固定要素。

q.en: Many garment firms in one district lower each firm’s costs. This is…
q.zh: 好多製衣廠集中一區令每間成本下降，係…

w.en: Industry growth outside the firm.
w.zh: 廠商以外嘅行業擴張。

q.en: In your own words: why does a rise in rent change AC but not MC?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解加租會改變 AC，但唔改變 MC？

ck.en: I said rent is a fixed cost.
ck.zh: 我有講租金係固定成本。

ck.en: I said MC only counts the extra cost of one more unit.
ck.zh: 我有講 MC 只計多生產一單位嘅額外成本。

ck.en: I said AC includes fixed cost spread over output.
ck.zh: 我有講 AC 包括攤分落每單位嘅固定成本。

hook.en: (Fictional business) In 2026 Ah Ying’s cousin Ah Kei opens a phone-repair stall in a Kwun Tong industrial building on his own. A year later two friends join him as partners.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）2026 年，阿瑩表哥阿基自己一個喺觀塘工廈開手機維修檔。一年後，兩個朋友加入做合夥人。

q.en: The stall owes $200,000 that it cannot pay. Must Ah Kei pay with his own savings?
q.zh: 檔口欠咗 $200,000 還唔到。阿基要唔要用自己嘅積蓄還？

o.en: No, only the stall’s money can be used.
o.zh: 唔使，只可以用檔口嘅錢。

w.en: A sole proprietor is not separate from the business, so personal assets can be taken to pay its debts.
w.zh: 獨資東主同生意冇分開，個人財產都可以拎去還債。

d.en: Sole proprietorships and partnerships are unincorporated: no separate legal status, owners bear unlimited liability, and the business’s life follows its owners. A partnership generally has 2–20 partners.
d.zh: Sole proprietorship 同 partnership 都係 unincorporated business：冇獨立法人地位，東主／合夥人負 unlimited liability，企業壽命跟住東主。Partnership 一般 2–20 人。

p.en: Unlimited liability: owners may have to use personal assets to pay the business’s debts.
p.zh: Unlimited liability：東主可能要用個人財產還生意嘅債。

p.en: Partners share capital, skills, decisions and profits.
p.zh: 合夥人共同出資、出力、決策同分享利潤。

s.en: Year 1: one owner, keeps all profit, bears all debts → sole proprietorship.
s.zh: 第一年：一個東主，利潤全歸佢，債務全由佢負 → 獨資。

s.en: Year 2: three partners share profit and decisions; each can be liable for all the debts → partnership.
s.zh: 第二年：三個合夥人分利潤、一齊決策；每人都可能要負責全部債務 → 合夥。

s.en: If a partner leaves or dies, the partnership may have to end.
s.zh: 如果有合夥人退出或者過身，合夥可能要結束。

q.en: Which is a feature of a sole proprietorship?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係獨資企業嘅特徵？

o.en: It can sell shares to the public.

w.en: It is unincorporated, so the owner’s liability is unlimited.
w.zh: 佢係 unincorporated，東主負無限責任。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of unlimited liability.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 unlimited liability 解釋。

o.en: Owners may have to pay the business’s debts with their personal assets.
o.zh: 東主可能要用個人財產還生意嘅債。
生意嘅債可以追到個人財產。

o.en: That is closer to perpetual succession.
The business can borrow without limit.
It is about who pays debts, not borrowing.
o.zh: 講嘅係邊個還債，唔係借幾多。

hook.en: (Fictional business) The repair stall grows and becomes “Ah Kei Repairs Limited”, a private limited company with 5 shareholders, in Kwun Tong.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）維修檔越做越大，喺觀塘變成「阿基維修有限公司」，係有 5 個股東嘅私人有限公司。

q.en: If the company fails owing more than it owns, do shareholders lose their homes to pay its debts?
q.zh: 如果公司倒閉，欠債多過資產，股東要唔要賣樓還債？

o.en: No. Their liability is limited to any unpaid share capital.
o.zh: 唔使。佢哋嘅責任只限於未繳足嘅股本。

w.en: Shareholders of a limited company have limited liability.
w.zh: 有限公司股東負有限責任。

d.en: A limited company is incorporated: a separate legal entity with perpetual succession; shareholders’ liability is limited to their unpaid share capital. A private limited company has at most 50 shareholders and restricts share transfer; a public limited company has no upper limit on shareholders and can offer shares to the public.
d.zh: Limited company 係 incorporated：有獨立法人地位（separate legal entity）、perpetual succession，股東 liability 只限於未繳足嘅股本。Private ltd 最多 50 個股東、股份轉讓受限；public ltd 股東數目冇上限，可以公開招股。

p.en: Separate legal entity: the company can own property, sign contracts, sue and be sued in its own name.
p.zh: 獨立法人：公司可以用自己名義擁有財產、簽合約、告人同被告。

p.en: Perpetual succession: the company continues when shareholders change.
p.zh: Perpetual succession：股東轉咗，公司照樣存在。

s.en: The company, not Ah Kei, signs the lease for the new shop.
s.zh: 簽新舖租約嘅係公司，唔係阿基本人。

s.en: A shareholder sells her shares to her sister: the company carries on.
s.zh: 一個股東將股份賣俾家姐：公司照樣運作。

s.en: To raise money from the public, it would have to become a public limited company.
s.zh: 想向公眾集資，就要變成公眾有限公司。

q.en: Which is correct about a private limited company?
q.zh: 以下關於私人有限公司嘅描述，邊句啱？

o.en: It can invite the public to buy its shares.
It ends when a shareholder dies.
o.zh: 有股東過身公司就結束。

o.en: It has at most 50 shareholders and restricts share transfer.
o.zh: 最多 50 個股東，股份轉讓受限。

w.en: Public offers are for public limited companies; limited liability and perpetual succession apply.
w.zh: 公開招股屬公眾有限公司；有限公司有有限責任同 perpetual succession。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of “separate legal entity”.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅「獨立法人」解釋。

o.en: The company is owned by the government.
The company exists in law apart from its owners: it can own property, sue and be sued in its own name.
o.zh: 法律上公司同股東分開：可以用自己名義擁有財產、告人同被告。

o.en: The company has only one owner.
Number of owners is not the point.

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Ah Kei Repairs Limited needs $1 million to open a shop at Yue Man Square. It can issue new shares or issue bonds.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）阿基維修有限公司要 $1,000,000 喺裕民坊開舖，可以發新股，或者發債券。

q.en: Someone who buys the company’s bonds becomes its…
q.zh: 買公司債券嘅人係公司嘅…

w.en: A bond is a loan to the company.
w.zh: 債券係借錢俾公司。

d.en: A share is ownership: holders are owners, receive dividends only if there is profit, and are paid last in liquidation. A bond or debenture is a loan: holders are creditors, receive fixed interest even if the company makes a loss, and are paid before shareholders in liquidation.
d.zh: Share = 擁有權：持有人係 owner，有盈利先派 dividend，清盤時最後先攞得返錢。Bond／debenture = 借貸：持有人係 creditor，收固定 interest（蝕錢都要俾），清盤時排喺股東之前。

p.en: Issuing new shares increases equity capital; issuing bonds increases debt.
p.zh: 發新股增加 equity capital；發債增加 debt。

t.en: Two ways to raise $1 million (fictional figures)
t.zh: 兩種集資方法（虛構數字）

s.en: New shares: new owners share future profits through dividends.
s.zh: 發新股：新股東透過 dividend 分享將來利潤。

s.en: Bonds at 5%: $50,000 interest every year, even in a loss year.
s.zh: 5% 債券：每年 $50,000 利息，蝕錢嗰年都要俾。

s.en: If the company is wound up, bondholders are repaid before shareholders.
s.zh: 公司清盤，債券持有人先過股東收錢。

q.en: Which is true of bondholders?
q.zh: 以下關於債券持有人嘅描述，邊句啱？

o.en: They are paid after shareholders in liquidation.
They own part of the company.
They receive dividends only when there is profit.
They receive fixed interest even when the company makes a loss.
o.zh: 公司蝕錢都要收到固定利息。

w.en: Bondholders are creditors with fixed interest.
w.zh: 債券持有人係收固定利息嘅債權人。

q.en: Pick the best one-line difference between a share and a bond.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅一句講出股票同債券嘅分別。

o.en: A share is ownership; a bond is a loan.
o.zh: 股票係擁有權；債券係借貸。

o.en: Both make the holder an owner.
o.zh: 兩樣都令持有人變東主。

o.en: A share pays fixed interest; a bond pays dividends.
o.zh: 股票收固定利息；債券收股息。

o.en: It is the other way round.

hook.en: Hong Kong today: the Water Supplies Department, a government department, supplies water. The Airport Authority, a statutory body wholly owned by the government, runs Hong Kong International Airport.
hook.zh: 今日香港：水務署係政府部門，負責供水。機場管理局係政府全資擁有嘅法定機構，負責營運香港國際機場。

q.en: Staff of the Water Supplies Department are…
q.zh: 水務署員工係…

w.en: A government department is run directly by the government.
w.zh: 政府部門由政府直接經營。

d.en: A public enterprise is wholly owned by the government. A government department is run directly by the government and its staff are civil servants. A public corporation is set up by law, has an independent board of directors, its staff are not civil servants, and it runs its daily operations more independently.
d.zh: Public enterprise 係政府全資擁有嘅企業。Government department 由政府部門直接經營，員工係公務員；public corporation 由法例成立，有獨立董事局，員工唔係公務員，日常運作較獨立。

p.en: Both are public enterprises; the difference is how they are run.
p.zh: 兩者都係公營企業；分別在於點樣管理。

s.en: Water Supplies Department → government department → civil servants.
s.zh: 水務署 → 政府部門 → 公務員。

s.en: Airport Authority → set up by law, own board → public corporation.
s.zh: 機管局 → 法例成立、有自己董事局 → public corporation。

s.en: Both are wholly owned by the government.
s.zh: 兩者都由政府全資擁有。

q.en: Which feature belongs to a public corporation?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係 public corporation 嘅特徵？

o.en: It is set up by law and has its own board of directors.
o.zh: 由法例成立，有自己嘅董事局。

o.en: It is owned by private shareholders.

w.en: A statutory body with an independent board.
w.zh: 有獨立董事局嘅法定機構。

q.en: Pick the best description of a public enterprise.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅公營企業描述。

o.en: Any business that serves the public.
Private shops serve the public too.
A company listed on the stock exchange.
An enterprise wholly owned by the government.
o.zh: 由政府全資擁有嘅企業。

hook.en: Kwun Tong today: a private gym in an industrial building charges members a monthly fee, while a government (LCSD) sports centre in the same district charges much lower fees.
hook.zh: 今日觀塘：工廈私人健身室收會員月費；同區政府康文署體育館收費就平好多。

q.en: The LCSD sports centre charges low fees. Does running it have no opportunity cost?
q.zh: 康文署體育館收費低。營運佢係咪冇 opportunity cost？

o.en: It still has an opportunity cost.

w.en: The land, staff and money could have been used for something else.
w.zh: 土地、人手同錢都可以用喺其他地方。

d.en: Private firms mainly aim at profit maximisation. Public enterprises may put social goals first, charging low prices or nothing. But government resources still have an opportunity cost, and without the profit incentive and competition, efficiency may be lower.
d.zh: Private firms 主要目標係 profit maximisation；public enterprises 可以以社會目標為先，定低價甚至免費。但政府資源仍然有 opportunity cost，而且缺少利潤誘因同競爭，效率可能較低。

p.en: Low price ≠ low cost: someone pays, often taxpayers.
p.zh: 低價 ≠ 低成本：總有人付，通常係納稅人。

t.zh: 健身室 vs 體育館

s.en: Private gym: aims at profit; it closes if members do not cover costs.
s.zh: 私人健身室：追求利潤；會費唔夠支付成本就會執笠。

s.en: LCSD centre: aims at public use; low fees, funded partly by taxes.
s.zh: 康文署體育館：以公眾使用為目標；收費低，部分由稅款支付。

s.en: Without profit pressure, it has less incentive to cut waste.
s.zh: 冇利潤壓力，減少浪費嘅誘因較弱。

q.en: Why may public enterprises be less efficient than private firms?
q.zh: 點解公營企業效率可能低過私人公司？

o.en: They are not allowed to charge prices.
They lack the profit incentive and often face less competition.
o.zh: 缺少利潤誘因，而且通常競爭較少。

w.en: Incentive and competition are the textbook reasons.
w.zh: 誘因同競爭係課本嘅原因。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why can a public enterprise charge low prices?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解公營企業可以收低價？

o.en: It may put social goals before profit, with costs covered partly by public funds.
o.zh: 佢可以以社會目標為先，成本部分由公帑支付。

o.en: Its resources have no opportunity cost.
They do have an opportunity cost.

chain.en: Public enterprises: social goals, efficiency questions
chain.zh: 公營企業：社會目標、效率問題

q.en: Which has limited liability?
q.zh: 以下邊種有有限責任？

w.en: Only incorporated companies give limited liability.
w.zh: 只有 incorporated 公司先有有限責任。

q.en: A company issues bonds. Its…
q.zh: 公司發債，佢嘅…

w.en: Bonds are loans.
w.zh: 債券係借貸。

q.en: The Airport Authority is an example of…
q.zh: 機管局係…

w.en: A statutory body with its own board.
w.zh: 有自己董事局嘅法定機構。

q.en: In your own words: why might Ah Kei turn his partnership into a limited company?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解阿基可能將合夥生意變成有限公司？

ck.en: I mentioned limited liability.
ck.zh: 我有提到有限責任。

ck.en: I mentioned separate legal entity or perpetual succession.
ck.zh: 我有提到獨立法人或 perpetual succession。

ck.en: I mentioned raising more capital through shares.
ck.zh: 我有提到可以發股份集更多資金。

hook.en: (Fictional business) In 2026 “Yue Man Noodles”, a noodle maker in a Kwun Tong industrial building, wants to grow.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）2026 年，觀塘工廈一間麵廠「裕民麵家」想擴張。

q.en: Yue Man Noodles buys more machines and hires more workers by itself. This is…
q.zh: 裕民麵家自己買多啲機器、請多啲人。呢個係…

w.en: No other firm is involved.
w.zh: 冇第二間廠商參與。

d.en: Internal expansion: a firm grows by itself (more plant, machines, workers, branches); no other firm is involved. External expansion: the firm combines with another firm, by merger (two become one) or acquisition/takeover (buying enough shares to control the other).
d.zh: Internal expansion：廠商靠自己擴大生產規模（加廠房、加機器、加人手、開分店），冇第二間廠商參與。External expansion：同另一間廠商結合——merger（合併成一間）或 acquisition／takeover（買夠股份控制另一間）。

p.en: Merger: both firms agree to form one new firm.
p.zh: Merger：兩間公司同意合併成一間。

p.en: Acquisition: one firm gains control of another by buying its shares.
p.zh: Acquisition：一間公司買股份取得另一間嘅控制權。

s.en: Open a second factory floor → internal.
s.zh: 租多一層工廈 → 內部擴張。

s.en: Join with a rival noodle maker to form “Kwun Tong Noodles” → merger.
s.zh: 同另一間麵廠合併成「觀塘麵業」→ merger。

s.en: Buy 60% of a dumpling maker’s shares → acquisition.
s.zh: 買入一間餃子廠 60% 股份 → acquisition。

q.en: A firm buys enough shares of another firm to control it. This is…
q.zh: 一間公司買夠另一間公司嘅股份去控制佢。呢個係…

w.en: Control through share purchase is acquisition (takeover).
w.zh: 透過買股份取得控制權係收購。

q.en: Pick the best test for internal vs external expansion.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅內部／外部擴張判斷方法。

o.en: Ask whether the firm borrows money.
Ask whether another firm is combined with it.
o.zh: 問：有冇同另一間廠商結合。

o.en: Ask whether the expansion happens inside the building.
o.zh: 問：擴張係咪喺大廈入面發生。

hook.en: (Fictional business) Yue Man Noodles merges with another noodle maker in Kwun Tong.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）裕民麵家同觀塘另一間麵廠合併。

q.en: Both firms make noodles. Which type of expansion is this?
q.zh: 兩間都係整麵。呢個係邊種擴張？

w.en: Same product, same stage of production.
w.zh: 同一產品、同一生產階段。

d.en: Horizontal expansion: expanding into the same product, or the same stage of production. It can be internal (opening more branches of the same kind) or external (merging with or acquiring a rival).
d.zh: Horizontal expansion：擴張到生產同一種產品、或者處於同一生產階段嘅業務。可以係 internal（自己開多幾間同類分店）或 external（同同行合併／收購）。

p.en: External horizontal expansion also removes a competitor.
p.zh: External horizontal expansion 仲可以減少競爭對手。

s.en: Open three more noodle shops → internal horizontal.
s.zh: 開多三間麵舖 → internal horizontal。

s.en: Buy a rival noodle maker → external horizontal.
s.zh: 收購對手麵廠 → external horizontal。

s.en: After the merger there is one fewer noodle maker competing.
s.zh: 合併之後少咗一間麵廠競爭。

q.en: Which is horizontal expansion?
q.zh: 以下邊個係橫向擴張？

o.en: A bakery buys a shipping company.
A bakery chain acquires another bakery chain.
o.zh: 一間餅店集團收購另一間餅店集團。

o.en: A bakery opens a café selling coffee.
A bakery buys a flour mill.

w.en: Same product, same stage.
w.zh: 同一產品、同一階段。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of horizontal expansion.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅橫向擴張解釋。

o.en: Growing into the same product or the same stage of production.
o.zh: 擴張到同一產品或同一生產階段。

o.en: Growing into an earlier stage of production.

o.zh: 擴張到完全無關嘅行業。

hook.en: (Fictional business) Yue Man Noodles buys a flour mill, then opens its own noodle shops at Yue Man Square.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）裕民麵家收購咗一間麵粉廠，之後喺裕民坊開自己嘅麵舖。

q.en: Buying the flour mill (its supplier) is which kind of vertical expansion?
q.zh: 收購麵粉廠（佢嘅供應商）係邊種縱向擴張？

w.en: Moving towards the earlier (upstream) stage is backward.
w.zh: 擴去較早（上游）階段係向後。

d.en: Vertical expansion: expanding into an earlier or later stage of production of the same product. Backward: into the upstream stage, to secure a stable supply of raw materials. Forward: into the downstream stage, to secure sales outlets.
d.zh: Vertical expansion：擴張到同一產品嘅較早或較後生產階段。Backward（向後）= 擴去上游，確保原料供應穩定；forward（向前）= 擴去下游，確保產品有銷售出路。

p.en: Flour → noodles → noodle shop: one product chain.
p.zh: 麵粉 → 麵 → 麵舖：同一條產品鏈。

s.en: Flour mill (earlier stage) ← backward.
s.zh: 麵粉廠（較早階段）← 向後。

s.en: Noodle factory (Yue Man Noodles).
s.zh: 麵廠（裕民麵家）。

s.en: Noodle shops (later stage) → forward.
s.zh: 麵舖（較後階段）→ 向前。

q.en: A noodle factory opens its own retail shops. This is…
q.zh: 麵廠開自己嘅零售舖。呢個係…

w.en: Retail is the later (downstream) stage.
w.zh: 零售係較後（下游）階段。

q.en: Pick the best motive for backward vertical expansion.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅向後縱向擴張動機。

o.en: To spread risk across unrelated industries.
o.zh: 將風險分散到無關行業。

o.en: To secure a stable supply of raw materials.

hook.en: (Fictional business) Yue Man Noodles starts making soy sauce, and later buys a travel agency.
hook.zh: （虛構生意）裕民麵家開始整豉油，之後再收購一間旅行社。

q.en: Buying a travel agency, unrelated to noodles, is…
q.zh: 收購同麵無關嘅旅行社，係…

w.en: A completely unrelated industry → conglomerate.
w.zh: 完全無關嘅行業 → 綜合擴張。

d.en: Lateral expansion: expanding into related products that do not compete directly. Conglomerate expansion: expanding into completely unrelated industries. Both diversify and spread risk.
d.zh: Lateral expansion：擴張到有關連但唔直接競爭嘅產品。Conglomerate expansion：擴張到完全唔相關嘅行業。兩者都可以 diversify，分散風險。

p.en: Soy sauce is related to noodles (same kitchens, same customers) but does not compete with noodles.
p.zh: 豉油同麵有關連（同一班客、同一類廚房），但唔同麵競爭。

s.en: Making soy sauce → related, not competing → lateral.
s.zh: 整豉油 → 有關但唔競爭 → lateral。

s.en: Buying a travel agency → unrelated → conglomerate.
s.zh: 收購旅行社 → 無關 → conglomerate。

s.en: If noodle sales fall, the other businesses can still earn.
s.zh: 如果麵嘅生意差，其他業務仍然有收入。

q.en: A sportswear maker starts selling sports drinks. This is most likely…
q.zh: 運動服裝廠開始賣運動飲品。呢個最可能係…

w.en: Related customers, not a competing product.
w.zh: 相關客群，唔係競爭產品。

q.en: Pick the shared motive of lateral and conglomerate expansion.
q.zh: 揀 lateral 同 conglomerate expansion 嘅共同動機。

o.en: Not all eggs in one basket.
o.zh: 唔好將所有雞蛋放落同一個籃。
