hook.en: (Fictional business) By 2026 Yue Man Noodles has grown in every direction. Why did it bother?
hook.zh: （虛構生意）到 2026 年，裕民麵家已經向各個方向擴張。點解要咁做？

q.en: Which motive applies to ALL types of expansion?
q.zh: 以下邊個動機適用於所有擴張？

w.en: A bigger firm can enjoy lower LRAC whatever direction it grows.
w.zh: 無論向邊個方向擴張，大咗都可以令 LRAC 下降。

d.en: Common motives: economies of scale, using resources more fully, a stronger brand. Horizontal (external) only: reducing competition. Vertical backward: secure raw materials; forward: secure sales outlets. Lateral and conglomerate: spread risk.
d.zh: 共通動機：享受 economies of scale、更有效運用資源、擴大品牌效益。Horizontal（external）獨有：減少競爭。Vertical backward：保障原料供應；forward：保障銷售出路。Lateral／conglomerate：分散風險。

p.en: Match each motive to the type of expansion that it fits.
p.zh: 將每個動機配對返適合嘅擴張類型。

s.en: Bought a rival noodle maker → fewer competitors (horizontal).
s.zh: 收購對手麵廠 → 少咗競爭（橫向）。

s.en: Bought the flour mill → steady flour supply (backward vertical).
s.zh: 收購麵粉廠 → 麵粉供應穩定（向後縱向）。

s.en: Bought a travel agency → spread risk (conglomerate).
s.zh: 收購旅行社 → 分散風險（綜合）。

q.en: Which motive is UNIQUE to external horizontal expansion?
q.zh: 以下邊個動機係外部橫向擴張獨有？

w.en: Only combining with a rival removes a competitor.
w.zh: 只有同對手結合先會減少競爭對手。

q.en: Pick the best match.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅配對。

o.zh: 綜合擴張 → 減少競爭。

o.en: Unrelated industries do not reduce competition.
o.zh: 無關行業唔會減少競爭。
向後縱向擴張 → 分散風險。

o.en: Forward vertical expansion → secure sales outlets.
o.zh: 向前縱向擴張 → 確保銷售出路。

chain.zh: 方向：橫向、縱向、側向、綜合

chain.en: Each direction has its own motive
chain.zh: 每個方向有自己嘅動機
全部都可以享受規模經濟

q.en: A shoe factory buys a leather tannery. This is…
q.zh: 鞋廠收購皮革廠。呢個係…

w.en: The tannery is upstream.
w.zh: 皮革廠係上游。

q.en: Two supermarket chains merge. This is…
q.zh: 兩間超市集團合併。呢個係…

w.en: Same stage, same product.
w.zh: 同一階段、同一產品。

q.en: A bank buys a fish farm. The main motive is most likely…
q.zh: 銀行收購魚場，最可能嘅動機係…

w.en: Unrelated industry → conglomerate.
w.zh: 無關行業 → 綜合擴張。

q.en: In your own words: how would you decide whether an expansion is horizontal or vertical?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：你點樣分辨一次擴張係橫向定縱向？

ck.en: I asked whether the other business makes the same product at the same stage.
ck.zh: 我有問對方係咪同一產品、同一生產階段。

ck.en: I said vertical means an earlier or later stage of the same product.
ck.zh: 我有講縱向即係同一產品嘅較早或較後階段。

ck.en: I gave an example.
ck.zh: 我有舉例子。

hook.en: Mong Kok, Tung Choi Street North (Goldfish Street): many shops sell the same common goldfish side by side.
hook.zh: 旺角通菜街北段（金魚街）：好多間舖並排賣同款嘅普通金魚。

q.en: One goldfish shop raises its price far above the others for the same common fish. What happens?
q.zh: 一間金魚舖將同款普通金魚嘅價錢加到遠高過其他舖。會點？

w.en: Identical goods and full information: buyers switch, so each seller must take the market price.
w.zh: 貨品一樣、資訊充足：買家會轉舖，所以每個賣家只可以接受市場價格。

d.en: Perfect competition: many small sellers, homogeneous products, free entry and exit, perfect market information. Every seller is a price taker. It does not exist in the real world; some markets come close.
d.zh: Perfect competition：好多細小賣家、產品同質（homogeneous）、自由進出、市場資訊完全；每個賣家都係 price taker。現實世界唔存在，只有近似嘅市場。

p.en: Price taker: a seller who can only accept the market price.
p.zh: Price taker：只可以接受市場價格嘅賣家。

t.zh: 點解金魚街接近完全競爭

s.en: Many shops, each small → no single shop moves the price.
s.zh: 舖多、每間細 → 冇一間可以影響價格。

s.en: Common goldfish look the same → homogeneous.
s.zh: 普通金魚睇落一樣 → 同質。

s.en: Prices are easy to compare walking down the street → good information.
s.zh: 行一轉就比較到價 → 資訊充足。

q.en: Which is NOT a feature of perfect competition?
q.zh: 以下邊樣唔係完全競爭嘅特徵？

w.en: Products are homogeneous in perfect competition.
w.zh: 完全競爭嘅產品係同質。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is a perfectly competitive seller a price taker?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解完全競爭嘅賣家係 price taker？

o.en: With identical products and many sellers, buyers switch if it charges more.
o.zh: 產品一樣、賣家又多，佢加價買家就會轉舖。

o.en: So it must accept the market price.
o.zh: 所以只可以接受市場價。

hook.en: Mong Kok, Tung Choi Street (the Ladies’ Market): hundreds of stalls sell phone cases, T-shirts and bags, each slightly different in design, location or service.
hook.zh: 旺角通菜街（女人街）：幾百個檔口賣手機殼、T 恤同手袋，款式、位置或服務各有少少唔同。

q.en: A Ladies’ Market stall raises its price a little. What most likely happens?
q.zh: 女人街一個檔口加少少價。最可能會點？

o.en: It loses some customers, but not all.
o.zh: 流失部分客，但唔係全部。

w.en: Its products are a little different, so some buyers stay: it is a price searcher.
w.zh: 產品有少少唔同，所以有啲客會留低：佢係 price searcher。

d.en: Monopolistic competition: many sellers, differentiated products, low entry barriers, and a lot of non-price competition (packaging, service, location, advertising). Each seller is a price searcher with a little pricing power.
d.zh: Monopolistic competition：好多賣家、產品有差異（differentiated）、入行障礙低、大量 non-price competition（包裝、服務、地點、廣告）；每個賣家係有少少定價能力嘅 price searcher。

p.en: Differentiation gives a little pricing power.
p.zh: 產品差異帶嚟少少定價能力。

s.en: Many stalls → many sellers.
s.zh: 檔口多 → 賣家多。

s.en: Different designs, friendlier owners, corner spots → differentiated products.
s.zh: 款式唔同、老闆親切、轉角位 → 產品有差異。

s.en: A new stall can open fairly easily → low entry barriers.
s.zh: 開新檔相對容易 → 入行障礙低。

q.en: Which is non-price competition?
q.zh: 以下邊個係 non-price competition？

o.en: A stall copies its neighbour’s price.
A stall cuts its price by $10.
A stall offers free phone-case customisation.
o.zh: 檔口免費幫你訂造手機殼。

w.en: Competing with service rather than price.
w.zh: 用服務而唔係價格競爭。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why can a monopolistically competitive seller set its own price a little?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解壟斷性競爭嘅賣家有少少定價能力？

o.en: Its product is a little different, so not all buyers leave when it raises the price.
o.zh: 產品有少少唔同，加價唔會令所有客走晒。

hook.en: Mong Kok, Fa Yuen Street (Sneakers Street): dozens of shops, but most shoes on the shelves come from a few big international sports brands.
hook.zh: 旺角花園街（波鞋街）：有幾十間舖，但貨架上大部分波鞋都嚟自幾個國際大品牌。

q.en: When one big brand cuts its price, what do the others most likely do?
q.zh: 一個大品牌減價，其他大品牌最可能點做？

o.en: Watch and react, because their sales are affected.
o.zh: 留意並作出反應，因為佢哋嘅銷量受影響。

w.en: A few dominant sellers are interdependent.
w.zh: 少數主導賣家互相依賴。

d.en: Oligopoly: a few dominant sellers (small sellers may exist), high entry barriers, interdependent decisions, prices tend to be rigid, and non-price competition is common.
d.zh: Oligopoly：少數幾個佔主導地位（dominant）嘅賣家（細賣家可以存在）、入行障礙高、決策互相依賴（interdependence）、價格傾向僵硬、常用 non-price competition。

p.en: Interdependence: each firm’s best move depends on what the others do.
p.zh: 互相依賴：每間公司點做最好，要睇其他公司點做。

p.en: Price wars hurt everyone, so firms compete with advertising and design.
p.zh: 價格戰對大家都唔好，所以多用廣告同設計競爭。

s.en: A few brands dominate shelves; small brands also exist → oligopoly.
s.zh: 幾個品牌主導貨架，亦有細品牌 → 寡頭壟斷。

s.en: Huge advertising and brand loyalty → high entry barriers.
s.zh: 大量廣告同品牌忠誠 → 入行障礙高。

s.en: They launch new designs and sign star athletes instead of cutting prices → non-price competition.
s.zh: 佢哋推新款、簽球星，而唔係減價 → 非價格競爭。

q.en: Which is a feature of oligopoly?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係寡頭壟斷嘅特徵？

o.en: Every firm is a price taker.
o.zh: 每間廠商都係 price taker。

w.en: Interdependence is the hallmark of oligopoly.
w.zh: 互相依賴係寡頭壟斷最大特徵。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why do oligopoly prices tend to be rigid?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解寡頭壟斷嘅價格傾向僵硬？

o.en: A price cut may start a price war, so firms prefer non-price competition.
o.zh: 減價可能觸發價格戰，所以廠商寧願用非價格競爭。

hook.en: Hong Kong today: the Water Supplies Department is the only supplier of piped fresh water to homes. A drug company with a patent is the only legal seller of that new medicine.
hook.zh: 今日香港：水務署係住宅食水嘅唯一供應者。持有專利嘅藥廠係嗰隻新藥唯一合法嘅賣家。

q.en: A monopolist raises its price. Does its quantity demanded fall?
q.zh: 壟斷者加價，佢嘅 quantity demanded 會唔會跌？

o.en: Yes. It still faces a downward-sloping demand curve.
o.zh: 會。佢仍然面對向下傾斜嘅 demand curve。

o.en: No. A monopolist can charge any price without losing sales.
o.zh: 唔會。壟斷者幾貴都唔會少賣。

w.en: Buyers can buy less or go without, even with no close substitute.
w.zh: 就算冇相近替代品，買家都可以少買或者唔買。

d.en: Monopoly: a single seller, no close substitutes, very high entry barriers. Sources: government franchise or statutory right, natural monopoly, patent or copyright, control of a key resource, collusion or merger. A monopolist still faces a downward-sloping demand curve.
d.zh: Monopoly：唯一賣家、冇相近替代品、入行障礙極高。來源：政府專營／法定授權、franchise、natural monopoly、patent／copyright、獨佔關鍵資源、合謀或合併。Monopolist 仍然面對向下傾斜嘅 demand curve。

p.en: Natural monopoly: one large firm can supply the market at a lower average cost than several firms (e.g. a water pipe network).
p.zh: Natural monopoly：一間大公司供應全個市場嘅平均成本低過幾間公司（例如水管網絡）。

s.en: Water network: building a second pipe network would be very costly → natural monopoly, run by government.
s.zh: 水管網絡：起第二套水管網成本極高 → natural monopoly，由政府經營。

s.en: Patent: the law gives the inventor the sole right to sell for a period.
s.zh: 專利：法例俾發明者一段時間嘅獨家銷售權。

s.en: Even so, if prices rise people use less: demand still slopes down.
s.zh: 即使係咁，加價大家都會少用：demand 仍然向下傾斜。

q.en: Which is a source of monopoly power?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係壟斷力嘅來源？

o.en: A patent on a new product
Many sellers of the same product

w.en: A patent legally blocks entry.
w.zh: 專利依法阻止其他人入行。

q.en: Pick the correct statement about a monopolist.
q.zh: 揀關於壟斷者嘅正確說法。

o.en: It is a price searcher facing a downward-sloping demand curve.
o.zh: 佢係 price searcher，面對向下傾斜嘅 demand curve。

o.en: It can sell any quantity at any price.
o.zh: 佢可以用任何價錢賣任何數量。

o.en: A monopolist can still make losses.

t.zh: 價格接受者同價格搜尋者

hook.en: (Fictional figures) In 2026 at the Ladies’ Market, a stall raises a T-shirt from $50 to $60 and still sells some. On Goldfish Street, a shop asks $10 for a common goldfish others sell at $5 and sells none.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年女人街，一個檔將 T 恤由 $50 加到 $60，仍然賣到一啲。金魚街一間舖將普通金魚定 $10，其他舖 $5，結果一條都賣唔出。

q.en: Which seller is a price searcher?
q.zh: 邊個賣家係 price searcher？

w.en: It loses some, not all, customers when it raises the price.
w.zh: 加價流失部分而唔係全部顧客。

d.en: A price taker can only accept the market price. A price searcher faces a downward-sloping demand curve: raising the price loses some, but not all, customers. Price competition means cutting prices; non-price competition uses product, service, location and promotion.
d.zh: Price taker 只可以接受市場價格；price searcher 面對向下傾斜嘅 demand curve，加價會流失部分（唔係全部）顧客。Price competition 靠減價；non-price competition 靠產品、服務、地點同宣傳。

p.en: Price searchers are found in monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly.
p.zh: Price searcher 見於壟斷性競爭、寡頭壟斷同壟斷。

s.en: Goldfish: identical product → asks above $5, sells nothing → price taker.
s.zh: 金魚：產品一樣 → 定高過 $5 就賣唔出 → price taker。

s.en: T-shirt: own design → at $60 sells fewer, but still sells → price searcher.
s.zh: T 恤：自家設計 → $60 賣少咗，但仍然賣到 → price searcher。

s.en: To sell more, the T-shirt stall can cut price, or add free name printing.
s.zh: 想賣多啲，T 恤檔可以減價，或者免費印名。

q.en: Which is price competition?
q.zh: 以下邊個係 price competition？

o.en: A stall gives free gift wrapping.
A stall offers “buy two, get $20 off”.
A stall moves to a corner spot.
A stall puts up a bigger sign.

w.en: A lower effective price is price competition.
w.zh: 實際價錢減咗就係價格競爭。

q.en: Pick the best test for a price searcher.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 price searcher 判斷方法。

o.en: If it raises its price, it loses some but not all customers.
o.zh: 加價會流失部分但唔係全部顧客。

o.en: It can charge any price without losing customers.
o.zh: 佢點定價都唔會流失顧客。

o.en: It searches for the lowest cost supplier.
The name refers to setting price.

chain.zh: 壟斷性競爭：多賣家、有差異
寡頭壟斷：少數主導、互相依賴

chain.en: More market power → more of a price searcher
chain.zh: 市場力量越大 → 越似 price searcher

q.en: Many stalls sell slightly different phone cases. This market is closest to…
q.zh: 好多檔口賣款式略有不同嘅手機殼，最接近…

w.en: Many sellers, differentiated products.
w.zh: 多賣家、產品有差異。

q.en: Firms watch each other’s every price move. This shows…
q.zh: 廠商密切留意對方每次定價，呢個顯示…

w.en: Interdependence.
w.zh: 互相依賴。

q.en: A monopolist raises its price. Quantity demanded…
q.zh: 壟斷者加價，quantity demanded…

w.en: Demand slopes down.
w.zh: Demand 向下傾斜。

q.en: In your own words: what decides whether a seller is a price taker or a price searcher?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：咩決定一個賣家係 price taker 定 price searcher？

ck.en: I mentioned how similar its product is to others’.
ck.zh: 我有提到產品同其他人有幾相似。

ck.en: I mentioned the number of sellers or market power.
ck.zh: 我有提到賣家數目或市場力量。

ck.en: I said what happens to customers when it raises its price.
ck.zh: 我有講加價時顧客會點。

hook.en: (Fictional businesses) In 2026, inside a Mong Kok computer centre, one shop sells graphics cards for the highest profit, while a charity next door refurbishes old laptops for students at cost.
hook.zh: （虛構商舖）2026 年，旺角電腦中心入面，一間舖賣顯示卡追求最大利潤；隔籬一間慈善機構以成本價翻新舊手提電腦俾學生。

q.en: What do economists usually assume a firm aims at?
q.zh: 經濟學一般假設廠商嘅目標係乜？

w.en: The standard assumption is profit maximisation.
w.zh: 標準假設係利潤最大化。

d.en: Firms are generally assumed to pursue profit maximisation. Other objectives include market share, corporate social responsibility, non-profit provision and survival.
d.zh: 一般假設廠商追求 profit maximisation；其他目標包括 market share、corporate social responsibility、non-profit provision 同 survival。

p.en: A new shop in a slow month may just aim to survive.
p.zh: 新開嘅舖喺淡月可能只求 survival。

s.en: Graphics-card shop → profit maximisation.
s.zh: 顯示卡舖 → 利潤最大化。

s.en: Phone shop selling below rivals to win buyers → market share.
s.zh: 手機舖平過對手搶客 → 市場佔有率。

s.en: Charity laptop shop → non-profit provision. A new shop in a bad month → survival.
s.zh: 慈善手提電腦舖 → 非牟利提供。淡月新舖 → 求存。

q.en: A firm donates part of its profit to recycle old computers. Which objective is this?
q.zh: 公司將部分利潤捐出回收舊電腦，係邊個目標？

o.zh: Corporate social responsibility 企業社會責任

w.en: Taking care of society beyond profit is CSR.
w.zh: 利潤以外照顧社會係 CSR。

q.en: Pick the best statement.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅說法。

o.zh: 佢哋仍然用緊稀缺資源。

o.en: All firms aim only at survival.

o.zh: 求存只係其中一個目標。

o.en: Firms are usually assumed to maximise profit, but real firms may have other objectives.
o.zh: 一般假設廠商追求最大利潤，但現實廠商可以有其他目標。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) A Mong Kok computer-centre shop sells keyboards. At $50 it sells 10 a day; at $40, 15; at $30, 18. Its TC is $300, $450 and $520 for those quantities.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）旺角電腦中心一間舖賣鍵盤。$50 一日賣 10 個；$40 賣 15 個；$30 賣 18 個。對應嘅 TC 係 $300、$450、$520。

q.en: At which price is total revenue (TR) the highest?
q.zh: 邊個價錢嘅 total revenue（TR）最高？

w.en: TR: $500, $600, $540. $40 gives the most.

d.en: TR = P × Q. Profit = TR − TC. Maximum TR is not the same as maximum profit.
d.zh: TR = P × Q；profit = TR − TC。TR 最大唔等於 profit 最大。

p.en: Selling more raises revenue but also raises cost.
p.zh: 賣多啲收入多咗，但成本都多咗。

s.en: $30: TR $540 − TC $520 = $20. Profit is highest at $50, not at the highest-TR price.
s.zh: $30：TR $540 − TC $520 = $20。利潤最高係 $50，唔係 TR 最高嗰個價。

q.en: (Fictional figures) A shop sells 20 mice at $25 each, and TC is $380. Its profit is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）一間舖以每隻 $25 賣出 20 隻滑鼠，TC 係 $380。佢嘅利潤係…

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why can maximum TR differ from maximum profit?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解 TR 最大唔一定係利潤最大？

o.zh: 因為 TR 包括成本。

o.en: Selling more adds revenue but also adds cost; profit depends on both.
o.zh: 賣多啲收入多咗但成本都多咗，利潤要睇兩者。
呢度價格明顯影響數量。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) A Mong Kok workshop makes phone-charging cables in a highly competitive market, so it sells each cable at the market price of $10. The MC of the 1st to 5th cable is $4, $6, $9, $10, $13.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）旺角一間工場喺高度競爭嘅市場整手機充電線，每條只可以賣市價 $10。第 1 至第 5 條嘅 MC 係 $4、$6、$9、$10、$13。

q.en: Should the workshop make the 5th cable?
q.zh: 應唔應該整第 5 條？

o.en: Yes, more output is always better.

w.en: That unit would reduce profit by $3.
w.zh: 嗰一件會令利潤少 $3。

d.en: For a price taker in perfect competition, MR = P. Produce one more unit as long as MR ≥ MC; profit is maximised at the output where MR = MC (P = MC).
d.zh: Perfect competition 入面，price taker 嘅 MR = P。只要 MR ≥ MC 就多生產一單位；profit 最大化嘅產量喺 MR = MC（即 P = MC）。

p.en: MR: the extra revenue from one more unit. MC: the extra cost.
p.zh: MR：多賣一單位增加嘅收入。MC：增加嘅成本。

s.en: 4th: MR 10 = MC 10 → +0, profit unchanged.
s.zh: 第 4 件：MR 10 = MC 10 → +0，利潤不變。

s.en: 5th: 10 < 13 → −3. Best output: 4 units, where MR = MC.
s.zh: 第 5 件：10 < 13 → −3。最佳產量：4 件，即 MR = MC。

q.en: (Fictional figures) Price is $8. MC of units 1–4: $3, $5, $8, $11. What output maximises profit?
q.zh: （虛構數字）價格 $8。第 1–4 件嘅 MC：$3、$5、$8、$11。邊個產量令利潤最大？

w.en: Produce while MR ≥ MC: the 3rd unit has MR = MC = $8; the 4th would lose $3.
w.zh: MR ≥ MC 就生產：第 3 件 MR = MC = $8；第 4 件會蝕 $3。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of the MR = MC rule.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 MR = MC 法則解釋。

o.en: Units with MC > MR lower profit.
o.zh: MC > MR 嘅單位會減少利潤。
喺 AC 最低嗰點生產。

o.en: Keep producing while each extra unit adds at least as much revenue as cost; stop where MR = MC.
o.zh: 只要每多一單位增加嘅收入唔少過成本就繼續生產；去到 MR = MC 就停。

t.en: Fixed cost and the best output

hook.en: (Fictional figures) The Mong Kok cable workshop’s rent rises by $100 a day.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）旺角充電線工場每日租金加咗 $100。

q.en: Should the workshop change its profit-maximising output?
q.zh: 工場應唔應該改變利潤最大化嘅產量？

o.en: No. Rent is fixed cost and does not change MC.
o.zh: 唔應該。租金係固定成本，唔影響 MC。

o.en: Yes. It should produce more to cover the rent.
o.zh: 應該。要生產多啲去抵消租金。

w.en: MR and MC are unchanged, so MR = MC at the same output.
w.zh: MR 同 MC 冇變，MR = MC 仍然喺同一產量。

d.en: A change in fixed cost changes total profit, but not the profit-maximising output, because fixed cost does not affect MC.
d.zh: Fixed cost 改變會改變總 profit，但唔會改變 profit 最大化嘅產量，因為 fixed cost 唔影響 MC。

p.en: Every output level’s profit falls by the same amount.
p.zh: 每個產量嘅利潤都同樣減少。

s.en: Before: best output 4 cables, daily profit $200.
s.zh: 之前：最佳產量 4 條，每日利潤 $200。

s.en: After: every output’s profit is $100 lower; at 4 cables it is $100.
s.zh: 之後：每個產量嘅利潤都少咗 $100；4 條時利潤係 $100。

s.en: The ranking of outputs is unchanged, so 4 cables is still best.
s.zh: 產量之間嘅排名冇變，4 條仍然最好。

q.en: Which change WOULD change the profit-maximising output?
q.zh: 以下邊個改變會改變利潤最大化產量？

o.en: A rise in the cost of copper used in each cable
o.zh: 每條線用嘅銅成本上升

o.en: A rise in insurance paid yearly
A rise in the shop’s licence fee

w.en: Copper is a variable cost, so MC rises.
w.zh: 銅係可變成本，所以 MC 上升。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does a rise in rent not change the best output?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解加租唔會改變最佳產量？

o.en: Rent does not change MC, so MR = MC happens at the same output.
o.zh: 租金唔影響 MC，所以 MR = MC 仍然喺同一產量。

o.en: Because rent is paid by the landlord.

hook.en: (Fictional figures) The Mong Kok cable workshop’s MC for the 1st to 3rd cable is $4, $6, $9, and its daily TFC is $20.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）旺角充電線工場第 1 至第 3 條嘅 MC 係 $4、$6、$9，每日 TFC 係 $20。

q.en: What is TVC at 3 cables?
q.zh: 產量 3 條時 TVC 係幾多？

d.en: TVC = the sum of the MC of every unit. TC = TFC + TVC. AC = TC ÷ Q. From an MC column you can rebuild TVC, TC and profit.
d.zh: TVC = 每一單位 MC 嘅總和；TC = TFC + TVC；AC = TC ÷ Q。由 MC 欄可以砌返 TVC、TC 同 profit。

p.en: MC never includes fixed cost.
p.zh: MC 永遠唔包括固定成本。

q.en: (Fictional figures) MC of units 1–4: $5, $7, $9, $11; TFC = $30. TC at 4 units is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）第 1–4 件 MC：$5、$7、$9、$11；TFC = $30。產量 4 件時 TC 係…

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does adding up MC give TVC, not TC?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解將 MC 加埋得到 TVC 而唔係 TC？

o.en: TVC is the MC of the last unit.
o.zh: TVC 係最後一單位嘅 MC。

o.en: TVC is the sum, not one MC.
o.zh: TVC 係總和，唔係一個 MC。

o.en: Each MC is the extra variable cost of one unit; fixed cost is never in MC.
o.zh: 每個 MC 係一單位嘅額外可變成本；MC 從來唔包括固定成本。
加返 TFC 先係 TC。

chain.zh: 目標：通常係利潤最大化

chain.en: Fixed cost changes profit, not the best output
chain.zh: 固定成本改變利潤，唔改變最佳產量

q.en: (Fictional figures) P = $12. MC: $6, $9, $12, $15. Best output is…

w.en: MR = MC at the 3rd unit.
w.zh: 第 3 件 MR = MC。

q.en: Rent doubles. The profit-maximising output…
q.zh: 租金加倍，利潤最大化產量…

w.en: Rent is fixed cost.
w.zh: 租金係固定成本。

q.en: Maximum TR means…
q.zh: TR 最大即係…

w.en: Costs matter too.
w.zh: 成本都要計。

q.en: In your own words: why does a firm stop producing where MR = MC?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解廠商去到 MR = MC 就停止生產？

ck.en: I said units with MR > MC add to profit.
ck.zh: 我有講 MR > MC 嘅單位會增加利潤。

ck.en: I said units with MC > MR reduce profit.
ck.zh: 我有講 MC > MR 嘅單位會減少利潤。

ck.en: I said MR is the price for a price taker.
ck.zh: 我有講 price taker 嘅 MR 就係價格。

t.en: Demand and the law of demand

hook.en: (Fictional figures) In 2026 Ah Ying would love a $3,000 phone she sees on Sai Yeung Choi Street South, but she has only $500.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年，阿瑩好想要西洋菜南街一部 $3,000 嘅手機，但佢得 $500。

q.en: Is her wish part of the demand for that phone?
q.zh: 佢嘅願望算唔算係嗰部手機嘅 demand？

o.en: No, it is not backed by ability to pay.

w.en: Demand needs both willingness and ability to pay.
w.zh: Demand 要同時有意願同能力購買。

d.en: Demand: the quantities buyers are willing and able to buy at different prices over a period of time (wants backed by purchasing power; a plan). A change in the good’s own price only moves along the same demand curve: a change in quantity demanded. Market demand is the horizontal summation of individual demands.
d.zh: Demand：喺唔同價格下，買家喺一段時間內願意而且有能力購買嘅數量（有購買力支持嘅 wants，係一個計劃）。價格改變只係沿住同一條 demand curve 改變 quantity demanded。Market demand = 個人 demand 嘅 horizontal summation（將數量相加）。

p.en: Law of demand: ceteris paribus, the higher the price, the smaller the quantity demanded.
p.zh: Law of demand：ceteris paribus，價格越高，quantity demanded 越細。

t.en: Market demand for bubble tea (fictional figures)
t.zh: 珍珠奶茶嘅市場需求（虛構數字）

s.en: At $30: Ah Ying plans 3 cups a week, her friend 2.
s.zh: $30：阿瑩每星期計劃買 3 杯，朋友 2 杯。

s.en: Market demand at $30 = 3 + 2 = 5 cups (add quantities, not prices).
s.zh: $30 嘅市場需求 = 3 + 2 = 5 杯（加數量，唔係加價錢）。

s.en: At $25 they plan 4 + 3 = 7: price down, quantity demanded up.
s.zh: $25 時計劃買 4 + 3 = 7 杯：價跌，quantity demanded 上升。

q.en: The price of bubble tea falls and people buy more. This is…
q.zh: 珍珠奶茶減價，大家買多咗。呢個係…

o.en: a shift of the demand curve

w.en: Own-price change → movement along the curve.
w.zh: 自身價格改變 → 沿線移動。

q.en: Pick the best definition of demand.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 demand 定義。

o.en: The quantities buyers are willing and able to buy at different prices over a period.
o.zh: 喺一段時間內，買家喺唔同價格下願意而且有能力購買嘅數量。

o.en: Willing and able, at each price.
o.zh: 願意兼有能力，每個價格。

o.en: Demand is a plan over a range of prices.
o.zh: Demand 係唔同價格下嘅計劃。

o.en: Wants without ability to pay are not demand.
o.zh: 冇購買力嘅 wants 唔係 demand。

t.en: Supply and the law of supply

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Before Lunar New Year 2026, florists on Flower Market Road in Mong Kok bring out more peach blossom as prices rise.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年農曆新年前，旺角花墟道嘅花店見桃花價錢上升，就拎多啲出嚟賣。

q.en: Prices of peach blossom rise. Ceteris paribus, florists offer…
q.zh: 桃花價錢上升，ceteris paribus，花店會賣…

w.en: Law of supply: higher price, larger quantity supplied.
w.zh: Law of supply：價高，quantity supplied 大。

d.en: Supply: the quantities sellers are willing and able to sell at different prices over a period of time. Law of supply: ceteris paribus, the higher the price, the larger the quantity supplied. Market supply is also a horizontal summation.
d.zh: Supply：喺唔同價格下，賣家喺一段時間內願意而且有能力出售嘅數量。Law of supply：ceteris paribus，價格越高，quantity supplied 越大。Market supply 同樣係 horizontal summation。

p.en: A change in the good’s own price → a change in quantity supplied (movement along the supply curve).
p.zh: 自身價格改變 → quantity supplied 改變（沿 supply curve 移動）。

s.en: At $200 a branch: shop A offers 20, shop B 30 → market 50.
s.zh: 每枝 $200：A 店賣 20 枝，B 店 30 枝 → 市場 50 枝。

s.en: At $300: A offers 30, B 40 → market 70.
s.zh: 每枝 $300：A 店 30 枝，B 店 40 枝 → 市場 70 枝。

s.en: Higher price → larger quantity supplied: a movement along the supply curve.
s.zh: 價高 → quantity supplied 大：沿 supply curve 移動。

q.en: Market supply is found by…
q.zh: Market supply 係點樣得出？

o.en: adding the prices of all sellers
o.zh: 將所有賣家嘅價格相加

o.en: adding the quantities each seller offers at each price
o.zh: 將每個價格下各賣家嘅數量相加

w.en: Horizontal summation adds quantities at each price.
w.zh: Horizontal summation 係喺每個價格下將數量相加。

q.en: Pick the best statement of the law of supply.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 law of supply 說法。

o.en: That mixes up cause and effect.
Sellers always sell everything they have.
Supply is a plan at each price.
o.zh: Supply 係每個價格下嘅計劃。

o.en: Ceteris paribus, the higher the price, the larger the quantity supplied.
o.zh: Ceteris paribus，價格越高，quantity supplied 越大。

o.en: Price and quantity supplied move together.
o.zh: 價格同 quantity supplied 同方向。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Goldfish Street, 2026: at $8 a fish, shops want to sell 300 a day and buyers want to buy 300.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年金魚街：每條 $8，金魚舖每日想賣 300 條，買家想買 300 條。

q.en: Is there pressure for the price to change?
q.zh: 價格有冇改變嘅壓力？

w.en: At equilibrium the price has no tendency to change.
w.zh: 均衡時價格冇改變嘅傾向。

d.en: The price at which Qd = Qs is the equilibrium price (Pe); the matching quantity is the equilibrium quantity (Qe). At this point the price has no tendency to change.
d.zh: Qd = Qs 嘅價格係 equilibrium price（Pe），對應數量係 equilibrium quantity（Qe）；喺呢點價格冇改變嘅傾向。

p.en: On a diagram, equilibrium is where the demand and supply curves cross.
p.zh: 圖上，均衡點係 demand curve 同 supply curve 嘅交點。

q.en: Which is true at equilibrium?
q.zh: 均衡時以下邊句啱？

o.en: Everyone who wants the good gets it free.

o.zh: Quantity demanded 等於 quantity supplied。

o.en: The price is the lowest possible.

w.en: Qd = Qs; scarcity still exists, since the good has a price.
w.zh: Qd = Qs；scarcity 仍然存在，因為貨品有價。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of equilibrium price.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 equilibrium price 解釋。

o.en: It is where Qd meets Qs.
o.zh: 佢係 Qd 同 Qs 相等嘅位置。

o.en: The price at which Qd = Qs, so it has no tendency to change.
o.zh: Qd = Qs 嘅價格，所以冇改變嘅傾向。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Sneakers Street, 2026: a limited sneaker is priced at $600. 500 people want a pair but shops have only 300.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年波鞋街：限量波鞋定價 $600，有 500 人想買，但舖頭只有 300 對。

q.en: How many pairs are actually sold?
q.zh: 實際賣出幾多對？

w.en: With a shortage, the quantity transacted is Qs.
w.zh: 有短缺時，成交量 = Qs。

d.en: P < Pe: Qd > Qs, excess demand (shortage); quantity transacted Qt = Qs; price tends to rise. P > Pe: Qs > Qd, excess supply (surplus); Qt = Qd; price tends to fall. Shortage is not the same as scarcity.
d.zh: P < Pe：Qd > Qs，excess demand（shortage），成交量 Qt = Qs，價格傾向上升。P > Pe：Qs > Qd，excess supply（surplus），Qt = Qd，價格傾向下跌。Shortage 唔等於 scarcity。

p.en: Qt is always the smaller of Qd and Qs.
p.zh: Qt 一定係 Qd 同 Qs 之中較細嗰個。

p.en: Scarcity exists even at equilibrium; shortage only below Pe.
p.zh: 均衡時都有 scarcity；shortage 只喺低過 Pe 時出現。

s.en: Qd 500 > Qs 300 → shortage of 200.
Only 300 pairs change hands: Qt = Qs = 300.
s.zh: 只得 300 對成交：Qt = Qs = 300。

s.en: Resale prices online rise: the price tends to rise.
s.zh: 網上轉售價上升：價格傾向上升。

q.en: (Fictional figures) At $50, Qd = 80 and Qs = 120. Which is correct?
q.zh: （虛構數字）$50 時 Qd = 80，Qs = 120。以下邊句啱？

o.en: Surplus of 40; Qt = 80; price tends to fall.

w.en: Qs > Qd → surplus; buyers take only 80.
w.zh: Qs > Qd → 過剩；買家只買 80。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is a shortage not the same as scarcity?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解 shortage 唔等於 scarcity？

o.en: Scarcity exists at every price including equilibrium; a shortage exists only when price is below Pe.
o.zh: 任何價格（包括均衡）都有 scarcity；shortage 只喺價格低過 Pe 時出現。

o.en: A shortage means the good is free.
The good still has a price.

hook.en: (Fictional figures) In 2026 a popular Mong Kok bakery sells egg tarts at $10, but Ah Ying queues 30 minutes for them. Her best alternative use of that time pays $40 an hour.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年，旺角一間人氣餅店蛋撻賣 $10，但阿瑩要排隊 30 分鐘。嗰段時間佢最好嘅其他用途每個鐘值 $40。

q.en: What is the full price of one egg tart for Ah Ying?
q.zh: 對阿瑩嚟講，一個蛋撻嘅 full price 係幾多？

w.en: $10 + half an hour × $40 = $30.

d.en: Full price = money price + non-money price (such as queuing time). Relative price is the price of one good expressed in terms of another good. If the same amount is added to both money prices, the dearer good’s relative price falls.
d.zh: Full price = money price + non-money price（例如排隊時間）。Relative price = 一件物品以另一件物品表示嘅價格。兩件物品嘅 money price 加同一個數，貴嗰件嘅 relative price 會下降。

p.en: People respond to full prices and relative prices, not only money prices.
p.zh: 大家會對 full price 同 relative price 作出反應，唔只係 money price。

s.en: Egg tart $10, milk tea $20: one milk tea = 2 egg tarts.
s.zh: 蛋撻 $10、奶茶 $20：一杯奶茶 = 2 個蛋撻。

s.en: Add $10 to both: $20 and $30: one milk tea = 1.5 egg tarts.
s.zh: 兩樣都加 $10：$20 同 $30：一杯奶茶 = 1.5 個蛋撻。

s.en: The dearer good (milk tea) became relatively cheaper.
s.zh: 貴嗰樣（奶茶）相對平咗。

q.en: (Fictional figures) A $4 bun and a $12 sandwich both rise by $4. The relative price of the sandwich in terms of buns…
q.zh: （虛構數字）$4 嘅包同 $12 嘅三文治同樣加 $4。三文治以包計嘅相對價格…

q.en: Pick the best explanation of full price.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 full price 解釋。

o.en: The money price plus the value of non-money costs such as queuing time.
o.zh: Money price 加上排隊時間等非金錢成本嘅價值。

o.en: Everything given up to get the good.
o.zh: 為得到貨品而付出嘅一切。

chain.en: Demand: willing and able to buy
Supply: willing and able to sell
Below Pe: shortage; above Pe: surplus
chain.zh: 低過 Pe：短缺；高過 Pe：過剩

chain.en: People respond to full and relative prices
chain.zh: 大家對全部價格同相對價格作反應

q.en: A good’s own price rises. On the demand curve this is…
q.zh: 貨品自身價格上升，喺 demand curve 上係…

w.en: Own-price change → movement along.
w.zh: 自身價格改變 → 沿線移動。

q.en: (Fictional figures) At $5, Qd = 60 and Qs = 40. Quantity transacted is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）$5 時 Qd = 60，Qs = 40。成交量係…

w.en: Qt = the smaller, Qs.
w.zh: Qt = 較細嗰個，即 Qs。

q.en: Which is true?
q.zh: 以下邊句啱？

o.zh: Market demand 係將價格相加。

w.en: Scarcity ≠ shortage.
w.zh: Scarcity ≠ shortage。

q.en: In your own words: what happens to price and quantity when the market price is below equilibrium?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：市場價格低過均衡價格時，價格同數量會點？

ck.en: I said Qd > Qs, a shortage.
ck.zh: 我有講 Qd > Qs，即係短缺。

ck.en: I said quantity transacted equals Qs.
ck.zh: 我有講成交量等於 Qs。

ck.en: I said the price tends to rise.
ck.zh: 我有講價格傾向上升。

t.zh: 沿線移動 vs 整條線移動

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Yau Ma Tei Fruit Market, 2026: the price of oranges falls from $10 to $8 a kilo and shops order more. A week later a health report praises oranges and shops order more at every price.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年油麻地果欄：橙由每公斤 $10 跌到 $8，舖頭入多咗貨。一星期後，有健康報告大讚橙，舖頭喺每個價格都買多咗。

q.en: The price of oranges falls and buyers buy more. On the demand curve this is…
q.zh: 橙減價，買家買多咗。喺 demand curve 上係…

w.en: A change in the good’s own price moves along the same curve.
w.zh: 貨品自身價格改變，係沿同一條線移動。

d.en: A change in the good’s own price changes the quantity demanded or supplied: a movement along the same curve. A change in any other factor changes demand or supply: the whole curve shifts.
d.zh: 貨品自己嘅價格改變 → quantity demanded／supplied 改變，沿住同一條線移動（movement along）。其他因素改變 → demand／supply 改變，成條線移（shift）。

p.en: “Change in quantity demanded” ≠ “change in demand”.
p.zh: 「Quantity demanded 改變」≠「demand 改變」。

t.en: Two events at the fruit market (fictional)

s.en: Orange price $10 → $8: buyers move down the demand curve → quantity demanded ↑.
s.zh: 橙價 $10 → $8：沿 demand curve 向下移 → quantity demanded ↑。

s.en: Health report: buyers want more at every price → demand ↑ → curve shifts right.
s.zh: 健康報告：每個價格都想買多啲 → demand ↑ → 曲線向右移。

s.en: Ask: did the good’s own price change? Yes → along. No → shift.
s.zh: 問：貨品自身價格有冇變？有 → 沿線；冇 → 移線。

q.en: Which causes the demand curve for oranges to shift?
q.zh: 以下邊樣會令橙嘅 demand curve 移動？

o.en: Sellers offering more oranges because the price rose
o.zh: 因為加價，賣家供應更多橙

o.en: A fall in the price of oranges
A rise in the price of apples, a substitute
A rise in the price of oranges

w.en: Only a change in another factor shifts demand.
w.zh: 只有其他因素改變先會令 demand 移動。

q.en: Pick the best test for “along” vs “shift”.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅「沿線」vs「移線」判斷方法。

o.en: If the good’s own price changed, it is a movement along; any other factor shifts the curve.
o.zh: 如果係貨品自身價格改變就係沿線；其他因素就係移線。
自身價格 vs 其他因素。

o.en: If quantity rises, the curve shifts right.
Quantity can rise along a curve too.
o.zh: 沿線移動數量都可以上升。

o.en: Any change in price shifts the curve.
o.zh: 任何價格改變都會令曲線移動。
自身價格只會沿線移動。

t.zh: 代替品、互補品同引申需求

hook.en: Yau Ma Tei today: buses and the MTR serve many of the same trips; printers need ink; the fruit market hires porters only because people buy fruit.
hook.zh: 今日油麻地：巴士同港鐵好多路線重疊；打印機要配墨水；果欄請搬運工人，係因為大家買生果。

q.en: Bus fares fall. What happens to the demand for MTR rides on the same routes?
q.zh: 巴士減價，同路線港鐵嘅 demand 會點？

w.en: Substitutes: a cheaper bus draws riders away from the MTR.
w.zh: 代替品：巴士平咗，部分乘客轉搭巴士。

d.en: Substitutes (competitive demand): a rise in the price of a substitute increases the demand for this good. Complements (joint demand): a rise in the price of a complement decreases the demand. Derived demand: the demand for a factor of production comes from the demand for the product.
d.zh: Substitutes（competitive demand）：替代品加價 → 呢件貨嘅 demand 增加。Complements（joint demand）：互補品加價 → demand 減少。Derived demand：對生產要素嘅 demand 嚟自對產品嘅 demand。

p.en: These are shifts of the demand curve, not movements along it.
p.zh: 呢啲係 demand curve 移動，唔係沿線移動。

s.en: Bus fare ↓ → MTR demand ↓ (substitutes).
s.zh: 巴士車費 ↓ → 港鐵 demand ↓（代替品）。

s.en: Printer price ↑ → ink demand ↓ (complements).
s.zh: 打印機加價 → 墨水 demand ↓（互補品）。

s.en: Fruit sales ↑ → demand for porters ↑ (derived demand).
s.zh: 生果銷量 ↑ → 搬運工人 demand ↑（引申需求）。

q.en: Games consoles become more expensive. What happens to the demand for console games?
q.zh: 遊戲機加價。遊戲機遊戲嘅 demand 會點？

o.en: Quantity demanded of games falls along the curve.
o.zh: 遊戲嘅 quantity demanded 沿線下跌。

w.en: Fewer consoles bought → less demand for games: the curve shifts left.
w.zh: 少人買遊戲機 → 遊戲 demand 減少：曲線向左移。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of derived demand.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅引申需求解釋。

o.en: Firms want a factor because people want the product it helps make.
o.zh: 廠商需要某種生產要素，係因為大家想要佢幫手生產嘅產品。

o.en: Demand for porters follows demand for fruit.
o.zh: 搬運工人嘅需求跟住生果嘅需求。

o.en: Demand that rises when price rises.
That breaks the law of demand.
Demand for two goods used together.
o.zh: 對一齊用嘅兩件貨嘅需求。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) In 2026 Ah Ying’s aunt gets a pay rise and shops at Yau Ma Tei Market: she buys more fresh fish and fewer cheap instant noodles.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年，阿瑩姨媽加咗人工，去油麻地街市買餸：多買咗鮮魚，少買咗平價即食麵。

q.en: For her, cheap instant noodles are…
q.zh: 對佢嚟講，平價即食麵係…

w.en: Income ↑, demand ↓ → inferior good.
w.zh: 收入 ↑，demand ↓ → inferior good。

d.en: Normal good: income ↑ → demand ↑. Inferior good: income ↑ → demand ↓. Expecting a future price rise → demand now ↑. The number of buyers and tastes also shift the demand curve.
d.zh: Normal good：收入增加 → demand 增加；inferior good：收入增加 → demand 減少。預期將來加價 → 而家 demand 增加。買家數目、喜好都會令 demand curve 移動。

p.en: Whether a good is normal or inferior depends on the buyer, not the good itself.
p.zh: 正常品定劣等品視乎買家，唔係物品本身。

s.en: Pay rise: fish demand ↑ (normal); instant-noodle demand ↓ (inferior).
s.zh: 加人工：魚 demand ↑（正常品）；即食麵 demand ↓（劣等品）。

s.en: News that pork prices will rise next week → pork demand now ↑.
s.zh: 有消息話下星期豬肉加價 → 而家豬肉 demand ↑。

s.en: More tourists visit Temple Street → demand for snacks ↑.
s.zh: 多咗遊客去廟街 → 小食 demand ↑。

q.en: Buyers expect the price of rice to rise next month. The demand for rice now…
q.zh: 買家預期下個月米價上升，而家米嘅 demand…

w.en: They buy more now before the rise.
w.zh: 佢哋會趁未加價買多啲。

q.en: Pick the best definition of an inferior good.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 inferior good 定義。

o.en: A good whose demand falls when income rises.
o.zh: 收入上升時 demand 下跌嘅物品。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Yau Ma Tei Typhoon Shelter, 2026: fuel prices rise and a week of storms keeps fishing boats in harbour.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年油麻地避風塘：燃油加價，再加上一星期風暴，漁船唔出得海。

q.en: What happens to the supply of fresh fish?
q.zh: 鮮魚嘅 supply 會點？

w.en: Higher costs and bad weather reduce supply at every price.
w.zh: 成本上升同惡劣天氣令每個價格下嘅供應減少。

d.en: Higher production costs or a unit tax → supply decreases. Better technology or a unit subsidy → supply increases. Joint supply: more of one means more of the other. Competitive supply: a rise in another good’s price decreases this good’s supply. Sellers expecting a price rise → supply now decreases. Weather and the number of sellers also matter.
d.zh: 生產成本上升、unit tax → supply 減少；技術進步、unit subsidy → supply 增加。Joint supply：一樣多咗，另一樣都多咗。Competitive supply：另一件貨加價 → 呢件貨 supply 減少。賣家預期加價 → 而家 supply 減少。天氣、賣家數目都會影響 supply。

p.en: All of these shift the whole supply curve.
p.zh: 以上全部都令成條 supply curve 移動。

s.en: Fuel price ↑ → cost ↑ → fish supply ↓.
s.zh: 燃油加價 → 成本 ↑ → 魚嘅 supply ↓。

s.en: More beef produced → more cattle hides too (joint supply).
s.zh: 多咗牛肉 → 牛皮都多咗（joint supply）。

s.en: A farmer’s land can grow lettuce or choi sum; choi sum price ↑ → lettuce supply ↓ (competitive supply).
s.zh: 農地可以種生菜或菜心；菜心加價 → 生菜 supply ↓（competitive supply）。

q.en: Which INCREASES the supply of a good?
q.zh: 以下邊樣會令 supply 增加？

o.en: Sellers expect the price to rise next month

w.en: Better technology lowers cost per unit.
w.zh: 技術進步降低每單位成本。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of joint supply.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 joint supply 解釋。

o.en: Two goods that are used together.
Two goods competing for the same resources.
o.zh: 兩件貨爭用同一啲資源。

o.en: Producing more of one good automatically produces more of another.
o.zh: 生產多咗一樣，自然會多咗另一樣。

t.en: Effects of shifts on Pe and Qe
t.zh: 移動對 Pe 同 Qe 嘅影響

hook.en: (Fictional) Yau Ma Tei Fruit Market before Mid-Autumn Festival 2026: demand for pomelos rises, and a good harvest raises supply at the same time.
hook.zh: （虛構）2026 年中秋前油麻地果欄：柚子 demand 上升，同時豐收令 supply 增加。

q.en: Demand and supply both increase. Which is certain?
q.zh: Demand 同 supply 都增加，邊樣係肯定？

w.en: Both shifts raise quantity; their effects on price pull in opposite directions.
w.zh: 兩個移動都令數量上升；對價格嘅影響就互相抵銷。

d.en: D↑: Pe↑ Qe↑. D↓: Pe↓ Qe↓. S↑: Pe↓ Qe↑. S↓: Pe↑ Qe↓. Simultaneous shifts: D↑ S↑ → Qe↑, Pe uncertain; D↑ S↓ → Pe↑, Qe uncertain (unless the sizes of the shifts are known).
d.zh: D↑：Pe↑ Qe↑；D↓：Pe↓ Qe↓；S↑：Pe↓ Qe↑；S↓：Pe↑ Qe↓。兩條線同時移：D↑S↑ → Qe↑、Pe 不確定；D↑S↓ → Pe↑、Qe 不確定（除非知道移動幅度）。

p.en: Method: find each shift’s effect on P and Q separately, then combine.
p.zh: 方法：分開搵每個移動對 P 同 Q 嘅影響，再合併。

s.en: D↑ alone: Pe↑, Qe↑.
s.zh: 只有 D↑：Pe↑、Qe↑。

s.en: S↑ alone: Pe↓, Qe↑.
s.zh: 只有 S↑：Pe↓、Qe↑。

s.en: Together: Qe↑ for sure; Pe depends on which shift is bigger.
s.zh: 一齊：Qe 一定 ↑；Pe 要睇邊個移得多。

q.en: Demand for a good increases while its supply decreases. Which is certain?
q.zh: 某貨品 demand 增加，同時 supply 減少。邊樣係肯定？

w.en: Both shifts push price up; their effects on quantity conflict.
w.zh: 兩個移動都推高價格；對數量嘅影響互相抵銷。

q.en: Pick the best method for two shifts at once.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅方法分析兩條線同時移。

o.en: Price always rises when anything changes.
o.zh: 有任何改變價格都一定上升。
只有 S↑ 會令價格下跌。

o.en: Without the sizes of the shifts, one result stays uncertain.
o.zh: 唔知幅度，其中一個結果仍然不確定。

o.en: Work out each shift’s effect on P and Q separately; where they agree the result is certain.
o.zh: 分開計每個移動對 P 同 Q 嘅影響；方向一致嘅就肯定。

chain.zh: 自身價格改變 → 沿線移動

chain.en: Demand factors: related goods, income, expectations, tastes
chain.zh: 需求因素：相關物品、收入、預期、喜好

chain.en: Supply factors: cost, tech, tax, weather, related goods
chain.zh: 供應因素：成本、技術、稅、天氣、相關物品

chain.en: Combine shifts to find Pe and Qe
chain.zh: 合併移動搵 Pe 同 Qe

q.en: Income rises and demand for a good falls. The good is…
q.zh: 收入上升，某物品 demand 下跌。佢係…

w.en: Income ↑ demand ↓.
w.zh: 收入 ↑ demand ↓。

q.en: Supply decreases, demand unchanged. Then…
q.zh: Supply 減少，demand 不變。結果…

w.en: S↓: Pe↑ Qe↓.
w.zh: S↓：Pe↑ Qe↓。

q.en: The price of a complement rises. Demand for this good…
q.zh: 互補品加價，呢件貨嘅 demand…

w.en: Joint demand.
w.zh: Joint demand。

q.en: In your own words: how do you tell a “change in demand” from a “change in quantity demanded”?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點樣分辨「demand 改變」同「quantity demanded 改變」？

ck.en: I said the good’s own price causes a change in quantity demanded.
ck.zh: 我有講自身價格改變引致 quantity demanded 改變。

ck.en: I said other factors cause a change in demand (a shift).
ck.zh: 我有講其他因素引致 demand 改變（移線）。

ck.en: I gave an example of each.
ck.zh: 我兩種都有舉例。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Yau Ma Tei Jade Market, 2026: a stall cuts the price of a jade bracelet from $100 to $80, and daily sales rise from 20 to 30.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年油麻地玉器市場：一個檔將玉鐲由 $100 減到 $80，每日銷量由 20 隻升到 30 隻。

q.en: Using the arc method, what is the % change in quantity?
q.zh: 用 arc method，數量變動百分比係幾多？

d.en: Ed = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔP (absolute value). The arc method uses the average of the two points: %ΔQ = (Q2 − Q1) ÷ [(Q1 + Q2)/2].
d.zh: Ed = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔP（取絕對值）。Arc method 用兩點嘅平均值計百分比：%ΔQ = (Q2 − Q1) ÷ [(Q1 + Q2)/2]。

p.en: The arc method gives the same answer whether price rises or falls between the two points.
p.zh: 用 arc method，無論加價定減價，兩點之間計出嚟都一樣。

q.en: (Fictional figures) Price rises from $9 to $11 and quantity demanded falls from 110 to 90. Ed (arc method) is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）價格由 $9 升到 $11，quantity demanded 由 110 跌到 90。Ed（arc method）係…

q.en: Pick the best description of what Ed measures.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 Ed 描述。

o.en: The slope of the demand curve.
How responsive quantity demanded is to a change in the good’s own price.
o.zh: Quantity demanded 對自身價格改變有幾敏感。

o.en: % change in Qd ÷ % change in P.
o.zh: Qd 變動百分比 ÷ P 變動百分比。

o.en: That is income, not own price.
o.zh: 呢個係收入，唔係自身價格。

t.zh: 有彈性、缺乏彈性同單位彈性

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Yau Ma Tei, 2026: when a jade stall cuts prices by 10%, sales jump 30%; when a pharmacy cuts the price of a daily medicine by 10%, sales rise only 2%.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年油麻地：玉器檔減價 10%，銷量升 30%；藥房將日常藥物減價 10%，銷量只升 2%。

q.en: Demand for the daily medicine is…
q.zh: 日常藥物嘅 demand 係…

d.en: Ed (absolute value) > 1: elastic; < 1: inelastic; = 1: unitary elastic; = 0: perfectly inelastic (vertical curve); = ∞: perfectly elastic (horizontal curve). A straight-line demand curve has a constant slope, but Ed changes along it: slope ≠ elasticity.
d.zh: Ed（取絕對值）> 1 elastic；< 1 inelastic；= 1 unitary elastic；= 0 perfectly inelastic（垂直）；= ∞ perfectly elastic（水平）。直線 demand curve 斜率不變，但 Ed 沿線改變：slope ≠ elasticity。

p.en: On a straight-line demand curve, Ed is higher at higher prices.
p.zh: 直線 demand curve 上，價格越高嘅位置 Ed 越大。

s.en: Jade: 30% ÷ 10% = 3 → elastic.
s.zh: 玉器：30% ÷ 10% = 3 → elastic。

s.en: Medicine: 2% ÷ 10% = 0.2 → inelastic.
s.zh: 藥物：2% ÷ 10% = 0.2 → inelastic。

s.en: A vertical demand curve would mean Ed = 0: quantity never changes.
s.zh: 垂直嘅 demand curve 代表 Ed = 0：數量完全唔變。

q.en: A perfectly elastic demand curve is…
q.zh: Perfectly elastic 嘅 demand curve 係…

w.en: Any price rise loses all buyers: Ed = ∞.
w.zh: 加少少價就流失晒所有買家：Ed = ∞。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is slope not the same as elasticity?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解斜率唔等於彈性？

o.en: A steeper curve is always more elastic.
o.zh: 越斜嘅線一定越有彈性。

o.en: Usually the opposite, and still not reliable.
o.zh: 通常相反，而且都唔可靠。

o.en: Elasticity uses percentage changes, which differ along a straight line even though the slope is constant.
o.zh: 彈性用百分比變動計，喺直線上唔同位置唔同，但斜率不變。

o.en: Elasticity is the slope multiplied by price.

t.zh: 影響需求價格彈性嘅因素

hook.en: (Fictional) Temple Street night market, 2026: many stalls sell similar phone cases, while a pharmacy nearby sells the one brand of insulin a patient needs.
hook.zh: （虛構）2026 年廟街夜市：好多檔口賣類似嘅手機殼；附近藥房賣病人必需嘅一款胰島素。

q.en: Why is demand for one stall’s phone cases likely to be elastic?
q.zh: 點解一個檔口手機殼嘅 demand 可能富彈性？

o.en: Many close substitutes are next door.
o.zh: 隔籬有好多相近代替品。

w.en: More and closer substitutes → more elastic.
w.zh: 代替品越多越接近 → 越 elastic。

d.en: More and closer substitutes → more elastic. Necessities are more inelastic. A larger share of income → more elastic. A longer time period → more elastic. Durability, habit and the number of uses also affect Ed.
d.zh: 替代品越多越接近 → 越 elastic；必需品較 inelastic；佔收入比例越大 → 越 elastic；時間越長 → 越 elastic；耐用品、習慣、用途多寡都會影響 Ed。

p.en: Ask each factor in turn, then weigh them.
p.zh: 逐個因素問，再權衡。

s.en: One stall’s phone cases: many substitutes → elastic.
s.zh: 一個檔嘅手機殼：代替品多 → elastic。

s.en: Insulin for a patient: necessity, no substitute → inelastic.
s.zh: 病人用嘅胰島素：必需、冇代替品 → inelastic。

s.en: A car: large share of income → more elastic.
s.zh: 汽車：佔收入比例大 → 較 elastic。

q.en: Which makes demand MORE inelastic?
q.zh: 以下邊樣令 demand 更缺乏彈性？

o.en: Buyers have a long time to adjust.
The good is a habit, like cigarettes for smokers.
o.zh: 貨品成癮，例如煙民嘅香煙。

o.en: It takes a large share of income.

w.en: Habit-forming goods are less responsive to price.
w.zh: 成癮物品對價格較唔敏感。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is demand more elastic in the long run?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解長期 demand 較富彈性？

o.en: Prices are always lower in the long run.
Buyers have more time to find substitutes and change habits.
o.zh: 買家有更多時間搵代替品、改習慣。

o.en: Income always falls in the long run.

t.zh: 總收益同需求價格彈性

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Back at the Jade Market: the bracelet stall cut its price from $100 to $80 and sales rose from 20 to 30 a day.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）返到玉器市場：玉鐲檔由 $100 減到 $80，每日銷量由 20 隻升到 30 隻。

q.en: What happened to the stall’s total revenue?
q.zh: 檔口嘅總收益點變？

d.en: Elastic: price and TR move in opposite directions. Inelastic: price and TR move in the same direction. Unitary: TR is unchanged. A price cut increases TR only when demand is elastic.
d.zh: Elastic：價格同 TR 反方向；inelastic：同方向；unitary：TR 不變。減價只會喺 demand elastic 時增加 TR。

p.en: Here TR means the seller’s total revenue = buyers’ total expenditure.
p.zh: 呢度 TR = 賣家總收益 = 買家總開支。

t.zh: 兩個價格改變（虛構數字）

s.en: Bracelet (elastic): price ↓ → TR ↑ ($2,000 → $2,400).
Medicine (inelastic): price ↑ 10%, quantity ↓ 2% → TR ↑.
s.zh: 藥物（inelastic）：價 ↑ 10%，數量 ↓ 2% → TR ↑。

s.en: Unitary: price ↑ 10%, quantity ↓ 10% → TR roughly unchanged.
s.zh: Unitary：價 ↑ 10%，數量 ↓ 10% → TR 大致不變。

q.en: Demand for a good is inelastic. A seller who wants higher TR should…
q.zh: 某貨品 demand 缺乏彈性。想增加 TR 嘅賣家應該…

w.en: Inelastic: price and TR move in the same direction.
w.zh: Inelastic：價格同 TR 同方向。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does a price cut raise TR when demand is elastic?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解 demand elastic 時減價會令 TR 上升？

o.en: The % rise in quantity is larger than the % fall in price.
o.zh: 數量上升嘅百分比大過價格下跌嘅百分比。

hook.en: (Fictional) Yau Ma Tei Fruit Market, early morning 2026: lychee prices jump, but this morning’s stock is all there is; next season farmers can plant more.
hook.zh: （虛構）2026 年油麻地果欄清晨：荔枝價錢急升，但今朝得嗰批貨；下一季果農先可以種多啲。

q.en: This morning, the supply of fresh lychees is…
q.zh: 今朝新鮮荔枝嘅 supply 係…

w.en: Fresh fruit cannot be stored or grown in hours, so Es is very low in the very short run.
w.zh: 新鮮生果唔可以儲，亦唔可以幾個鐘內種出嚟，所以極短期 Es 好低。

d.en: Es = %ΔQs ÷ %ΔP. Supply is more elastic with more time, easily transferred factors, spare capacity or stocks, and easy entry. Fresh fruit cannot be stored, so Es is very low in the very short run.
d.zh: Es = %ΔQs ÷ %ΔP。時間越長、生產要素越易轉移、有剩餘產能或存貨、容易入行 → supply 越 elastic。新鮮生果唔可以儲，極短期 Es 好低。

p.en: Es is positive: price and quantity supplied move together.
p.zh: Es 係正數：價格同 quantity supplied 同方向。

s.en: This morning: stock fixed → Es near 0.
s.zh: 今朝：貨量固定 → Es 接近 0。

s.en: Next week: shippers bring more from other farms → Es higher.
s.zh: 下星期：可以由其他果園運多啲嚟 → Es 較高。

s.en: Next season: farmers plant more → Es higher still.
s.zh: 下一季：果農種多啲 → Es 更高。

q.en: Which makes supply MORE elastic?
q.zh: 以下邊樣令 supply 更富彈性？

o.en: Factors are hard to move between uses.
Firms have spare capacity and stocks.
o.zh: 廠商有剩餘產能同存貨。

o.en: Entry to the industry is difficult.

w.en: Spare capacity and stocks let output respond quickly.
w.zh: 有剩餘產能同存貨，產量可以快速回應。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is supply more elastic in the long run?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解長期 supply 較富彈性？

o.en: Producers have time to change all their inputs and new firms can enter.
o.zh: 生產者有時間調整所有投入，新廠商亦可以入行。

o.en: Demand is higher in the long run.
Prices never change in the long run.

chain.en: Determinants: substitutes, necessity, share of income, time
chain.zh: 因素：代替品、必需性、佔收入比例、時間

chain.en: Ed decides how TR responds to price
chain.zh: Ed 決定 TR 點回應價格

q.en: Demand is elastic. A price rise makes TR…
q.zh: Demand elastic，加價會令 TR…

w.en: Elastic: opposite direction.
w.zh: Elastic：反方向。

q.en: Ed = 0 means the demand curve is…
q.zh: Ed = 0 代表 demand curve 係…

w.en: Perfectly inelastic.
w.zh: 完全缺乏彈性。

q.en: Which good probably has the most inelastic demand?
q.zh: 以下邊件貨嘅 demand 最可能最缺乏彈性？

w.en: Necessity, tiny share of income, no close substitute as a whole.
w.zh: 必需品、佔收入極少、整體冇相近代替品。

q.en: In your own words: why would a jade stall cut prices but a pharmacy not cut the price of a daily medicine?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解玉器檔會減價，但藥房唔會將日常藥物減價？

ck.en: I said jade demand is elastic and medicine demand is inelastic.
ck.zh: 我有講玉器 demand elastic，藥物 demand inelastic。

ck.en: I linked elasticity to what happens to TR.
ck.zh: 我有將彈性同 TR 嘅變化連埋一齊。

ck.en: I gave a determinant (substitutes or necessity).
ck.zh: 我有講一個影響因素（代替品或必需品）。

hook.en: (Fictional policy) Shek Kip Mei, 2011: in this game scenario, the government sets a maximum price of $20 on a popular estate-market snack whose equilibrium price is $30.
hook.zh: （虛構政策）2011 年石硤尾：喺呢個遊戲情境入面，政府將屋邨街市一款人氣小食定最高價 $20，而均衡價係 $30。

q.en: Is this price ceiling effective?
q.zh: 呢個 price ceiling 有冇效？

o.en: Yes, it is set below Pe.
o.zh: 有，佢定喺 Pe 以下。

o.en: No, it is set above Pe.
o.zh: 冇，佢定喺 Pe 以上。

w.en: A ceiling must be below Pe to bind.
w.zh: 價格上限要低過 Pe 先有效。

d.en: A price ceiling is a legal maximum price. It is effective only when set below the equilibrium price: price falls, a shortage appears (Qd > Qs), and quantity transacted Qt = Qs, which is less than before.
d.zh: Price ceiling 係法定最高價格。要定喺 equilibrium price 以下先有效：價格下降、出現 shortage（Qd > Qs），成交量 Qt = Qs，比原本少。

p.en: A ceiling at or above Pe changes nothing.
p.zh: 定喺 Pe 或以上嘅上限冇影響。

s.en: At $30: Qd = Qs = 500 a day.
s.zh: $30：Qd = Qs = 每日 500 份。

s.en: At $20: Qd = 700, Qs = 300 → shortage of 400.
Only 300 are sold: Qt = Qs, fewer than the 500 before.
s.zh: 只賣出 300 份：Qt = Qs，少過原本 500 份。

q.en: An effective price ceiling causes…
q.zh: 有效嘅價格上限會引致…

w.en: Below Pe: Qd > Qs, and sellers only supply Qs.
w.zh: 低過 Pe：Qd > Qs，賣家只供應 Qs。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does an effective ceiling reduce the quantity sold?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解有效嘅價格上限會令成交量減少？

o.en: At the lower price, sellers offer less, and buyers cannot buy more than is supplied.
o.zh: 價低咗，賣家供應少咗，買家亦唔可能買多過供應。

o.en: Buyers want less at a lower price.

hook.en: (Fictional policy) Same $20 snack in Shek Kip Mei, 2011: 700 people want one each day, but only 300 are made.
hook.zh: （虛構政策）同一款 $20 小食，2011 年石硤尾：每日 700 人想買，但只整 300 份。

q.en: Price can no longer decide who gets the snack. What will?
q.zh: 價格再唔可以決定邊個買到。咁靠乜？

o.en: Non-price rules such as queuing or first come, first served
o.zh: 非價格準則，例如排隊、先到先得

w.en: A legal maximum stops bidding, so other rules take over.
w.zh: 法定上限令人唔可以出高價，其他準則取而代之。

d.en: Under an effective price ceiling, price cannot allocate the good, so non-price competition takes over: queuing, first come first served, lottery, favouritism. Black markets, extra charges and lower quality also appear; queuing time raises the full price.
d.zh: 有效嘅 price ceiling 下，價格唔可以分配貨品，就靠 non-price competition：排隊、先到先得、抽籤、人情。仲會出現 black market、額外收費、質素下降；排隊時間令 full price 上升。

p.en: The money price is lower, but the full price may not be.
p.zh: 金錢價格低咗，但 full price 未必低。

s.en: Long queues form → the full price = $20 + time spent.
s.zh: 大排長龍 → full price = $20 + 排隊時間。

s.en: Some buyers resell outside at $35 → black market.
s.zh: 有人喺外面以 $35 轉售 → 黑市。

s.en: The stall makes portions smaller → lower quality.
s.zh: 檔口將份量整細 → 質素下降。

q.en: Which is NOT a likely result of an effective price ceiling?
q.zh: 以下邊樣唔係有效價格上限嘅可能結果？

w.en: A ceiling below Pe causes a shortage, not a surplus.
w.zh: 低過 Pe 嘅上限引致短缺，唔係過剩。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why can the full price rise under a price ceiling?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解價格上限下 full price 可以上升？

o.en: Sellers add a service charge by law.
o.zh: 法例要求賣家收服務費。

o.en: Buyers must add the value of their queuing time to the lower money price.
o.zh: 買家要喺較低嘅金錢價格上加上排隊時間嘅價值。

hook.en: Hong Kong, 1 May 2011: the statutory minimum wage of $28 an hour came into force.
hook.zh: 2011 年 5 月 1 日：香港 $28 嘅法定最低工資生效。

q.en: A minimum wage is which kind of price control?
q.zh: 最低工資係邊種價格管制？

o.en: A price ceiling in the labour market
A price floor in the labour market

w.en: It is a legal minimum price for labour.
w.zh: 佢係勞動嘅法定最低價格。

d.en: A price floor is a legal minimum price. It is effective only when set above the equilibrium price: price rises, a surplus appears (Qs > Qd), and Qt = Qd. A minimum wage is a price floor in the labour market; if set above the market wage, a surplus of labour (unemployment) appears.
d.zh: Price floor 係法定最低價格。要定喺 equilibrium price 以上先有效：價格上升、出現 surplus（Qs > Qd），Qt = Qd。Minimum wage 係勞工市場嘅 price floor，高過市場工資就會出現勞工過剩（失業）。

p.en: In the labour market, workers supply labour and firms demand it.
p.zh: 勞工市場：工人供應勞動，廠商需求勞動。

t.zh: 一個勞工市場（虛構數字）

s.en: Market wage $40 an hour: 1,000 workers hired.
s.zh: 市場工資每小時 $40：請 1,000 人。

s.en: Floor at $45 (above $40): firms hire 900; 1,050 want to work.
Surplus of labour = 150; employment Qt = Qd = 900.
s.zh: 勞工過剩 150 人；就業人數 Qt = Qd = 900。

q.en: A minimum wage set BELOW the market wage will…
q.zh: 最低工資定喺市場工資以下會…

w.en: A floor below Pe is ineffective.
w.zh: 低過 Pe 嘅下限冇效。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why can an effective minimum wage cause unemployment?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解有效嘅最低工資可能引致失業？

o.en: Firms must hire everyone who applies.
o.zh: 廠商一定要請晒所有求職者。

o.en: Above the market wage, more people want to work but firms hire fewer.
o.zh: 高過市場工資，想做嘅人多咗，但廠商請少咗。

t.zh: 有效 vs 無效嘅管制

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Shek Kip Mei, Yen Chow Street cloth bazaar, 2026: the equilibrium price of a roll of cloth is $100.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年石硤尾欽州街棚仔布市場：一疋布嘅均衡價係 $100。

q.en: A price ceiling of $120 is set. Is it effective?
q.zh: 定 $120 嘅價格上限，有冇效？

w.en: The market price $100 is already below the ceiling.
w.zh: 市價 $100 已經低過上限。

d.en: A price ceiling at or above Pe, or a price floor at or below Pe, is ineffective: the market is unaffected. Under an effective price floor, sellers’ TR depends on Ed: demand elastic → TR falls; inelastic → TR rises.
d.zh: Price ceiling 定喺 Pe 或以上、price floor 定喺 Pe 或以下都係 ineffective，市場唔受影響。有效 price floor 下賣家 TR 點變睇 Ed：demand elastic → TR 跌；inelastic → TR 升。

p.en: Ceiling: effective below Pe. Floor: effective above Pe.
p.zh: 上限：低過 Pe 先有效。下限：高過 Pe 先有效。

s.en: Ceiling $120 → ineffective; ceiling $80 → effective (shortage).
s.zh: 上限 $120 → 無效；上限 $80 → 有效（短缺）。

s.en: Floor $80 → ineffective; floor $120 → effective (surplus).
s.zh: 下限 $80 → 無效；下限 $120 → 有效（過剩）。

s.en: Under the $120 floor, sellers’ TR rises only if demand is inelastic.
s.zh: $120 下限之下，只有 demand inelastic 時賣家 TR 先會上升。

q.en: An effective price floor is imposed and demand is elastic. Sellers’ TR…
q.zh: 實施有效嘅價格下限，而 demand 富彈性。賣家 TR…

w.en: Price ↑ with elastic demand → TR ↓.
w.zh: 價 ↑ 而 demand elastic → TR ↓。

q.en: Pick the best rule for when a price floor is effective.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅規則：價格下限幾時有效？

o.zh: 要睇同 Pe 嘅相對位置。

o.en: When it is set above the equilibrium price.
Otherwise the market price is already above it.
o.zh: 否則市價本身已經高過佢。

o.en: When it is set below the equilibrium price.

hook.en: Before the global garment quota system ended in 2005, Hong Kong’s textile exports to markets such as the United States and the European Union were limited by quotas, and quota holders could transfer quotas to other traders.
hook.zh: 全球成衣配額制度喺 2005 年結束之前，香港輸往美國、歐盟等市場嘅紡織品受配額限制，持有配額嘅商人可以將配額轉讓俾其他商人。

stops.src: LegCo paper on Hong Kong’s Textiles Quota Allocation System (1998–99); HKPC press release, 23 Aug 2005

q.en: Why could a quota be sold for money?
q.zh: 點解配額可以賣錢？

o.en: It let the holder sell in a market where the price was pushed up by limited supply.
o.zh: 持有人可以喺一個因為供應受限而價格被推高嘅市場賣貨。

w.en: Limited quantity raises price; the right to sell has value.
w.zh: 數量受限令價格上升；出售權因此有價值。

d.en: A quota is a legal maximum quantity. It is effective only when set below the equilibrium quantity: the supply curve becomes vertical (kinked) at the quota, price rises, quantity falls. Quota holders earn extra income (quota rights have value), and quality may rise.
d.zh: Quota 係法定最高數量。要定喺 equilibrium quantity 以下先有效：supply curve 喺配額數量變垂直（kinked），價格上升、數量減少；持有配額嘅人賺到額外收入（quota rights 有價值），質素可能提高。

p.en: A quota at or above Qe is ineffective.
p.zh: 定喺 Qe 或以上嘅配額無效。

s.en: Free market: 1,000 shirts at $50.
Quota 600 → supply vertical at 600 → price rises to $70.
s.zh: 配額 600 件 → supply 喺 600 變垂直 → 價格升到 $70。

s.en: Each quota unit earns extra income, so quota rights can be sold.
s.zh: 每單位配額帶嚟額外收入，所以配額可以買賣。

q.en: An effective quota leads to…
q.zh: 有效嘅配額會引致…

o.en: a shortage at the market price
a lower price and a larger quantity
a higher price and a smaller quantity

w.en: Supply is cut, so price rises and quantity falls.
w.zh: 供應被削減，價升量跌。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why may quality rise under a quota?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解配額下質素可能提高？

o.en: With quantity limited, sellers earn more by selling higher-value versions of each unit.
o.zh: 數量受限，賣家每單位賣較高價值嘅款式可以賺更多。

chain.zh: 低過 Pe 嘅上限 → 短缺
高過 Pe 嘅下限 → 過剩
最低工資 → 可能失業

chain.en: Quota below Qe → price up, quantity down
chain.zh: 低過 Qe 嘅配額 → 價升量跌

q.en: A price ceiling set above Pe…
q.zh: 定喺 Pe 以上嘅價格上限…

w.en: Ineffective.
w.zh: 無效。

q.en: Under an effective price floor, Qt equals…
q.zh: 有效價格下限下，Qt 等於…

w.en: Buyers decide how much is sold.
w.zh: 由買家決定成交量。

q.en: Quota rights have value because…
q.zh: 配額有價值，因為…

o.en: the quota raises the market price

w.en: Higher price → extra income for holders.
w.zh: 價格上升 → 持有人有額外收入。

q.en: In your own words: why does a price ceiling below Pe lead to queues?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解低過 Pe 嘅價格上限會引致排隊？

ck.en: I said Qd > Qs at the lower price.
ck.zh: 我有講價低咗 Qd > Qs。

ck.en: I said price can no longer allocate the good.
ck.zh: 我有講價格再唔可以分配貨品。

ck.en: I said non-price rules like queuing take over.
ck.zh: 我有講排隊等非價格準則取而代之。

hook.en: (Fictional policy and figures) Shek Kip Mei, 2026: a $4 unit tax is placed on sellers of bottled sugary drinks. Before the tax, Pe = $10 and 100 bottles are sold a day.
hook.zh: （虛構政策同數字）2026 年石硤尾：向含糖樽裝飲品賣家徵 $4 從量稅。徵稅前 Pe = $10，每日賣 100 支。

q.en: After the tax, the price consumers pay most likely…
q.zh: 徵稅後，消費者付嘅價格最可能…

w.en: In general both sides share the tax.
w.zh: 一般情況下買賣雙方分擔稅款。

d.en: A unit tax on sellers shifts the supply curve up by the tax per unit. In general, the price consumers pay rises by less than the tax; the net price producers receive (market price − tax) falls; quantity transacted falls.
d.zh: 向賣家徵 unit tax，supply curve 向上移，垂直距離等於每單位稅款。一般情況下，消費者付嘅價格上升但升幅細過稅款；生產者收到嘅淨價格（市價 − 稅）下跌；成交量減少。

p.en: Pc = price consumers pay; Pp = Pc − tax = price producers keep.
p.zh: Pc = 消費者付嘅價；Pp = Pc − 稅 = 生產者實收。

t.zh: 徵 $4 稅之後（虛構數字）

s.en: Supply shifts up by $4.
s.zh: Supply 向上移 $4。

s.en: New market price Pc = $13; producers keep Pp = $13 − $4 = $9.
s.zh: 新市價 Pc = $13；生產者實收 Pp = $13 − $4 = $9。

s.en: Quantity falls from 100 to 80 bottles.
s.zh: 成交量由 100 支跌到 80 支。

q.en: A unit tax on sellers shifts the supply curve…
q.zh: 向賣家徵從量稅，supply curve…

o.en: downward by the tax per unit
upward by the tax per unit
o.zh: 向上移，距離等於每單位稅款

w.en: Sellers need $4 more at each quantity.
w.zh: 每個數量下賣家都要多收 $4。

q.en: Pick the best description of Pp after a unit tax.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅徵稅後 Pp 描述。

o.en: The market price minus the tax: what producers actually keep.
o.zh: 市價減稅款：生產者實際收到嘅錢。

o.en: Pp is usually below the old Pe.
o.zh: Pp 通常低過原本 Pe。

o.en: The market price plus the tax.

hook.en: Hong Kong today: cigarettes carry a heavy tobacco duty. Many smokers keep buying even when the price rises.
hook.zh: 今日香港：香煙有重稅。好多煙民加價都照買。

q.en: Demand for cigarettes is inelastic. Who bears more of a cigarette tax?
q.zh: 香煙 demand 缺乏彈性。邊個負擔較多煙稅？

w.en: The less elastic side bears more.
w.zh: 彈性較低嗰一方負擔較多。

d.en: Tax incidence: the side with the lower elasticity bears more of the tax. Demand perfectly inelastic → consumers bear all; demand perfectly elastic → producers bear all. Consumer burden = rise in price paid; producer burden = fall in net price.
d.zh: Tax incidence：邊一方嘅 elasticity 較低，就負擔較多稅款。Demand perfectly inelastic → 消費者負擔全部；demand perfectly elastic → 生產者負擔全部。消費者負擔 = 付價升幅；生產者負擔 = 淨價跌幅。

p.en: Who pays the tax to the government is not the same as who bears it.
p.zh: 邊個交稅俾政府，唔等於邊個負擔稅款。

t.zh: 再睇含糖飲品稅（虛構數字）

s.en: Consumers: $10 → $13, burden $3 per bottle.
Producers: $10 → $9, burden $1 per bottle.
Consumers bear more, so demand is less elastic than supply here.
s.zh: 消費者負擔較多，所以呢度 demand 嘅彈性低過 supply。

q.en: Demand for a good is perfectly elastic. A unit tax is borne…
q.zh: 某貨品 demand 完全有彈性。從量稅由…

w.en: Consumers will not pay a cent more, so price paid cannot rise.
w.zh: 消費者一蚊都唔肯多俾，所以付價唔可以升。

q.en: Pick the best rule for tax incidence.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅稅負規則。

o.en: Consumers always bear all of it.
Only if demand is perfectly inelastic.
o.zh: 只有 demand 完全缺乏彈性先係。

o.en: The less elastic side bears more of the tax.
o.zh: 彈性較低嘅一方負擔較多稅款。

o.en: The side that hands the tax to the government bears it all.
o.zh: 交稅俾政府嗰一方負擔全部。
法定交稅者 ≠ 實際負擔者。

hook.en: (Fictional policy and figures) Shek Kip Mei estate market, 2026: the government pays vegetable sellers a $2 subsidy per catty. Before the subsidy, Pe = $10 and 100 catties are sold.
hook.zh: （虛構政策同數字）2026 年石硤尾屋邨街市：政府每斤菜補貼賣家 $2。補貼前 Pe = $10，賣 100 斤。

q.en: After the subsidy, the price consumers pay most likely…
q.zh: 補貼後，消費者付嘅價最可能…

w.en: Supply increases, so the market price falls.
w.zh: Supply 增加，市價下跌。

d.en: A unit subsidy to sellers shifts the supply curve down by the subsidy per unit. The price consumers pay falls, the price producers receive (market price + subsidy) rises, and quantity transacted increases. The less elastic side gains more.
d.zh: 俾賣家 unit subsidy，supply curve 向下移，距離等於每單位補貼。消費者付嘅價格下跌，生產者收到嘅價格（市價 + 補貼）上升，成交量增加；elasticity 較低嗰一方得到較多好處。

p.en: Producers receive Pp = Pc + subsidy.
p.zh: 生產者收 Pp = Pc + 補貼。

s.en: Supply shifts down by $2.
s.zh: Supply 向下移 $2。

s.en: Consumers pay $9; producers receive $9 + $2 = $11.
Quantity rises from 100 to 120 catties.
s.zh: 成交量由 100 斤升到 120 斤。

q.en: Under a unit subsidy, the price producers receive is…
q.zh: 從量補貼下，生產者收到嘅價格係…

o.en: the market price minus the subsidy
the market price plus the subsidy

w.en: Pp = Pc + subsidy.
w.zh: Pp = Pc + 補貼。

q.en: Pick the best statement about who gains from a subsidy.
q.zh: 揀關於邊個得益於補貼嘅最好說法。

o.en: Only producers gain, since they receive the money.
o.zh: 只有生產者得益，因為錢俾咗佢哋。

o.en: Both sides gain, and the less elastic side gains more.
o.zh: 雙方都得益，彈性較低嗰方得益較多。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) The sugary-drink tax: Pe was $10; after the $4 tax, Pc = $13, Pp = $9, Qt = 80 bottles a day.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）含糖飲品稅：原本 Pe = $10；徵 $4 稅後 Pc = $13、Pp = $9、Qt = 每日 80 支。

q.en: What is the daily tax revenue?
q.zh: 每日稅收係幾多？

w.en: Tax revenue = tax per unit × new quantity = 4 × 80.
w.zh: 稅收 = 每單位稅 × 新成交量 = 4 × 80。

d.en: Tax revenue = tax per unit × new quantity. Consumer burden = (Pc − Pe) × Qt; producer burden = (Pe − Pp) × Qt. Consumers’ total expenditure = Pc × Qt. Subsidy expenditure = subsidy per unit × new quantity.
d.zh: 稅收 = 每單位稅 × 新成交量。消費者負擔 = (Pc − Pe) × Qt；生產者負擔 = (Pe − Pp) × Qt。消費者總開支 = Pc × Qt。補貼開支 = 每單位補貼 × 新成交量。

p.en: Check: consumer burden + producer burden = tax revenue.
p.zh: 驗算：消費者負擔 + 生產者負擔 = 稅收。

s.en: Consumer burden = (13 − 10) × 80 = $240; producer burden = (10 − 9) × 80 = $80.
Check: $240 + $80 = $320. Consumers’ total expenditure = 13 × 80 = $1,040.

q.en: (Fictional figures) Vegetable subsidy: $2 per catty, new quantity 120 catties. Government spending is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）蔬菜補貼每斤 $2，新成交量 120 斤。政府開支係…

w.en: 2 × 120 = $240, using the new quantity.

q.en: Pick the most common mistake to avoid when calculating tax revenue.
q.zh: 揀計稅收時最常見要避免嘅錯誤。

o.en: Multiplying the tax by the quantity.
Using the old quantity instead of the new quantity.
o.zh: 用咗原本數量而唔係新成交量。

o.en: Revenue uses Qt after the tax.
Checking that burdens add up to revenue.
o.zh: 驗算負擔加埋等於稅收。

t.en: Aims and effectiveness of taxes and subsidies
t.zh: 稅同補貼嘅目的同成效

hook.en: Hong Kong today: the government taxes cigarettes partly to reduce smoking. Many smokers keep smoking after price rises.
hook.zh: 今日香港：政府對香煙徵稅，部分目的係減少吸煙。好多煙民加價之後照食。

q.en: If demand for cigarettes is inelastic, a tax will…
q.zh: 如果香煙 demand 缺乏彈性，徵稅會…

o.en: raise a lot of revenue but cut smoking only a little
o.zh: 收到好多稅，但吸煙只減少一點

o.en: cut smoking a lot but raise little revenue
o.zh: 大幅減少吸煙，但稅收少

w.en: Inelastic: quantity falls little, so revenue stays high.
w.zh: 缺乏彈性：數量跌得少，所以稅收高。

d.en: A unit tax can reduce consumption (e.g. of cigarettes): the more elastic demand is, the more quantity falls. When demand is inelastic, the tax raises much revenue but quantity falls little. A unit subsidy encourages production or consumption, but costs government money.
d.zh: 徵 unit tax 可以減少消費（例如香煙）：demand 越 elastic，數量跌得越多；demand inelastic 時稅收多但數量跌得少。Unit subsidy 用嚟鼓勵生產或消費，要政府出錢。

p.en: The same tax cannot both raise maximum revenue and cut consumption the most.
p.zh: 同一個稅好難同時做到稅收最多同消費減得最多。

s.en: Aim to cut smoking → works better when demand is elastic.
s.zh: 目的係減少吸煙 → demand 越 elastic 越有效。

s.en: Aim to raise revenue → works better when demand is inelastic.
s.zh: 目的係增加稅收 → demand 越 inelastic 越有效。

s.en: Cigarette demand is fairly inelastic, so the tax raises revenue more than it cuts smoking.
s.zh: 香煙 demand 頗缺乏彈性，所以稅收效果大過減少吸煙。

q.en: A subsidy aims to raise the use of electric buses. It works best when…
q.zh: 補貼想增加電動巴士嘅使用。幾時最有效？

o.zh: demand 同 supply 都富彈性

o.en: demand and supply are perfectly inelastic
o.zh: demand 同 supply 完全缺乏彈性

w.en: Elastic responses mean quantity rises more.
w.zh: 反應越有彈性，數量升得越多。

q.en: Pick the best judgement about a tax on cigarettes.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅煙稅判斷。

o.en: Because demand is inelastic, it raises much revenue but reduces smoking only a little.
o.zh: 因為 demand 缺乏彈性，稅收多但吸煙只減少一點。

o.en: It has no effect at all.
Inelastic demand means many keep buying.
o.zh: 缺乏彈性代表好多人照買。

chain.zh: 從量稅令 supply 上移
從量補貼令 supply 下移

chain.en: Calculate revenue and burdens with the new Qt
chain.zh: 用新 Qt 計稅收同負擔

q.en: Pe $20; after a $5 tax, Pc $23, Qt 50. Consumer burden is…
q.zh: Pe $20；徵 $5 稅後 Pc $23、Qt 50。消費者負擔係…

q.en: Supply is perfectly inelastic. A unit tax is borne…
q.zh: Supply 完全缺乏彈性。從量稅由…

w.en: The less elastic side bears all.
w.zh: 彈性最低嗰方負擔全部。

q.en: A unit subsidy to sellers makes Pp…
q.zh: 向賣家發從量補貼，Pp 會…

w.en: Pp = Pc + subsidy, above old Pe.
w.zh: Pp = Pc + 補貼，高過原本 Pe。

q.en: In your own words: why does the less elastic side bear more of a tax?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解彈性較低嘅一方負擔較多稅款？

ck.en: I said the less elastic side cannot easily change its quantity.
ck.zh: 我有講彈性低嘅一方難以改變數量。

ck.en: I said the price moves more against that side.
ck.zh: 我有講價格對嗰一方嘅不利變動較大。

ck.en: I gave an example such as cigarettes.
ck.zh: 我有舉例，例如香煙。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) At Mei Ho House, Shek Kip Mei, in 2026, Ah Ying would pay at most $30 for her 1st cup of milk tea, $20 for the 2nd and $12 for the 3rd.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年石硤尾美荷樓，阿瑩第 1 杯奶茶最多肯俾 $30，第 2 杯 $20，第 3 杯 $12。

q.en: What is her total benefit (TB) from 3 cups?
q.zh: 3 杯奶茶嘅總利益（TB）係幾多？

d.en: Marginal benefit (MB) is the most a consumer is willing to pay for one more unit; it usually diminishes. The demand curve is the MB curve. Total benefit (TB) = the sum of MB of all units consumed.
d.zh: Marginal benefit（MB）係消費者為多一單位最多願意付嘅錢，通常遞減。Demand curve 就係 MB curve。Total benefit（TB）= 所有已消費單位嘅 MB 加埋。

p.en: MB falls because each extra cup satisfies her less.
p.zh: MB 遞減，因為每多一杯帶嚟嘅滿足感少咗。

s.en: MB: $30, $20, $12 → diminishing.
TB of 2 cups = $50; TB of 3 cups = $62.
Plot MB against cups and you get her demand curve.
s.zh: 將 MB 對杯數畫出嚟，就係佢嘅 demand curve。

q.en: Why is the demand curve the MB curve?
q.zh: 點解 demand curve 就係 MB curve？

o.en: At each quantity it shows the most the buyer will pay for one more unit.
o.zh: 喺每個數量，佢顯示買家為多一單位最多願意付幾多。
因為買家付嘅就係佢哋嘅 MB。
因為 MB 永遠係零。
因為 demand 包括成本。

w.en: Willingness to pay for each unit traces the demand curve.
w.zh: 對每單位嘅最高付款意願就係 demand curve。

q.en: Pick the best definition of marginal benefit.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 marginal benefit 定義。

o.en: The most a consumer is willing to pay for one more unit.
o.zh: 消費者為多一單位最多願意付嘅錢。

o.en: Willingness to pay at the margin.
Price paid can be below MB.

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Milk tea at Mei Ho House sells for $12 a cup. Ah Ying’s MB for cups 1–3 is $30, $20, $12.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）美荷樓奶茶每杯 $12。阿瑩第 1–3 杯嘅 MB 係 $30、$20、$12。

q.en: What is her consumer surplus from buying 3 cups?
q.zh: 佢買 3 杯嘅消費者盈餘係幾多？

d.en: Consumer surplus (CS) = TB − TE = the sum of (MB − P) for every unit bought; the area below the demand curve and above the price. When price falls, CS increases.
d.zh: Consumer surplus（CS）= TB − TE = 每個買咗嘅單位 (MB − P) 加埋；即係 demand curve 以下、價格以上嘅面積。價格下跌，CS 增加。

p.en: TE (total expenditure) = P × Q = 12 × 3 = $36.

t.zh: 兩種方法得出 $26（虛構數字）

s.en: Unit by unit: 18 + 8 + 0 = $26.
If the price falls to $10, CS rises: 20 + 10 + 2 = $32.

q.en: On a diagram, consumer surplus is the area…
q.zh: 圖上，消費者盈餘係…嘅面積

o.en: below the demand curve and above the price
o.zh: demand curve 以下、價格以上

o.en: above the supply curve and below the price
o.zh: supply curve 以上、價格以下

w.en: Willingness to pay above what is paid.
w.zh: 肯俾嘅錢減實付。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of consumer surplus.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅消費者盈餘解釋。

o.en: The money sellers earn above cost.
o.zh: 賣家收入高過成本嘅部分。

o.en: The difference between what buyers are willing to pay and what they actually pay, summed over units bought.
o.zh: 買家願意付同實際付之間嘅差額，所有買咗嘅單位加埋。

t.zh: 邊際成本同生產者盈餘

hook.en: (Fictional figures) A Shek Kip Mei milk-tea stall in a competitive market sells at $12. Its MC for cups 1–3 is $4, $7, $12, and its daily TFC is $5.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）石硤尾一個奶茶檔喺競爭市場以 $12 出售。第 1–3 杯嘅 MC 係 $4、$7、$12，每日 TFC 係 $5。

q.en: What is its producer surplus from 3 cups?
q.zh: 3 杯嘅生產者盈餘係幾多？

d.en: In perfect competition the supply curve is the MC curve. Producer surplus (PS) = TR − TVC = the sum of (P − MC) for every unit = profit + TFC; the area below the price and above the supply curve. PS is not the same as profit.
d.zh: Perfect competition 下 supply curve 就係 MC curve。Producer surplus（PS）= TR − TVC = 每單位 (P − MC) 加埋 = profit + TFC；即係價格以下、supply curve 以上嘅面積。PS 唔等於 profit。

t.zh: PS vs 利潤（虛構數字）

s.en: PS = profit + TFC = 8 + 5 = $13.

q.en: Which is correct?
q.zh: 以下邊句啱？

w.en: PS deducts only variable cost.
w.zh: PS 只減可變成本。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is PS not the same as profit?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解 PS 唔等於利潤？

o.zh: PS 包括消費者嘅得益。

o.en: Profit is always larger than PS.
PS subtracts only variable cost (TVC); profit subtracts total cost, including TFC.
o.zh: PS 只減可變成本（TVC）；利潤要減總成本，包括 TFC。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Shek Kip Mei, 2026: for one market for milk tea, the MB of each cup falls and the MC of each cup rises.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年石硤尾奶茶市場：每杯嘅 MB 遞減，每杯嘅 MC 遞增。

q.en: Up to which cup should society produce to make total social surplus largest?
q.zh: 社會應該生產到第幾杯，社會總盈餘先最大？

w.en: Every cup with MB > MC adds surplus; stop where MB = MC.
w.zh: 每杯 MB > MC 都增加盈餘；去到 MB = MC 就停。

d.en: Total social surplus (TSS) = CS + PS = Σ(MB − MC). TSS is largest (efficiency) at the quantity where MB = MC. Efficient does not mean equitable (fair).
d.zh: Total social surplus（TSS）= CS + PS = Σ(MB − MC)。TSS 最大 = efficiency，即係生產到 MB = MC 嘅數量。Efficient 唔等於 equitable（公平）。

p.en: In a competitive market without intervention, equilibrium is where MB = MC.
p.zh: 冇干預嘅競爭市場，均衡點就係 MB = MC。

s.en: Produce while MB ≥ MC: 3 cups, TSS = 26 + 13 + 2 = $41. A 4th cup would subtract $8.
s.zh: MB ≥ MC 就生產：3 杯，TSS = 26 + 13 + 2 = $41。第 4 杯會減少 $8。

q.en: Which statement is correct?
q.zh: 以下邊句啱？

o.en: TSS is largest where MB is highest.
o.zh: MB 最高時 TSS 最大。

o.en: An efficient outcome may not be fair.
o.zh: 有效率嘅結果未必公平。

o.en: Efficiency means everyone gets the same amount.
o.zh: 效率即係每人得到一樣多。

w.en: Efficiency is about total surplus, not how it is shared.
w.zh: 效率講總盈餘，唔講點分。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of efficiency.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅效率解釋。

o.en: Producing the quantity where MB = MC, so total social surplus is as large as possible.
o.zh: 生產到 MB = MC 嘅數量，令社會總盈餘最大。

o.en: Making the price as low as possible.
Low price is not the test.
Units with MC > MB lower TSS.
o.zh: MC > MB 嘅單位會減少 TSS。

t.en: Deadweight loss and the functions of price
t.zh: 無謂損失同價格嘅功能

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Same Shek Kip Mei milk-tea market (MB: 30, 20, 14, 8; MC: 4, 7, 12, 16): what if output stops at 2 cups, or is pushed to 4, instead of the efficient 3?
hook.zh: （虛構數字）同一個石硤尾奶茶市場（MB：30、20、14、8；MC：4、7、12、16）：如果產量停喺 2 杯，或者推到 4 杯，而唔係有效率嘅 3 杯，會點？

q.en: If only 2 cups are made, is surplus lost?
q.zh: 如果只整 2 杯，會唔會損失盈餘？

o.en: No, fewer cups always save resources.
o.zh: 唔會，整少啲一定慳資源。

o.en: Yes. The 3rd cup had MB $14 > MC $12, so $2 of surplus is lost.
o.zh: 會。第 3 杯 MB $14 > MC $12，損失咗 $2 盈餘。

w.en: Not producing a unit with MB > MC loses surplus.
w.zh: 唔生產 MB > MC 嘅單位會損失盈餘。

d.en: Under-production (Q < Q*): the missing units have MB > MC. Over-production (Q > Q*): the extra units have MC > MB. Both reduce TSS; the reduction is deadweight loss. Price has a rationing function (deciding who gets the good) and an allocative function (guiding resources to their uses).
d.zh: Under-production（Q < Q*）：少咗嘅單位 MB > MC；over-production（Q > Q*）：多出嘅單位 MC > MB。兩者都令 TSS 減少，減少嘅部分叫 deadweight loss。價格有 rationing function（決定邊個得到貨品）同 allocative function（引導資源用途）。

p.en: Deadweight loss is surplus nobody gets.
p.zh: Deadweight loss 係冇人得到嘅盈餘。

p.en: Price rations the good to those willing to pay it, and signals sellers how much to make.
p.zh: 價格將貨品分配俾肯付嗰個價嘅人，亦話俾賣家知要生產幾多。

s.en: Efficient Q* = 3: TSS $41.
s.zh: 有效率 Q* = 3：TSS $41。

s.en: Under-production at 2: the 3rd cup’s $2 is lost → DWL $2.
s.zh: 生產不足（2 杯）：損失第 3 杯嘅 $2 → DWL $2。

s.en: Over-production at 4: the 4th cup has MC 16 > MB 8 → DWL $8.
s.zh: 過度生產（4 杯）：第 4 杯 MC 16 > MB 8 → DWL $8。

q.en: Over-production means the extra units have…
q.zh: 過度生產代表多出嘅單位…

w.en: Each extra unit costs more than it is worth to buyers.
w.zh: 每個多出嘅單位成本高過佢對買家嘅價值。

q.en: Pick the best description of the allocative function of price.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅價格 allocative function 描述。

o.en: Price signals guide resources to the uses where they are most wanted.
o.zh: 價格訊號引導資源去最需要佢嘅用途。

o.en: Price decides which buyer gets the good.
o.zh: 價格決定邊個買家得到貨品。

chain.en: MB curve = demand; MC curve = supply
CS = Σ(MB − P); PS = Σ(P − MC)
Too much or too little → deadweight loss
chain.zh: 太多或太少 → 無謂損失

q.en: (Fictional figures) MB of 1st–2nd unit: $15, $9; price $9. CS is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）第 1–2 單位 MB：$15、$9；價格 $9。CS 係…

q.en: PS equals…
q.zh: PS 等於…

w.en: TR − TVC.
w.zh: TR − TVC。

q.en: Total social surplus is largest where…
q.zh: 社會總盈餘喺…最大

w.en: Efficiency.
w.zh: 效率。

q.en: In your own words: why does producing beyond MB = MC create deadweight loss?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解生產超過 MB = MC 會造成無謂損失？

ck.en: I said the extra units have MC > MB.
ck.zh: 我有講多出嘅單位 MC > MB。

ck.en: I said each such unit lowers total social surplus.
ck.zh: 我有講每個咁嘅單位都令社會總盈餘減少。

ck.en: I named the lost surplus deadweight loss.
ck.zh: 我有將損失嘅盈餘叫做 deadweight loss。

t.en: Deadweight loss of a price ceiling

hook.en: (Fictional policy and figures) Hung Hom, 2013, in this game scenario: rents of small flats are capped at $8,000 a month. Without the cap, Pe = $10,000 and 100 flats are let.
hook.zh: （虛構政策同數字）2013 年紅磡，喺呢個遊戲情境：細單位月租上限 $8,000。冇上限時 Pe = $10,000，租出 100 個單位。

q.en: Under the cap only 80 flats are let. For the 81st–100th flats, how do MB and MC compare?
q.zh: 有上限之後只租出 80 個單位。第 81–100 個單位嘅 MB 同 MC 點比較？

w.en: Those units were worth more to tenants than they cost to supply, but they are no longer let.
w.zh: 嗰啲單位對租客嘅價值高過供應成本，但而家冇租出。

d.en: An effective price ceiling cuts quantity from Qe to Qs. Units between Qs and Qe have MB > MC but are not produced: under-production, deadweight loss, and TSS falls. PS must fall; the change in CS is uncertain (a lower price helps, buying less hurts).
d.zh: 有效嘅 price ceiling 令成交量由 Qe 跌到 Qs，Qs 同 Qe 之間嗰啲單位 MB > MC 但冇生產，係 under-production，出現 deadweight loss，TSS 減少。PS 一定減少；CS 點變就唔確定（平咗得益，但買少咗損失）。

p.en: DWL = ½ × (Qe − Qs) × (MB − MC at Qs) for straight-line curves.
p.zh: 直線曲線下：DWL = ½ × (Qe − Qs) × (Qs 位置嘅 MB − MC)。

s.en: At Qs = 80, tenants would pay up to $12,000 (MB); landlords need $8,000 (MC).
s.zh: Qs = 80 時，租客最多肯俾 $12,000（MB）；業主要 $8,000（MC）。

s.en: Landlords get a lower rent on fewer flats → PS falls for sure.
s.zh: 業主租金低咗、租出少咗 → PS 一定減少。

q.en: Under an effective price ceiling, which is certain?
q.zh: 有效價格上限下，邊樣係肯定？

w.en: CS may rise or fall; PS and TSS fall.
w.zh: CS 可升可跌；PS 同 TSS 一定跌。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is the change in CS uncertain under a ceiling?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解價格上限下 CS 嘅變化唔確定？

o.en: Remaining buyers pay less (gain), but some units are no longer bought (loss).
o.zh: 留低嘅買家付少咗（得益），但有啲單位冇得買（損失）。

o.en: Because consumers never gain from low prices.
o.zh: 因為消費者從來唔會因低價得益。

o.en: They do gain on units still bought.

o.zh: 因為 CS 一定等於 PS。

t.en: Deadweight loss of a price floor

hook.en: (Fictional policy and figures) Hung Hom pier, 2013, in this game scenario: a minimum price of $50 a kilo is set for fresh fish whose Pe is $40; 1,000 kg were sold before, 800 kg after.
hook.zh: （虛構政策同數字）2013 年紅磡碼頭，喺呢個遊戲情境：鮮魚定最低價每公斤 $50，原本 Pe = $40；之前賣 1,000 公斤，之後賣 800 公斤。

q.en: Which side certainly loses surplus?
q.zh: 邊一方一定損失盈餘？

w.en: Buyers pay more and buy less, so CS falls for sure.
w.zh: 買家付多咗又買少咗，CS 一定減少。

d.en: An effective price floor cuts quantity from Qe to Qd: under-production with deadweight loss. CS must fall; the change in PS is uncertain (a higher price helps, selling less hurts). A minimum wage above the market wage has the same effect.
d.zh: 有效嘅 price floor 令成交量由 Qe 跌到 Qd，係 under-production，有 deadweight loss。CS 一定減少；PS 點變唔確定（貴咗得益，但賣少咗損失）。Minimum wage 定喺市場工資以上都會有同樣效果。

p.en: Mirror image of a price ceiling.
p.zh: 同價格上限係鏡像。

s.en: At Qd = 800, MB = $50 and MC = $30.
Fishermen gain on 800 kg at a higher price but lose the other 200 kg: PS uncertain.
s.zh: 漁民 800 公斤賣貴咗，但少賣 200 公斤：PS 不確定。

q.en: Under an effective price floor, which is certain?
q.zh: 有效價格下限下，邊樣係肯定？

w.en: CS falls; PS uncertain; TSS falls.
w.zh: CS 減少；PS 不確定；TSS 減少。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of the DWL under a price floor.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅價格下限無謂損失解釋。

o.en: Units between Qd and Qe have MB > MC but are no longer traded.
o.zh: Qd 同 Qe 之間嘅單位 MB > MC，但冇再成交。

o.en: Too much is produced and sold.
Less is sold under a floor.

hook.en: (Fictional policy and figures) Hung Hom market, 2013, in this game scenario: imports of a vegetable are limited to 70 crates a day. Without the quota, 100 crates were sold.
hook.zh: （虛構政策同數字）2013 年紅磡街市，喺呢個遊戲情境：某種蔬菜每日進口限 70 箱。冇配額時賣 100 箱。

q.en: Does total social surplus fall under the quota?
q.zh: 配額下社會總盈餘會唔會減少？

w.en: Crates 71–100 had MB > MC but are not traded.
w.zh: 第 71–100 箱 MB > MC，但冇成交。

d.en: An effective quota cuts quantity to the quota and raises price: under-production with deadweight loss. CS must fall; quota holders’ PS may rise (quota rent); TSS must fall.
d.zh: 有效嘅 quota 令成交量跌到配額數量，價格上升，係 under-production，有 deadweight loss。CS 一定減少；持有配額嘅賣家 PS 可能增加（quota rent），TSS 一定減少。

p.en: Quota rent: extra income from selling the limited quantity at a higher price.
p.zh: Quota rent：以較高價賣有限數量帶嚟嘅額外收入。

s.en: At Q = 70, MB = $14 a crate, MC = $8.
Quota holders sell 70 crates at a higher price: their PS may rise.
s.zh: 持有配額嘅賣家以較高價賣 70 箱：PS 可能增加。

q.en: Under an effective quota, which is certain?
q.zh: 有效配額下，邊樣係肯定？

w.en: Buyers pay more for less; PS may rise.
w.zh: 買家付多咗買少咗；PS 可能增加。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of quota rent.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 quota rent 解釋。

o.en: The extra income quota holders earn because the quota pushes the price up.
o.zh: 因為配額推高價格，持有人賺到嘅額外收入。

o.en: Scarcity value of the right to sell.
The rent paid for a market stall.
A tax paid to the government.

t.en: Deadweight loss of a unit tax

hook.en: (Fictional policy and figures) Whampoa, Hung Hom, 2013, in this game scenario: a $4 unit tax on a drink cuts sales from 100 to 80 a day; the government collects $320.
hook.zh: （虛構政策同數字）2013 年紅磡黃埔，喺呢個遊戲情境：某飲品徵 $4 從量稅，每日銷量由 100 跌到 80；政府收 $320。
