q.en: Is the $320 of tax revenue a loss to society?
q.zh: $320 稅收係咪社會嘅損失？

o.en: Yes, all of it is lost.
No, it is transferred to the government.

w.en: Revenue moves from buyers and sellers to the government.
w.zh: 稅收由買賣雙方轉去政府。

d.en: A unit tax reduces quantity: under-production. With a tax, TSS = CS + PS + tax revenue; tax revenue is only a transfer from buyers and sellers to the government, not a loss. The real loss is the deadweight-loss triangle. The more elastic demand or supply, the larger the DWL.
d.zh: Unit tax 令成交量減少，係 under-production。有稅嘅時候 TSS = CS + PS + tax revenue；稅收只係由買賣雙方轉移去政府，唔係損失。真正嘅損失係 deadweight loss 三角形。Demand 或 supply 越 elastic，DWL 越大。

p.en: DWL = ½ × tax × fall in quantity, for straight-line curves.
p.zh: 直線曲線下：DWL = ½ × 稅款 × 數量跌幅。

s.en: Quantity falls 100 → 80.
Revenue $4 × 80 = $320: a transfer.
DWL = ½ × 4 × 20 = $40: the real loss.
s.zh: DWL = ½ × 4 × 20 = $40：真正損失。

q.en: Which makes the DWL of a unit tax LARGER?
q.zh: 以下邊樣令從量稅嘅 DWL 更大？

w.en: More elastic → quantity falls more → bigger triangle.
w.zh: 越有彈性 → 數量跌得越多 → 三角形越大。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is tax revenue not counted as a loss?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解稅收唔計做損失？

o.en: A value judgement, not the reason.
It is a transfer to the government, which can use it; only the lost trades are a loss.
o.zh: 佢轉移咗俾政府，政府可以用；只有冇發生嘅交易先係損失。

o.en: Because buyers do not pay any of it.
o.zh: 因為買家冇負擔任何稅款。

t.en: Deadweight loss of a unit subsidy

hook.en: (Fictional policy and figures) Whampoa, 2013, in this game scenario: a $2 subsidy per unit raises sales of a snack from 100 to 120 a day.
hook.zh: （虛構政策同數字）2013 年黃埔，喺呢個遊戲情境：每單位 $2 補貼令某小食每日銷量由 100 升到 120。

q.en: For units 101–120, how do MC and MB compare?
q.zh: 第 101–120 單位嘅 MC 同 MB 點比較？

w.en: Beyond Qe, each extra unit costs more than buyers value it.
w.zh: 超過 Qe，每個多出嘅單位成本高過買家對佢嘅評價。

d.en: A unit subsidy raises quantity above Qe; the extra units have MC > MB: over-production with deadweight loss. CS and PS both rise, but the government’s subsidy spending is larger than their gains together. TSS = CS + PS − subsidy expenditure, so TSS falls.
d.zh: Unit subsidy 令成交量增加到 Qe 以上，多出嚟嗰啲單位 MC > MB，係 over-production，有 deadweight loss。CS 同 PS 都增加，但政府補貼開支大過兩者增幅，TSS = CS + PS − subsidy expenditure，TSS 減少。

p.en: A subsidy can still be justified for other aims (e.g. a positive externality), but in a market with no externality it lowers TSS.
p.zh: 補貼可以為咗其他目的（例如 positive externality），但冇外部性嘅市場會令 TSS 減少。

s.en: Subsidy spending = $2 × 120 = $240.
CS + PS rise by $220 together.
s.zh: CS 同 PS 合共增加 $220。

q.en: With a unit subsidy, TSS equals…
q.zh: 有從量補貼時，TSS 等於…

w.en: The subsidy is paid by taxpayers, so it is subtracted.
w.zh: 補貼由納稅人支付，所以要減。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of over-production under a subsidy.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅補貼下過度生產解釋。

o.en: The subsidy encourages units whose MC is greater than their MB.
o.zh: 補貼鼓勵生產 MC 大過 MB 嘅單位。

chain.en: Free market: MB = MC, TSS largest
chain.zh: 自由市場：MB = MC，TSS 最大

chain.en: Ceiling, floor, quota, tax → too little
chain.zh: 上限、下限、配額、稅 → 太少

chain.en: Tax revenue is a transfer, not a loss

q.en: Under an effective price ceiling, PS…
q.zh: 有效價格上限下，PS…

w.en: Lower price, fewer units.
w.zh: 價低、量少。

q.en: A unit tax of $5 cuts quantity from 60 to 50 (straight-line curves). DWL is…
q.zh: $5 從量稅令數量由 60 跌到 50（直線曲線）。DWL 係…

q.en: A unit subsidy causes…
q.zh: 從量補貼引致…

o.en: a surplus that the government buys

w.en: Quantity above Qe.
w.zh: 數量高過 Qe。

q.en: In your own words: why do both a unit tax and a unit subsidy create deadweight loss?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解從量稅同從量補貼都會造成無謂損失？

ck.en: I said the tax leads to too little output (MB > MC units lost).
ck.zh: 我有講稅令產量太少（損失 MB > MC 嘅單位）。

ck.en: I said the subsidy leads to too much output (MC > MB units added).
ck.zh: 我有講補貼令產量太多（加咗 MC > MB 嘅單位）。

ck.en: I said both move output away from MB = MC.
ck.zh: 我有講兩者都令產量偏離 MB = MC。

hook.en: Hung Hom today: traffic queuing for the Cross-Harbour Tunnel adds exhaust fumes and delays for other people on the roads nearby.
hook.zh: 今日紅磡：排隊入紅隧嘅車龍為附近嘅人帶嚟廢氣同延誤。

q.en: Do drivers pay residents for the fumes they breathe?
q.zh: 司機有冇賠償附近居民吸入嘅廢氣？

w.en: A cost falls on third parties without compensation: a negative externality.
w.zh: 第三者承受成本而冇補償：負外部性。

d.en: A negative externality: production or consumption imposes a cost on third parties who are not compensated. Social cost = private cost + external cost (MSC = MPC + MEC). The market only counts MPC, so it over-produces.
d.zh: Negative externality：生產或消費令第三者承受成本，但唔使賠償。Social cost = private cost + external cost，即 MSC = MPC + MEC。市場只睇 MPC，所以會 over-production。

p.en: Third party: someone outside the transaction.
p.zh: 第三者：交易以外嘅人。

s.en: Private cost to the driver: fuel, toll, time = $100.
s.zh: 司機嘅私人成本：油、隧道費、時間 = $100。

s.en: External cost to others: fumes and extra delay = $30.
s.zh: 其他人承受嘅外部成本：廢氣同延誤 = $30。

s.en: Social cost = $130, but the driver decides on $100 → too many trips.
s.zh: 社會成本 = $130，但司機只按 $100 決定 → 車程太多。

q.en: With a negative externality, a free market produces…
q.zh: 有負外部性時，自由市場會生產…

w.en: It ignores the external cost, so MPC < MSC.
w.zh: 佢忽略咗外部成本，所以 MPC < MSC。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does the market over-produce with a negative externality?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解有負外部性時市場會過度生產？

o.en: Decision-makers count only private cost, which is below social cost.
o.zh: 決策者只計私人成本，而私人成本低過社會成本。

o.en: Because third parties want more of it.

hook.en: Hong Kong today: when Ah Ying gets a flu vaccine, she protects herself and also lowers the chance that classmates catch flu from her.
hook.zh: 今日香港：阿瑩打流感針，保護自己之餘，亦減低同學被佢傳染嘅機會。

q.en: Do her classmates pay her for this benefit?
q.zh: 同學有冇為呢個好處俾錢佢？

w.en: A benefit to third parties without payment: a positive externality.
w.zh: 第三者得益而冇付錢：正外部性。

d.en: A positive externality: production or consumption benefits third parties who do not pay. Social benefit = private benefit + external benefit (MSB = MPB + MEB). The market only counts MPB, so it under-produces.
d.zh: Positive externality：生產或消費令第三者得益，但唔使俾錢。Social benefit = private benefit + external benefit，即 MSB = MPB + MEB。市場只睇 MPB，所以會 under-production。

p.en: Examples: vaccination, education, a beautiful garden others can see.
p.zh: 例子：疫苗、教育、其他人睇到嘅靚花園。

s.en: Private benefit to Ah Ying: $150; price $200 → she might not get it.
s.zh: 阿瑩嘅私人得益：$150；價錢 $200 → 佢可能唔打。

s.en: External benefit to others: $100 → social benefit $250 > $200.
s.zh: 其他人嘅外部得益：$100 → 社會得益 $250 > $200。

s.en: Society wants this shot, but the market alone may not deliver it → under-production.
s.zh: 社會想佢打，但單靠市場未必做到 → 生產不足。

q.en: Which is a positive externality?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係正外部性？

o.en: A homeowner’s rooftop garden that neighbours enjoy looking at
o.zh: 鄰居可以欣賞嘅天台花園

o.en: Your own enjoyment of your lunch

w.en: Neighbours benefit without paying.
w.zh: 鄰居得益而唔使俾錢。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why does the market under-produce with a positive externality?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解有正外部性時市場會生產不足？

o.en: Because third parties pay too much.
Buyers count only private benefit, which is below social benefit.
o.zh: 買家只計私人得益，而私人得益低過社會得益。

hook.en: Hong Kong, 31 December 2022: the plastic shopping bag charge rose from at least 50 cents to at least $1 a bag.
hook.zh: 2022 年 12 月 31 日：香港膠袋收費由每個最少 5 毫加到最少 $1。

stops.src: Environmental Protection Department, Enhanced Plastic Shopping Bag Charging Scheme

q.en: What is the levy trying to do?
q.zh: 徵費想做到乜？

o.en: Raise the price of all goods
Make shoppers face more of the external cost of plastic bags
o.zh: 令購物者承擔更多膠袋嘅外部成本

w.en: A charge raises the private cost towards the social cost.
w.zh: 收費令私人成本接近社會成本。

d.en: Ways governments deal with externalities: taxes or charges (e.g. the plastic bag levy), regulation, subsidies, government provision, patents and copyright, and public education. Each has limits, e.g. it is hard to measure external cost accurately.
d.zh: 政府處理 externality 嘅方法：徵稅或收費（例如膠袋徵費）、法例管制、補貼、政府提供、專利同版權、公眾教育。每種方法都有限制，例如好難準確量度 external cost。

p.en: Negative externality → tax, charge or regulation; positive externality → subsidy or provision.
p.zh: 負外部性 → 稅、收費或管制；正外部性 → 補貼或政府提供。

s.en: Plastic bags (negative) → a charge per bag.
s.zh: 膠袋（負外部性）→ 按個收費。

s.en: Vaccines (positive) → free or subsidised shots.
s.zh: 疫苗（正外部性）→ 免費或資助接種。

s.en: Limit: nobody knows the exact external cost, so the right levy is hard to set.
s.zh: 限制：冇人知外部成本準確係幾多，所以好難定啱嘅徵費。

q.en: Which tool fits a POSITIVE externality best?
q.zh: 以下邊個工具最適合處理正外部性？

w.en: A subsidy raises the private benefit towards the social benefit.
w.zh: 補貼令私人得益接近社會得益。

q.en: Pick the best limitation of using a tax to correct a negative externality.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅以稅糾正負外部性嘅限制。

o.en: It is hard to measure the external cost, so the tax may be set too high or too low.
o.zh: 外部成本好難量度，稅可能定得太高或太低。

o.en: Taxes always remove the externality completely.
o.zh: 稅一定可以完全消除外部性。

hook.en: (Fictional) Hung Hom, 2026: a restaurant’s kitchen exhaust blows into the flat upstairs. The two sides meet and agree that the restaurant fits a filter, paid for partly by the resident.
hook.zh: （虛構）2026 年紅磡：一間餐廳嘅廚房抽氣吹入樓上單位。兩邊傾掂，由餐廳裝過濾器，住客出部分錢。

q.en: Why could they solve it without the government?
q.zh: 點解佢哋唔使政府都解決到？

o.en: Only two parties, clear rights, low cost of negotiating
o.zh: 只有兩方、權利清楚、傾嘅成本低

w.en: Few parties and clear property rights make bargaining easy.
w.zh: 涉及嘅人少、產權清楚，議價就容易。

d.en: Market solutions: when property rights are clearly defined and transaction costs are low, those affected and those causing the externality can bargain (market exchange), internalising the external cost. Mergers or acquisitions can also internalise it. With many parties and high transaction costs, this rarely works.
d.zh: 市場方法：產權清楚界定、交易成本低，受影響嘅人同製造 externality 嘅人可以自己傾（market exchange），將外部成本內部化；合併或收購亦可以。牽涉人數多、交易成本高就好難成功。

p.en: Transaction costs: the time and money needed to find, negotiate with and enforce agreements with the other side.
p.zh: 交易成本：搵對方、傾同執行協議所需嘅時間同金錢。

t.en: Why it works here, but not for tunnel fumes
t.zh: 點解呢度得，但隧道廢氣唔得

s.en: Restaurant vs one flat: two parties, easy to meet → bargain works.
s.zh: 餐廳 vs 一個單位：兩方、容易見面 → 議價成功。

s.en: Tunnel traffic vs thousands of residents: too many parties → transaction costs too high.
s.zh: 隧道車流 vs 幾千個居民：人太多 → 交易成本太高。

s.en: So the tunnel case needs government action instead.
s.zh: 所以隧道個案要靠政府出手。

q.en: Market solutions are LEAST likely to work when…
q.zh: 市場方法最難成功嘅情況係…

o.en: many people are affected and transaction costs are high
o.zh: 受影響嘅人好多、交易成本高

w.en: High transaction costs block bargaining.
w.zh: 交易成本高會阻礙議價。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of “internalising” an externality.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅「內部化」外部性解釋。

o.en: Making the decision-maker take the external cost or benefit into account.
o.zh: 令決策者將外部成本或得益計入考慮。

t.zh: 有外部性時嘅效率：MSB = MSC

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Hung Hom pier, 2026: a ferry service’s engines pollute the harbour. The market runs 12 trips a day, but counting the pollution, 10 would be efficient.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年紅磡碼頭：渡輪引擎污染海港。市場每日行 12 班，但計埋污染，10 班先有效率。

q.en: What is the efficient number of trips here?
q.zh: 呢度有效率嘅班次係幾多？

w.en: Efficiency counts social, not private, costs and benefits.
w.zh: 效率要計社會而唔係私人嘅成本同得益。

d.en: With externalities, the free market produces where MPB = MPC, but efficient output is where MSB = MSC. Negative externality → market output too high (over-production); positive externality → too low (under-production). Both create deadweight loss.
d.zh: 有 externality 時，自由市場產量喺 MPB = MPC，但 efficient output 喺 MSB = MSC。Negative externality → 市場產量太多（over-production）；positive externality → 太少（under-production）；兩者都有 deadweight loss。

p.en: Without externalities, MPB = MSB and MPC = MSC, so the market is efficient.
p.zh: 冇外部性時 MPB = MSB、MPC = MSC，市場就有效率。

s.en: Market: MPB = MPC at 12 trips.
s.zh: 市場：MPB = MPC 喺 12 班。

s.en: Add external cost: MSC rises above MPC; MSB = MSC at 10 trips.
s.zh: 加埋外部成本：MSC 高過 MPC；MSB = MSC 喺 10 班。

s.en: Trips 11–12 have MSC > MSB → deadweight loss.
s.zh: 第 11–12 班 MSC > MSB → 無謂損失。

q.en: With a positive externality and no intervention, market output is…
q.zh: 有正外部性又冇干預，市場產量…

w.en: MPB < MSB, so too little is produced.
w.zh: MPB < MSB，生產太少。

q.en: Pick the best rule for efficiency with externalities.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅有外部性時嘅效率規則。

o.en: Produce as little as possible to avoid pollution.

o.zh: 零產量損失有用嘅班次。

o.en: Produce where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost.
Produce where private benefit equals private cost.
o.zh: 生產到私人得益 = 私人成本。

chain.en: Third parties bear costs or gain benefits
chain.zh: 第三者承受成本或得到好處

chain.en: MSC = MPC + MEC; MSB = MPB + MEB
Market: MPB = MPC → too much or too little
chain.zh: 市場：MPB = MPC → 太多或太少

chain.en: Fix by government tools or bargaining
chain.zh: 用政府工具或議價解決

q.en: Second-hand smoke is an example of…
q.zh: 二手煙係…

w.en: Non-smokers bear a cost.
w.zh: 非吸煙者承受成本。

q.en: MPC = $50, MEC = $20. MSC is…
q.zh: MPC = $50，MEC = $20。MSC 係…

w.en: MSC = MPC + MEC.
w.zh: MSC = MPC + MEC。

q.en: Bargaining between neighbours works best when…
q.zh: 鄰居之間議價最有效嘅情況係…

o.en: few parties and low transaction costs

w.en: Low transaction costs.
w.zh: 交易成本低。

q.en: In your own words: why does the plastic bag levy move the market towards efficiency?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解膠袋徵費會令市場更接近有效率？

ck.en: I said plastic bags have an external cost.
ck.zh: 我有講膠袋有外部成本。

ck.en: I said the levy raises the private cost towards the social cost.
ck.zh: 我有講徵費令私人成本接近社會成本。

ck.en: I said fewer bags are used, closer to MSB = MSC.
ck.zh: 我有講用少咗膠袋，接近 MSB = MSC。

hook.en: Central, 2016: in the same Exchange Square tower, an investment banker and an office cleaner earn very different incomes.
hook.zh: 2016 年中環：喺交易廣場同一座大廈入面，投資銀行家同寫字樓清潔工嘅收入相差好遠。

q.en: Which is the main reason the banker earns more?
q.zh: 銀行家收入較高嘅主要原因係乜？

o.en: More human capital and skills the market values highly
o.zh: 有更多 human capital，技能嘅市場價值高

o.en: The banker works in a taller building
o.zh: 銀行家喺高啲嘅大廈返工

w.en: Education, training and scarce skills earn more.
w.zh: 教育、培訓同稀缺技能收入較高。

d.en: Sources: talent and ability, human capital (education, training, experience), age, gender, the market value of skills, compensating differentials (unpleasant or dangerous jobs pay more), wage methods, wage discrimination, and unequal ownership of capital and property (rent, interest, dividends).
d.zh: 收入唔平均嘅來源：天賦同能力、human capital（教育、培訓、經驗）、年齡、性別、技能嘅市場價值、compensating differentials（厭惡性或危險工作要俾多啲人工）、工資計算方法、工資歧視，同埋資本同物業擁有權唔平均（租金、利息、股息）。

p.en: Property income adds to the gap: owners earn rent, interest and dividends.
p.zh: 物業收入會擴大差距：業主有租金、利息同股息。

t.zh: 中環嘅三份收入（2016 年）

s.en: Banker: years of training, scarce skills → high wage.
s.zh: 銀行家：多年培訓、技能稀缺 → 高工資。

s.en: Window cleaner on a skyscraper: dangerous job → paid more than an indoor cleaner (compensating differential).
s.zh: 摩天大廈外牆清潔工：危險工作 → 人工高過室內清潔工（compensating differential）。

s.en: A flat owner who rents out a unit: extra income from property.
s.zh: 將單位放租嘅業主：物業帶嚟額外收入。

q.en: A worker on night shifts is paid more than a day-shift worker in the same job. This is…
q.zh: 同一份工，夜更工人收入高過日更。呢個係…

w.en: Extra pay for unpleasant conditions.
w.zh: 因為工作條件差而多俾嘅人工。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of human capital.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 human capital 解釋。

o.en: The skills and knowledge a worker gains through education, training and experience.
o.zh: 工人透過教育、培訓同經驗獲得嘅技能同知識。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Five Central households earn $10k, $20k, $30k, $40k and $100k a month (total $200k).
hook.zh: （虛構數字）中環五個住戶每月收入 $10k、$20k、$30k、$40k、$100k（合共 $200k）。

q.en: What share of total income do the poorest 40% (two households) receive?
q.zh: 最窮嘅 40%（兩戶）佔總收入幾多？

d.en: Lorenz curve: the horizontal axis is the cumulative % of households ranked from poorest; the vertical axis is their cumulative % of income. The diagonal is the line of perfect equality. The more the curve bends away from the diagonal, the more unequal the distribution.
d.zh: Lorenz curve：橫軸係由最窮排起嘅住戶累積百分比，縱軸係佢哋所佔收入嘅累積百分比。對角線係 line of perfect equality；條曲線越彎、離對角線越遠，收入分配就越唔平均。

p.en: Always rank households from poorest to richest first.
p.zh: 一定要先由最窮排到最富。

s.en: The curve sits well below the diagonal: income is unequal.
s.zh: 曲線明顯喺對角線下面：收入唔平均。

q.en: If every household earned the same, the Lorenz curve would be…
q.zh: 如果每戶收入一樣，Lorenz curve 會係…

o.en: a curve far below the diagonal

w.en: Every x% of households would get x% of income.
w.zh: x% 住戶得到 x% 收入。

q.en: Pick the best reading of a Lorenz curve.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 Lorenz curve 解讀。

o.en: A higher curve means people are poorer.
The further the curve is from the diagonal, the more unequal the income distribution.
o.zh: 曲線離對角線越遠，收入分配越唔平均。

o.en: The diagonal shows the poorest households.
o.zh: 對角線代表最窮嘅住戶。

hook.en: Hong Kong, 2016 By-census: the Gini coefficient based on original monthly household income was 0.539, up from 0.537 in 2011.
hook.zh: 2016 年中期人口統計：按原本每月住戶收入計，香港嘅堅尼系數係 0.539，2011 年係 0.537。

stops.src: GovHK press release, 9 Jun 2017 (2016 Population By-census)

q.en: Did income distribution become more or less equal from 2011 to 2016 (original income)?
q.zh: 2011 至 2016 年（原本收入），收入分配變得較平均定較唔平均？

w.en: A higher Gini means more unequal; 0.537 → 0.539 is a slight rise.
w.zh: 堅尼系數越高越唔平均；0.537 → 0.539 係輕微上升。

d.en: Gini coefficient = A ÷ (A + B), where A is the area between the diagonal and the Lorenz curve, and B is the area under the curve. It ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality); higher means more unequal. It shows only the distribution of income, not living standards, and the same value can come from different distributions.
d.zh: Gini coefficient = A ÷ (A + B)，A 係對角線同 Lorenz curve 之間嘅面積，B 係曲線下面嘅面積。數值由 0（完全平均）到 1（完全唔平均），越大越唔平均。佢只睇收入分配，唔反映生活水平高低，同一個數值亦可以嚟自唔同嘅分配。

p.en: A rich and a poor economy can have the same Gini.
p.zh: 富裕同貧窮嘅經濟體系可以有一樣嘅堅尼系數。

s.en: 0.539 is between 0 and 1, closer to the unequal end than 0.3 would be.
s.zh: 0.539 喺 0 同 1 之間，比 0.3 更接近唔平均嗰端。

s.en: It says nothing about whether incomes are high or low.
s.zh: 佢冇話到收入高定低。

s.en: After taxes and social transfers, the 2016 figure was 0.473: lower.
s.zh: 計埋稅同社會福利轉移後，2016 年數字係 0.473：較低。

q.en: Which statement about the Gini coefficient is correct?
q.zh: 以下關於堅尼系數嘅描述，邊句啱？

o.en: A value of 1 means perfect equality.
It does not show the standard of living.
A higher value means more equal.
Each value matches only one income distribution.
o.zh: 每個數值只對應一種收入分配。

w.en: It measures distribution only.
w.zh: 佢只量度分配。

q.en: Pick the best limitation of the Gini coefficient.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅堅尼系數限制。

o.en: Different Lorenz curves can give the same Gini, and it ignores income levels.
o.zh: 唔同 Lorenz curve 可以有一樣嘅堅尼系數，亦忽略收入水平。

hook.en: Hong Kong, 2016: after taxes and social transfers, the Gini coefficient fell from 0.539 (original income) to 0.473.
hook.zh: 2016 年香港：計埋稅同社會福利轉移後，堅尼系數由 0.539（原本收入）降到 0.473。

stops.src: GovHK press release, 9 Jun 2017 (2016 Population By-census)

q.en: Why is the Gini lower after taxes and transfers?
q.zh: 點解計埋稅同轉移之後堅尼系數較低？

o.en: Higher earners pay more tax and lower earners receive transfers.
o.zh: 高收入人士交多啲稅，低收入人士收到轉移支付。
除稅後大家收入都多咗。

w.en: Taxes and transfers narrow the gap.
w.zh: 稅同轉移支付收窄差距。

d.en: Ways to narrow income gaps: progressive income tax (the higher the income, the higher the average tax rate), cash transfers (e.g. allowances), transfers in kind (e.g. public housing, public healthcare), and a minimum wage. A minimum wage may cause unemployment among low-skilled workers, so its effect on the income gap is uncertain.
d.zh: 拉近收入：progressive income tax（收入越高，average tax rate 越高）、cash transfers（例如津貼）、transfers in kind（例如公屋、公營醫療）同 minimum wage。Minimum wage 可能令低技術工人失業，所以對收入差距嘅效果唔一定。

p.en: Average tax rate = total tax ÷ income.
p.zh: Average tax rate = 總稅款 ÷ 收入。

s.en: 0% on the first $50,000; 10% on the next $100,000; 20% above $150,000.
Income $100,000: tax $5,000 → average rate 5%.

q.en: Public housing is an example of…
q.zh: 公屋係…

w.en: A good or service given instead of cash.
w.zh: 俾嘅係物品或服務，唔係現金。

q.en: Pick the best definition of a progressive income tax.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅累進所得稅定義。

o.en: A tax whose average rate rises as income rises.
o.zh: 收入越高，平均稅率越高嘅稅。

o.en: A tax where richer people pay more dollars.
A proportional tax also does that.
A tax that rises every year.

t.zh: 拉近機會；公平 vs 效率

hook.en: Hong Kong today: public primary and secondary education is free, and the government subsidises university places and public healthcare.
hook.zh: 今日香港：公營中小學教育免費，政府資助大學學額同公營醫療。

q.en: Free education mainly aims to equalise…
q.zh: 免費教育主要想拉近…

w.en: It helps children from poorer families build human capital.
w.zh: 佢幫助基層家庭嘅小朋友建立 human capital。

d.en: Equalising opportunities: subsidised education, subsidised healthcare, anti-discrimination laws, social enterprises and job training. Pursuing equity may sacrifice efficiency: high tax rates and welfare may reduce the incentive to work and invest (disincentive effect); in-kind subsidies can make MB ≠ MC; and there are administrative costs.
d.zh: 拉近機會：資助教育、資助醫療、反歧視法例、社會企業同職業培訓。追求 equity 可能犧牲 efficiency：高稅率同福利可能減低工作同投資意欲（disincentive effect）、實物資助令 MB ≠ MC，仲有行政成本。

p.en: Equity: fairness. Efficiency: making TSS as large as possible.
p.zh: Equity：公平。Efficiency：令 TSS 最大。

s.en: Subsidised job training → more workers gain skills → opportunities more equal.
s.zh: 資助職業培訓 → 更多工人學到技能 → 機會更平均。

s.en: Very high income tax → some people work less → output may fall (disincentive).
s.zh: 好高嘅所得稅 → 有人少做啲 → 產出可能減少（disincentive）。

s.en: Running schemes needs staff and checks → administrative cost.
s.zh: 推行計劃要人手同審查 → 行政成本。

q.en: Which is a disincentive effect?
q.zh: 以下邊樣係 disincentive effect？

o.en: High tax rates reduce people’s willingness to work more.
o.zh: 高稅率令人唔想做多啲。

o.en: A minimum wage raises some workers’ pay.
o.zh: 最低工資令部分工人加人工。

w.en: Lower reward for extra work → less work.
w.zh: 多做嘅回報低咗 → 做少咗。

q.en: Pick the best statement about equity and efficiency.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅公平同效率說法。

o.en: Policies that improve equity may reduce efficiency, so societies face a trade-off.
o.zh: 改善公平嘅政策可能降低效率，所以社會要取捨。

o.en: An efficient outcome is always fair.
o.zh: 有效率嘅結果一定公平。

o.en: Equity and efficiency always move together.

chain.zh: 取捨：公平 vs 效率

q.en: A Gini coefficient of 0 means…
q.zh: 堅尼系數 0 代表…

w.en: Lorenz curve = diagonal.
w.zh: Lorenz curve = 對角線。

q.en: A Comprehensive Social Security Assistance payment is…
q.zh: 綜援金係…

w.en: Cash given to households.
w.zh: 俾住戶嘅現金。

q.en: Hong Kong’s 2016 Gini (original income) was…
q.zh: 2016 年香港堅尼系數（原本收入）係…

w.en: 0.473 is after taxes and transfers.
w.zh: 0.473 係計埋稅同轉移之後。

q.en: In your own words: why might making incomes more equal reduce efficiency?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解令收入更平均可能降低效率？

ck.en: I mentioned the disincentive effect of high taxes or welfare.
ck.zh: 我有提到高稅或福利嘅 disincentive effect。

ck.en: I mentioned MB ≠ MC under in-kind subsidies, or administrative cost.
ck.zh: 我有提到實物資助令 MB ≠ MC，或者行政成本。

ck.en: I said this is a trade-off, not a rule against equity.
ck.zh: 我有講呢個係取捨，唔係反對公平。

hook.en: Central, 2016: a foreign-owned bank in Central and a local tea restaurant on Graham Street both produce services in Hong Kong.
hook.zh: 2016 年中環：一間外資銀行同嘉咸街一間本地茶餐廳，都喺香港生產服務。

q.en: Is the foreign-owned bank’s output in Central part of Hong Kong’s GDP?
q.zh: 外資銀行喺中環嘅產出算唔算香港 GDP？

o.en: Yes, it is produced by a resident unit in Hong Kong.
o.zh: 算，係香港居民生產單位喺本地生產。

w.en: GDP looks at where it is produced and by resident units, not the owner’s nationality.
w.zh: GDP 睇喺邊度生產、由居民單位生產，唔睇老闆國籍。

d.en: GDP: the market value of all final goods and services produced by all resident producing units of an economy over a period of time. GDP is a flow, not a stock. Paid domestic helpers’ services count in GDP; unpaid housework does not.
d.zh: GDP：一段時間內，經濟體系內所有 resident producing units 生產嘅所有最終物品同服務嘅市場價值。GDP 係 flow，唔係 stock；睇生產喺邊度、由邊個 resident 生產，唔睇老闆國籍。有薪家務助理嘅服務計入 GDP，自己做家務就唔計。

p.en: Final goods only: intermediate goods are already inside final goods’ value.
p.zh: 只計最終物品：中間產品嘅價值已經包含喺最終物品入面。

s.en: A Graham Street café’s milk tea sold this year → in.
s.zh: 嘉咸街茶餐廳今年賣出嘅奶茶 → 計。

s.en: A paid domestic helper’s cleaning → in; a parent’s own housework → out.
s.zh: 有薪家務助理嘅清潔 → 計；父母自己做家務 → 唔計。

s.en: The value of all flats standing in Central (a stock) → out.
s.zh: 中環所有現存樓宇嘅價值（存量）→ 唔計。

q.en: Which is counted in Hong Kong’s GDP?
q.zh: 以下邊樣計入香港 GDP？

o.en: A mother cooking for her own family
o.zh: 媽媽為自己屋企人煮飯

o.en: Flour bought by a bakery to make bread
o.zh: 餅店買嚟整麵包嘅麵粉

o.en: The value of all shares held on 31 December
o.zh: 12 月 31 日持有嘅所有股票價值

w.en: A marketed final service by a resident unit.
w.zh: 由居民單位提供、有市場交易嘅最終服務。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why is GDP a flow?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解 GDP 係流量？

o.en: It measures production over a period of time, such as a year.
o.zh: 佢量度一段時間（例如一年）內嘅生產。

o.en: It measures the value of assets at a point in time.
o.zh: 佢量度某一時點嘅資產價值。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Graham Street, 2026: a wholesaler sells tea leaves for $20 to a café, which sells milk tea for a total of $50.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年嘉咸街：批發商以 $20 將茶葉賣俾茶餐廳，茶餐廳賣奶茶合共收 $50。

q.en: How much value does the café add?
q.zh: 茶餐廳增值咗幾多？

w.en: $50 output − $20 intermediate consumption = $30.

d.en: Production approach: value added = value of output − intermediate consumption. GDP is the sum of value added by all resident producing units. Counting only final goods and adding up the value added at every stage give the same figure, which avoids double counting.
d.zh: Production approach：value added = 產出價值 − intermediate consumption。將所有 RPU 嘅 value added 加埋就係 GDP。只計 final goods 同計晒每個階段嘅 value added 會得出同一個數，咁先唔會 double counting。

p.en: Double counting: adding the tea leaves’ $20 again inside the $50 milk tea.
p.zh: 重複計算：將 $50 奶茶入面已有嘅 $20 茶葉再加一次。

s.en: Tea farm sells leaves to the wholesaler for $8 → value added $8.
s.zh: 茶園以 $8 將茶葉賣俾批發商 → 增值 $8。

s.en: Wholesaler sells to the café for $20 → value added $12.
s.zh: 批發商以 $20 賣俾茶餐廳 → 增值 $12。

s.en: Café sells milk tea for $50 → value added $30. Total $8 + $12 + $30 = $50 = the final good’s value.
s.zh: 茶餐廳賣奶茶 $50 → 增值 $30。合共 $8 + $12 + $30 = $50 = 最終產品價值。

q.en: (Fictional figures) A baker buys flour for $40 and sells bread for $100. Her value added is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）麵包師傅用 $40 買麵粉，麵包賣 $100。佢嘅增值係…

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why do we subtract intermediate consumption?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解要減中間消耗？

o.en: To avoid double counting what earlier producers already made.
o.zh: 避免重複計算前面生產者已經生產嘅部分。

hook.en: (Fictional figures) A small economy’s year: households spend $500, firms invest $200, the government buys $150, exports are $400 and imports are $350.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）某細小經濟體系一年內：住戶消費 $500、廠商投資 $200、政府購買 $150、出口 $400、進口 $350。

q.en: What is GDP?
q.zh: GDP 係幾多？

d.en: GDP = C + I + G + (X − M). I = gross domestic fixed capital formation + changes in inventories. G excludes transfer payments. M is subtracted because C, I, G and X already include imported goods. Buying a second-hand flat or shares is not investment in GDP.
d.zh: Expenditure approach：GDP = C + I + G + (X − M)。I = gross domestic fixed capital formation + changes in inventories；G 唔包括 transfer payments；減 M 因為 C、I、G、X 已經包咗進口嘢。買二手樓或者股票唔係 GDP 入面嘅 investment。

p.en: Investment in GDP means new capital goods and inventory changes, not buying financial assets.
p.zh: GDP 入面嘅投資係新資本財同存貨變動，唔係買金融資產。

s.en: A café buys a new coffee machine → I.
s.zh: 茶餐廳買新咖啡機 → I。

s.en: The government pays an old-age allowance → transfer, not in G.
s.zh: 政府派長者生活津貼 → 轉移支付，唔計入 G。

s.en: An investor buys shares on the stock exchange → not I.
s.zh: 投資者喺股票市場買股票 → 唔計入 I。

q.en: Which is part of G in the expenditure approach?
q.zh: 以下邊樣屬於開支法嘅 G？

o.en: A firm buying a used flat
Salaries paid to public school teachers

w.en: Government buys teachers’ services; allowances are transfers.
w.zh: 政府購買教師服務；津貼係轉移支付。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why are imports subtracted?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解要減進口？

o.en: C, I, G and X already include spending on imported goods, which were not produced here.
o.zh: C、I、G、X 已經包括買進口貨嘅開支，而嗰啲唔係本地生產。

o.en: Imports are counted twice in X.
o.zh: 進口喺 X 計咗兩次。

o.en: Imports are bad for the economy.
A value judgement, not the reason.

t.en: The income approach, factor cost and market prices
t.zh: 收入法、要素成本同市價

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Central, 2026: a small firm pays $300 in wages; its rent, interest, profit and depreciation total $150; it pays $20 indirect tax and receives no subsidy.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年中環：一間細公司付工資 $300；租金、利息、利潤同折舊合共 $150；佢交 $20 間接稅，冇收補貼。

q.en: What is its contribution to GDP at factor cost?
q.zh: 佢對按要素成本計算嘅 GDP 貢獻係幾多？

w.en: Compensation of employees $300 + gross operating surplus $150.
w.zh: 僱員報酬 $300 + 總營運盈餘 $150。

d.en: Income approach: GDP at factor cost = compensation of employees + gross operating surplus (rent, interest, profit, depreciation). GDP at market prices = GDP at factor cost + indirect taxes − subsidies.
d.zh: Income approach：GDP at factor cost = 僱員報酬 + gross operating surplus（租金、利息、利潤、折舊）。GDP at market prices = GDP at factor cost + indirect taxes − subsidies。

p.en: Indirect taxes raise market prices above factor cost; subsidies lower them.
p.zh: 間接稅令市價高過要素成本；補貼令市價低過要素成本。

t.en: From factor cost to market prices (fictional figures)
t.zh: 由要素成本到市價（虛構數字）

s.en: Add indirect tax $20, subtract subsidies $0.
s.zh: 加間接稅 $20，減補貼 $0。

s.en: GDP at market prices = $470.
s.zh: 按市價 GDP = $470。

q.en: GDP at market prices = GDP at factor cost +…
q.zh: 按市價 GDP = 按要素成本 GDP +…

w.en: Market prices include indirect taxes and are reduced by subsidies.
w.zh: 市價包括間接稅，減去補貼。

q.en: Pick the best description of gross operating surplus.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 gross operating surplus 描述。

o.en: Rent, interest, profit and depreciation earned in production.
o.zh: 生產中賺到嘅租金、利息、利潤同折舊。
非工資要素收入加折舊。

t.zh: GNI 同 GDP 唔計嘅嘢

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Central Pier, 2026: Hong Kong residents earn $80 in factor income from abroad, and non-residents earn $50 in factor income in Hong Kong. GDP is $1,000.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）2026 年中環碼頭：香港居民喺外地賺 $80 要素收入，非居民喺香港賺 $50 要素收入。GDP 係 $1,000。

q.en: What is GNI?
q.zh: GNI 係幾多？

d.en: GNI = GDP + net external factor income (factor income earned abroad by residents − factor income earned locally by non-residents). Transfer payments, second-hand goods (only the agent’s commission counts), rises in property and share prices, and pure financial transactions are not counted in GDP.
d.zh: GNI = GDP + net external factor income（居民喺外地賺嘅要素收入 − 非居民喺本地賺嘅要素收入）。Transfer payments、二手貨（只計經紀佣金）、樓價同股價升值、純金融交易都唔計入 GDP。

p.en: GDP: produced inside. GNI: earned by residents.
p.zh: GDP：本地生產。GNI：居民賺取。

s.en: A second-hand flat sold for $8 million → only the agent’s commission counts.
s.zh: 二手樓以 $800 萬成交 → 只計經紀佣金。

s.en: Shares rise in value → not production, not counted.
s.zh: 股價上升 → 唔係生產，唔計。

s.en: An old-age allowance → a transfer, not counted.
s.zh: 長者生活津貼 → 轉移支付，唔計。

q.en: Which is counted in GDP?
q.zh: 以下邊樣計入 GDP？

o.en: The price of the second-hand flat
An estate agent’s commission on a second-hand flat
o.zh: 二手樓買賣嘅經紀佣金

w.en: The commission pays for a service produced this year.
w.zh: 佣金係為今年生產嘅服務而付。

q.en: Pick the best explanation of the difference between GDP and GNI.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅 GDP 同 GNI 分別解釋。

o.en: GDP counts production within the economy; GNI counts income earned by its residents, wherever they earn it.
o.zh: GDP 計本地生產；GNI 計居民賺取嘅收入，唔理喺邊度賺。

o.en: Only if net external factor income is zero.
o.zh: 只有外地要素收入淨額係零先相等。

chain.en: GDP: final output of residents in a period
chain.zh: GDP：居民一段時間內嘅最終產出

chain.en: Production approach: sum of value added
Expenditure approach: C + I + G + (X − M)
Income approach: factor cost → market prices
chain.zh: 收入法：要素成本 → 市價

chain.en: GNI = GDP + net external factor income
chain.zh: GNI = GDP + 外地要素收入淨額

q.en: Which is NOT counted in GDP?
q.zh: 以下邊樣唔計入 GDP？

w.en: Not marketed.
w.zh: 冇市場交易。

q.en: Net external factor income is negative. Then…
q.zh: 外地要素收入淨額係負數。咁…

w.en: GNI = GDP + a negative number.
w.zh: GNI = GDP + 負數。

q.en: In your own words: why do the three approaches give the same GDP?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解三種方法計出嘅 GDP 一樣？

ck.en: I said the value of output equals what is spent on it.
ck.zh: 我有講產出價值等於用喺佢身上嘅開支。

ck.en: I said that spending becomes income to factors.
ck.zh: 我有講呢啲開支變成生產要素嘅收入。

ck.en: I mentioned the circular flow or avoiding double counting.
ck.zh: 我有提到循環流程或避免重複計算。

t.zh: 名義 GDP 同實質 GDP

hook.en: (Fictional figures) A small economy’s nominal GDP rises from $1,000 to $1,100 in a year, while prices rise 10%.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）某細小經濟體系嘅名義 GDP 一年內由 $1,000 升到 $1,100，同期物價升 10%。

q.en: Did the economy produce more goods and services?
q.zh: 經濟體系有冇生產多咗物品同服務？

o.en: No, the rise is all price.

w.en: Real GDP = 1,100 ÷ 110 × 100 = 1,000: unchanged.

d.en: Nominal GDP uses current prices; real GDP uses base-year prices, removing the effect of price changes. Real GDP = nominal GDP ÷ GDP deflator × 100. A rise in nominal GDP may come only from higher prices, without more output.
d.zh: Nominal GDP 用當期價格計；real GDP 用基期價格計，剔走價格變動嘅影響。Real GDP = nominal GDP ÷ GDP deflator × 100。Nominal GDP 上升，可能只係物價升，產量未必多咗。

p.en: To compare output across years, use real GDP.
p.zh: 比較唔同年份嘅產量，要用實質 GDP。

t.zh: 分開價格同數量（虛構數字）

s.en: Year 1: nominal $1,000, deflator 100 → real $1,000.
s.zh: 第 1 年：名義 $1,000，deflator 100 → 實質 $1,000。

s.en: Year 2: nominal $1,100, deflator 110 → real $1,000.
s.zh: 第 2 年：名義 $1,100，deflator 110 → 實質 $1,000。

s.en: Output did not grow; only prices did.
s.zh: 產量冇增長，只係物價升咗。

q.en: (Fictional figures) Nominal GDP is $1,200 and the GDP deflator is 120. Real GDP is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）名義 GDP $1,200，GDP deflator 120。實質 GDP 係…

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why use real GDP to compare output over time?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解比較唔同時間嘅產量要用實質 GDP？

o.en: It removes the effect of price changes, so changes reflect output.
o.zh: 佢剔走價格變動，變化反映產量。

o.en: It is always larger than nominal GDP.

t.en: Per capita GDP and growth rates
t.zh: 人均 GDP 同增長率

hook.en: (Fictional figures) Economy A’s real GDP is $1,000 with 10 people; Economy B’s is $1,500 with 30 people.
hook.zh: （虛構數字）A 經濟體系實質 GDP $1,000，人口 10 人；B 經濟體系 $1,500，人口 30 人。

q.en: Which has the higher real per capita GDP?
q.zh: 邊個嘅實質人均 GDP 較高？

o.en: B, because its GDP is larger

w.en: Per capita = GDP ÷ population.
w.zh: 人均 = GDP ÷ 人口。

d.en: Per capita GDP = GDP ÷ population. Growth rate = (this year − last year) ÷ last year × 100%. To compare economies with different populations, use per capita figures; to see changes in living standards, use real per capita GDP.
d.zh: Per capita GDP = GDP ÷ 人口。Growth rate =（今年 − 去年）÷ 去年 × 100%。比較唔同人口嘅經濟體系要用 per capita，睇生活水平變化要用 real per capita GDP。

p.en: Real GDP can rise while real per capita GDP falls, if population grows faster.
p.zh: 如果人口增長更快，實質 GDP 上升但實質人均 GDP 可以下跌。

s.en: Population: 10 → 11.
Real per capita GDP: $100 → about $95.5: it fell.
s.zh: 實質人均 GDP：$100 → 約 $95.5：下跌咗。

q.en: (Fictional figures) Real GDP rises from $800 to $880. The growth rate is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）實質 GDP 由 $800 升到 $880。增長率係…

q.en: Pick the best measure of changes in average living standards over time.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅量度平均生活水平變化嘅指標。

o.en: Removes price changes and population size.

t.en: Limits of GDP as a measure of living standards
t.zh: GDP 量度生活水平嘅限制

hook.en: Hong Kong Park, Central, on a Sunday: people enjoy free time with family. None of that leisure shows up in GDP.
hook.zh: 星期日中環香港公園：大家同家人享受閒暇。呢啲閒暇完全唔會反映喺 GDP。

q.en: If everyone worked on Sundays instead, GDP might rise. Would living standards surely rise?
q.zh: 如果大家星期日都返工，GDP 可能上升。生活水平係咪一定提高？

o.en: Yes, more GDP always means better lives.
o.zh: 一定，GDP 多就一定生活好。

w.en: GDP ignores leisure.
w.zh: GDP 冇計閒暇。

d.en: Limits of using GDP to compare living standards: price levels, population, output mix (weapons or consumer goods), unrecorded production (housework, volunteering, the underground economy), leisure, pollution, income distribution, quality; across places, exchange rates and purchasing power also matter.
d.zh: 用 GDP 比較生活水平嘅限制：物價水平、人口、產出組合（軍火定消費品）、冇記錄嘅生產（家務、義工、地下經濟）、閒暇、污染、收入分配、質素，跨地區比較仲要考慮匯率同購買力。

p.en: Use real per capita GDP, and still check these limits.
p.zh: 用實質人均 GDP，再考慮呢啲限制。

t.zh: GDP 一樣，生活唔同（虛構）

s.en: Economy X spends much on weapons; Y on schools and hospitals → Y’s people may live better.
s.zh: X 用好多錢喺軍火；Y 用喺學校同醫院 → Y 嘅人可能生活較好。

s.en: X has heavy pollution; Y has clean air → GDP misses this.
s.zh: X 污染嚴重；Y 空氣清新 → GDP 冇反映。

s.en: X’s income goes mostly to a few people → average hides inequality.
s.zh: X 嘅收入大部分落入少數人手 → 平均數掩蓋不平均。

q.en: Which is NOT a limitation of GDP as a measure of living standards?
q.zh: 以下邊樣唔係用 GDP 量度生活水平嘅限制？

w.en: Counting final goods avoids double counting; it is a rule, not a limit on welfare.
w.zh: 只計最終物品係避免重複計算嘅規則，唔係福利限制。

q.en: Pick the best explanation: why can two economies with the same real per capita GDP have different living standards?
q.zh: 揀最好嘅解釋：點解實質人均 GDP 一樣，生活水平都可以唔同？

o.en: Because per capita figures are always wrong.
Leisure, pollution, output mix and income distribution can differ.
o.zh: 閒暇、污染、產出組合同收入分配可以唔同。

t.zh: 物價指數同消費物價指數

hook.en: Graham Street Market, Central: the price of a basket of household goods changes every month. Hong Kong compiles CPI(A), CPI(B), CPI(C) and the Composite CPI.
hook.zh: 中環嘉咸街街市：一籃子家庭用品嘅價格每個月都變。香港編製 CPI(A)、CPI(B)、CPI(C) 同綜合 CPI。

q.en: (Fictional figures) A basket costs $200 in the base year and $230 now. The price index is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）一籃子貨品基期 $200，而家 $230。物價指數係…

d.en: Price index = current-period price ÷ base-period price × 100; the base period = 100. The CPI measures changes in the prices of a basket of consumer goods and services bought by households; its weights come from the Household Expenditure Survey. Inflation rate = (this period’s CPI − last period’s CPI) ÷ last period’s CPI × 100%.
d.zh: Price index = 當期價格 ÷ 基期價格 × 100，基期 = 100。CPI 量度住戶一籃子消費品同服務嘅價格變動，權數嚟自住戶開支統計調查。Inflation rate =（今期 CPI − 上期 CPI）÷ 上期 CPI × 100%。

p.en: Weights: items households spend more on count more.
p.zh: 權數：住戶花費較多嘅項目比重較大。

s.en: CPI last year: 104; this year: 107.
s.zh: 去年 CPI：104；今年：107。

s.en: Not 3%: divide by last year’s CPI, not 100.
s.zh: 唔係 3%：要除去年 CPI，唔係除 100。

q.en: (Fictional figures) CPI rises from 120 to 126. The inflation rate is…
q.zh: （虛構數字）CPI 由 120 升到 126。通脹率係…

q.en: Pick the most common mistake in calculating the inflation rate from CPI.
q.zh: 揀用 CPI 計通脹率最常見嘅錯誤。

o.en: Subtracting last period’s CPI from this period’s.
o.zh: 用今期 CPI 減上期 CPI。

o.en: Dividing the change by 100 instead of by last period’s CPI.
o.zh: 將變動除 100，而唔係除上期 CPI。

t.zh: GDP 平減物價指數 vs CPI

hook.en: Central Pier, today: ferries bring in imported food for households, while Hong Kong firms export services such as finance and logistics.
hook.zh: 今日中環碼頭：渡輪運入住戶食用嘅進口食品，同時香港公司出口金融同物流等服務。

q.en: The price of imported rice rises. Which index includes it directly?
q.zh: 進口米加價。邊個指數直接包括佢？

w.en: The CPI includes imported consumer goods; the GDP deflator covers only domestic output.
w.zh: CPI 包括進口消費品；GDP deflator 只包括本地產出。

d.en: GDP deflator = nominal GDP ÷ real GDP × 100. It covers all goods and services produced locally (including capital goods and exports, excluding imports), and its basket changes with output. The CPI uses a fixed basket of household consumer goods and services only, including imported consumer goods.
d.zh: GDP deflator = nominal GDP ÷ real GDP × 100，包括本地生產嘅所有物品同服務（包括資本財同出口，唔包括進口），籃子隨產出變動。CPI 用固定籃子，只包括住戶消費品（包括進口消費品）。

p.en: Different coverage → the two can give different inflation figures.
p.zh: 涵蓋範圍唔同 → 兩者計出嘅通脹可以唔同。

s.en: Imported rice price ↑ → CPI ↑; GDP deflator not directly.
s.zh: 進口米加價 → CPI ↑；GDP deflator 唔直接受影響。

s.en: Price of new office machinery made locally ↑ → GDP deflator ↑; CPI not.
s.zh: 本地製造嘅新辦公室機器加價 → GDP deflator ↑；CPI 唔會。

s.en: Price of exported financial services ↑ → GDP deflator ↑; CPI not.
s.zh: 出口金融服務加價 → GDP deflator ↑；CPI 唔會。

q.en: Which price change affects the GDP deflator but NOT the CPI?
q.zh: 以下邊個價格變動影響 GDP deflator 但唔影響 CPI？

o.en: A rise in rents paid by households
A rise in the price of imported fruit
A rise in bus fares paid by households
o.zh: 住戶付嘅巴士車費上升

o.en: A rise in the price of locally made machinery bought by firms
o.zh: 廠商購買嘅本地製造機器加價

w.en: A capital good produced locally is in GDP but not in the household basket.
w.zh: 本地生產嘅資本財喺 GDP 入面，但唔喺住戶籃子入面。

q.en: Pick the best one-line difference.
q.zh: 揀最好嘅一句講出分別。

o.en: Exports are in the deflator, not the CPI.
They measure exactly the same prices.
o.zh: 兩者量度完全一樣嘅價格。

o.en: The GDP deflator covers all local output; the CPI covers a fixed basket of household consumption, including imports.
o.zh: GDP deflator 涵蓋所有本地產出；CPI 涵蓋住戶消費嘅固定籃子，包括進口。

chain.en: Nominal GDP mixes price and output
chain.zh: 名義 GDP 混合咗價格同產量
實質 GDP = 名義 ÷ deflator × 100

chain.en: Real per capita GDP for living standards
chain.zh: 用實質人均 GDP 睇生活水平
GDP 忽略閒暇、污染、分配

chain.en: Price indices: CPI and GDP deflator
chain.zh: 物價指數：CPI 同 GDP deflator

q.en: Nominal GDP $2,200, deflator 110. Real GDP is…
q.zh: 名義 GDP $2,200，deflator 110。實質 GDP 係…

q.en: CPI rises from 100 to 103. The inflation rate is…
q.zh: CPI 由 100 升到 103。通脹率係…

q.en: To compare living standards of two economies, it is best to use…
q.zh: 比較兩個經濟體系嘅生活水平，最好用…

o.en: real per capita GDP, with its limits in mind
o.zh: 實質人均 GDP，並考慮其限制

w.en: Adjust for prices and population.
w.zh: 調整物價同人口。

q.en: In your own words: why might real per capita GDP rise while people feel worse off?
q.zh: 用自己嘅說話講：點解實質人均 GDP 上升，但大家可能覺得生活差咗？

ck.en: I mentioned leisure or working hours.
ck.zh: 我有提到閒暇或工時。

ck.en: I mentioned pollution or quality of life.
ck.zh: 我有提到污染或生活質素。

ck.en: I mentioned income distribution.
ck.zh: 我有提到收入分配。
